instructions: Place dry couscous in a large heatproof bowl and drizzle with 2 tbsp olive oil, rubbing between fingers to coat grains â€” this prevents clumping | Pour boiling water or broth over couscous, season with a pinch of salt, and cover tightly with a plate or plastic wrap | Let sit undisturbed for exactly 5 minutes | Remove cover and fluff couscous thoroughly with a fork, breaking up any clumps until light and airy | Spread fluffed couscous on a tray to cool to room temperature â€” this prevents it from cooking further and becoming mushy | While couscous cools, prepare the vegetables: dice cucumber, tomatoes, and bell pepper into uniform small cubes, and finely dice red onion | Transfer cooled couscous to a large serving bowl | Add all diced vegetables, chopped parsley, and mint | In a small bowl, whisk together lemon juice, extra virgin olive oil, salt, and pepper | Pour dressing over the salad and toss gently but thoroughly with forks to combine | Taste and adjust seasoning â€” it should be bright and fresh | Sprinkle crumbled feta on top if using | Refrigerate for at least 20 minutes before serving to let flavors meld | Serve chilled or at room temperature as a side dish or light lunch

ingredients: 1 box (500g) lasagna sheets (oven-ready or boiled), 500g ground beef, 1 onion (diced), 4 cloves garlic (minced), 2 cans (400g each) crushed tomatoes, 2 tbsp tomato paste, 1 tsp dried oregano, 1 tsp dried basil, salt and pepper, 3 tbsp butter, 3 tbsp all-purpose flour, 3 cups whole milk, 1/4 tsp nutmeg, 500g ricotta cheese, 1 large egg, 1/2 cup Parmesan cheese (grated), 400g mozzarella cheese (shredded), fresh basil for garnish
instructions: Make meat sauce: brown ground beef in a large pot over medium-high heat, breaking it apart, for 8 minutes | Add diced onion and cook for 5 minutes | Add minced garlic, oregano, and basil, cooking for 1 minute | Stir in tomato paste, then pour in crushed tomatoes | Season with salt and pepper, bring to a simmer, reduce heat to low, and cook for 30 minutes, stirring occasionally | Make bÃ©chamel sauce: melt butter in a saucepan, whisk in flour, and cook for 1 minute | Gradually pour in milk while whisking constantly | Cook for 5-7 minutes, whisking often, until thick enough to coat the back of a spoon | Season with nutmeg and salt | In a bowl, mix ricotta cheese with egg and half the Parmesan | Preheat oven to 375Â°F (190Â°C) | To assemble: spread a thin layer of meat sauce on the bottom of a 9x13-inch baking dish | Lay lasagna sheets in a single layer (break to fit if needed) | Spread 1/3 of ricotta mixture, then 1/3 of meat sauce, then 1/4 of bÃ©chamel, then a sprinkle of mozzarella | Repeat layers two more times (pasta, ricotta, meat sauce, bÃ©chamel, mozzarella) | Top final layer with remaining bÃ©chamel, mozzarella, and Parmesan | Cover with foil (tent foil so it doesn't touch cheese) and bake for 25 minutes | Remove foil and bake another 20-25 minutes until bubbly and golden brown on top | Let lasagna rest for 15 minutes before slicing â€” this is crucial for clean slices | Garnish with fresh basil and serve

ingredients: 500g potato gnocchi (fresh or shelf-stable), 3 cups fresh basil leaves (packed), 1/3 cup pine nuts (toasted), 3 cloves garlic, 1/2 cup extra virgin olive oil, 1/2 cup Parmesan cheese (freshly grated), 1/4 cup Pecorino cheese (grated), salt, reserved pasta water, extra Parmesan for serving
instructions: Toast pine nuts in a dry pan over medium heat for 2-3 minutes, shaking frequently, until golden and fragrant | Make pesto: combine basil, toasted pine nuts, garlic, and a pinch of salt in a food processor | Pulse until roughly chopped, then with the motor running, slowly stream in olive oil until smooth | Transfer to a bowl and stir in grated Parmesan and Pecorino by hand â€” do not blend the cheese | Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil | Cook gnocchi according to package directions â€” they are done about 1 minute after they float to the surface | Scoop gnocchi out with a slotted spoon rather than draining through a colander (they are delicate) | Reserve 1/2 cup pasta water | Return hot gnocchi to the empty pot off the heat | Add pesto and a splash of reserved pasta water | Toss gently with a rubber spatula â€” gnocchi are fragile so be careful not to break them | Add more pasta water a little at a time until pesto becomes creamy and coats each gnocco | Serve immediately in warm bowls with a generous snowfall of extra Parmesan on top | Do not reheat as the basil will oxidize and turn dark

ingredients: 800g beef chuck (cut into 2-inch chunks), 2 cans (400ml each) coconut milk, 4 stalks lemongrass (bruised), 6 kaffir lime leaves, 2 turmeric leaves (optional), 2 tbsp tamarind paste, 1 tbsp sugar, salt to taste, 3 tbsp vegetable oil. Spice paste: 10 dried red chilies (soaked), 6 shallots, 5 cloves garlic, 2-inch galangal, 2-inch ginger, 1 tbsp ground coriander, 1 tsp cumin, 1/2 tsp fennel
instructions: Make spice paste: blend soaked dried chilies, shallots, garlic, galangal, ginger, coriander, cumin, and fennel in a food processor with a splash of water until a smooth paste forms | Heat vegetable oil in a large heavy pot or Dutch oven over medium heat | Fry the spice paste for 8-10 minutes, stirring constantly, until it darkens and the oil separates â€” this step is crucial for deep flavor | Add beef chunks and stir to coat with the paste, browning slightly for 5 minutes | Pour in coconut milk, add bruised lemongrass stalks, kaffir lime leaves, and turmeric leaves | Bring to a gentle simmer, then reduce heat to low | Cook uncovered for 2 1/2 to 3 hours, stirring every 20 minutes to prevent sticking, especially towards the end | At first the mixture will look soupy, but it will slowly reduce â€” patience is key | After about 2 hours, the sauce will thicken and darken in color | Add tamarind paste and sugar, continuing to cook and stir | In the final 30 minutes, stir more frequently as the sauce reduces to a thick paste that clings to the beef | The rendang is done when the beef is fork-tender and the sauce is very thick, dark brown, and almost dry â€” it should coat the beef rather than pool as a liquid | Remove lemongrass and lime leaves | Serve with steamed jasmine rice or coconut rice and a side of cucumber salad

ingredients: 1 1/2 cups all-purpose flour, 1 cup dashi or water, 2 large eggs, 3 cups green cabbage (finely shredded), 3 green onions (thinly sliced), 8 slices thinly sliced pork belly, 2 tbsp vegetable oil, okonomiyaki sauce, Japanese mayonnaise (Kewpie), bonito flakes (katsuobushi), aonori (seaweed flakes), pickled red ginger (beni shoga)
instructions: Finely shred cabbage — the pieces should be thin and uniform for even cooking | In a large bowl, whisk together flour and dashi/water until smooth | Beat in eggs one at a time | Add shredded cabbage and sliced green onions to the batter, folding until cabbage is well coated — the batter is mostly cabbage held together | Heat 1 tbsp vegetable oil in a large non-stick skillet over medium heat | Pour half the cabbage batter into the pan and shape into a round pancake about 1-inch thick — do not press down | Lay 4 slices of pork belly across the top of the pancake | Cook for 4-5 minutes until the bottom is golden brown and set | Carefully flip the okonomiyaki using two spatulas so the pork side is now down | Cook for another 5 minutes until pork is crispy and the pancake is cooked through | Flip once more (pork side up) and slide onto a plate | Drizzle generously with okonomiyaki sauce in a zigzag pattern | Squeeze Japanese mayonnaise in parallel lines, then drag a toothpick or skewer through to create a decorative pattern | Sprinkle with bonito flakes, aonori seaweed, and pickled red ginger | Repeat with remaining batter | Serve immediately while the bonito flakes dance from the heat

ingredients: 1 package (450g) phyllo dough (thawed), 3 cups mixed nuts (walnuts, pistachios, or almonds, finely chopped), 1 cup unsalted butter (melted), 1 tsp ground cinnamon, 1/4 tsp ground cloves, 1 cup granulated sugar, 3/4 cup water, 1/2 cup honey, 1 tsp vanilla extract, 1 strip lemon peel, 1 cinnamon stick
instructions: Thaw phyllo dough overnight in the refrigerator, then let it come to room temperature for 1 hour before using — do not unwrap until ready | Preheat oven to 350°F (175°C) | In a bowl, combine finely chopped mixed nuts with ground cinnamon and ground cloves | Unwrap phyllo and lay the sheets flat, covering with a damp kitchen towel to prevent them from drying out while you work | Melt butter completely | Brush the bottom of a 9x13-inch baking dish generously with melted butter | Place one sheet of phyllo in the dish and brush with butter | Repeat, layering and buttering each sheet, until you have 8-10 buttered sheets as the bottom layer | Sprinkle a thin even layer of the nut mixture over the phyllo | Add 2 more buttered phyllo sheets, then another layer of nuts | Repeat this pattern (2 sheets, nuts, 2 sheets, nuts) until all nuts are used, ending with the remaining 8-10 sheets of phyllo on top — each one buttered individually | Use a very sharp knife to cut the baklava into diamond shapes: make diagonal cuts about 1 1/2 inches apart in one direction, then diagonal cuts in the opposite direction | Cut all the way through to the bottom layer | Bake for 45-50 minutes until the top is deep golden brown and crispy | While baklava bakes, make the syrup: combine sugar, water, honey, vanilla, lemon peel, and cinnamon stick in a saucepan | Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer for 10 minutes until slightly thickened | Remove lemon peel and cinnamon stick | When baklava comes out of the oven, immediately pour the hot syrup evenly over the entire surface — you should hear it sizzle | Let baklava cool completely at room temperature, uncovered, for at least 4-6 hours or overnight — this allows the syrup to fully absorb and the layers to set | Once cooled, re-cut along the same lines and serve at room temperature

ingredients: 2 tbsp butter, 1 medium onion (diced), 4 cloves garlic (minced), 1 kg ripe tomatoes (roughly chopped, or 2 cans/800g whole peeled tomatoes), 2 cups vegetable or chicken broth, 1/2 cup heavy cream, 1/4 cup fresh basil leaves (plus more for garnish), 1 tbsp sugar (to balance acidity), salt and black pepper to taste, 1/4 tsp red pepper flakes (optional), grilled cheese sandwiches for serving
instructions: Melt butter in a large pot over medium heat | Add diced onion and sautÃ© for 6-7 minutes until soft and translucent | Add minced garlic and red pepper flakes if using, cooking for 1 minute until fragrant | If using fresh tomatoes: add chopped tomatoes and cook for 10 minutes, stirring occasionally, until they break down and release their juices | If using canned tomatoes: add them with their juices and break them up with a spoon | Pour in broth and bring to a simmer | Reduce heat to low and cook for 20-25 minutes, stirring occasionally, until tomatoes are completely soft and flavors meld | Remove from heat and add fresh basil leaves | Using an immersion blender, purÃ©e soup directly in the pot until completely smooth â€” alternatively, carefully blend in batches in a countertop blender | For an ultra-smooth texture, strain soup through a fine mesh sieve back into the pot, pressing with a spatula to extract all liquid | Return soup to low heat and stir in heavy cream | Add sugar, then season with salt and black pepper â€” taste and adjust balance between sweet and acidic | Heat gently for 5 minutes without boiling | Ladle into warm bowls and garnish with a swirl of cream and fresh basil leaves | Serve immediately with a classic grilled cheese sandwich for dipping

ingredients: 1 large head green cabbage, 500g ground beef, 1 cup cooked white rice, 1 medium onion (finely diced), 3 cloves garlic (minced), 1 large egg (lightly beaten), 1 tsp salt, 1/2 tsp black pepper, 1 tsp paprika, 1 tsp dried dill, 1 can (400g) crushed tomatoes, 1 can (400g) tomato sauce, 2 tbsp brown sugar, 1 tbsp lemon juice, 2 tbsp olive oil, sour cream for serving, fresh dill for garnish
instructions: Bring a very large pot of water to a boil | Carefully remove the core from the cabbage with a sharp knife | Place whole cabbage in boiling water and blanch for 3-5 minutes | As outer leaves soften, gently peel them off with tongs one at a time — you need about 12-14 leaves | Set leaves aside to cool, and trim the thick center vein of each leaf flat so they roll easily | In a large bowl, combine ground beef, cooked rice, diced onion, garlic, beaten egg, salt, pepper, paprika, and dill | Mix thoroughly with your hands until well combined | Lay a cabbage leaf flat with the stem end toward you | Place a generous 2-3 tablespoons of meat filling near the base | Fold the sides inward, then roll tightly from the base to the tip like a burrito | Repeat with remaining leaves and filling | In a separate bowl, mix crushed tomatoes, tomato sauce, brown sugar, and lemon juice | Spread a thin layer of tomato mixture on the bottom of a large Dutch oven or deep baking dish | Arrange cabbage rolls seam-side down in snug concentric circles | Pour remaining tomato sauce over the rolls, ensuring they are mostly covered | Drizzle olive oil on top | Cover with a lid or foil and bake at 350°F (175°C) for 1 hour | Remove cover and bake 15 more minutes to thicken the sauce slightly | Serve cabbage rolls hot with a dollop of sour cream and sprinkle of fresh dill

ingredients: 3 cups day-old cooked short-grain rice (cold), 1 cup kimchi (chopped, plus 2 tbsp kimchi liquid), 2 large eggs, 3 tbsp vegetable oil, 1 tbsp sesame oil, 2 tbsp soy sauce, 1 tbsp gochujang (Korean chili paste), 3 cloves garlic (minced), 3 green onions (sliced), 1 tsp sesame seeds, 1 sheet roasted seaweed (gim, crumbled), 2 fried eggs for topping (optional)
instructions: If rice is freshly made, spread it on a tray and refrigerate for 30 minutes — cold day-old rice is essential for good fried rice texture | Chop kimchi into small bite-size pieces and reserve 2 tbsp of its liquid | In a small bowl, mix soy sauce, gochujang, and kimchi liquid to make the sauce | Heat 2 tbsp vegetable oil in a wok or large skillet over high heat until smoking | Add chopped kimchi and stir-fry for 2 minutes until fragrant and slightly caramelized | Add minced garlic and stir-fry for 30 seconds | Add cold rice to the wok, breaking up any clumps with a spatula | Spread rice in an even layer and let it sear undisturbed for 1 minute, then toss | Drizzle sauce mixture over rice and toss continuously for 3-4 minutes until rice is heated through and evenly coated | Drizzle sesame oil around the edges and toss once more | Push rice to one side of the wok, add remaining 1 tbsp vegetable oil to the empty side | Crack 2 eggs into the oil and scramble until just set, then mix into the rice | Add sliced green onions and toss briefly | Transfer to serving bowls and top each with a fried egg (cooked sunny-side up in a separate pan) | Sprinkle with sesame seeds and crumbled roasted seaweed | Serve immediately — mix the runny yolk into the hot rice before eating

ingredients: 3 large eggplants (sliced into 1/2-inch rounds), salt, olive oil for frying, 500g ground lamb or beef, 1 large onion (diced), 4 cloves garlic (minced), 1 can (400g) crushed tomatoes, 1 tbsp tomato paste, 1/2 tsp ground cinnamon, 1/2 tsp ground allspice, 1 tsp dried oregano, 1/4 cup red wine (optional), salt and pepper. For bÃ©chamel: 4 tbsp butter, 4 tbsp flour, 3 cups whole milk, 1/4 tsp nutmeg, 2 egg yolks, 1/2 cup Parmesan or kefalotyri cheese (grated)
instructions: Lay eggplant slices on baking sheets, sprinkle both sides generously with salt, and let sit for 30 minutes â€” salt draws out bitterness and moisture | Pat eggplant dry with paper towels to remove salt and released liquid | Heat olive oil in a large skillet and fry eggplant slices in batches until golden brown on both sides, about 2-3 minutes per side | Drain fried eggplant on paper towels and set aside | In a large pan, brown ground lamb/beef over high heat, breaking it apart, for 8 minutes | Drain excess fat, then add diced onion and cook for 5 minutes until softened | Add minced garlic, cinnamon, allspice, and oregano, cooking for 1 minute | Stir in tomato paste, then pour in crushed tomatoes and red wine | Simmer meat sauce for 20 minutes until thick and rich, then season with salt and pepper | Make bÃ©chamel: melt butter in a saucepan, whisk in flour, and cook for 1 minute | Gradually pour in warm milk while whisking constantly | Cook for 5-7 minutes, whisking often, until thick | Season with nutmeg and salt, then remove from heat | In a small bowl, temper egg yolks by slowly adding a few spoonfuls of hot bÃ©chamel while whisking, then pour yolk mixture back into the bÃ©chamel, whisking vigorously | Stir in grated cheese | Preheat oven to 375Â°F (190Â°C) | Assemble in a 9x13 baking dish: layer half the eggplant on the bottom, spread all meat sauce evenly, top with remaining eggplant, then pour bÃ©chamel over everything â€” spread to edges | Bake for 40-45 minutes until bÃ©chamel is puffed and golden brown on top | Remove from oven and let moussaka rest for at least 20-30 minutes before slicing â€” it needs time to set, otherwise it will collapse | Slice into squares and serve warm

ingredients: 500g large shrimp (peeled and deveined, tails left on), 1/2 cup all-purpose flour, 1 tsp salt, 1/2 tsp garlic powder, 2 large eggs, 1 tbsp water, 2 cups sweetened shredded coconut, 1 cup panko breadcrumbs, vegetable oil for deep frying, 1/2 cup sweet chili sauce for dipping, lime wedges for serving
instructions: Peel shrimp, leaving the tail segment intact — the tail acts as a handle for dipping and eating | Pat shrimp completely dry with paper towels — moisture prevents coating from sticking | Set up breading station with three shallow bowls: Bowl 1: flour mixed with salt and garlic powder. Bowl 2: eggs beaten with 1 tbsp water. Bowl 3: shredded coconut mixed with panko breadcrumbs (panko adds extra crunch) | Holding each shrimp by the tail, dredge in flour, shaking off excess | Dip floured shrimp into egg wash, letting excess drip off | Press shrimp firmly into coconut-panko mixture, coating all sides generously — use your other hand for dry mixtures to avoid clumping | Place coated shrimp on a parchment-lined tray | For extra crispy coating, refrigerate coated shrimp for 20 minutes before frying | Heat vegetable oil in a deep pot or deep fryer to 350°F (175°C) — use enough oil to fully submerge shrimp | Fry shrimp in small batches (4-5 at a time) for 2-3 minutes until coconut is golden brown and shrimp are pink and cooked through | Do not overcrowd — it drops the oil temperature and makes coating greasy | Use a slotted spoon to transfer fried shrimp to a paper towel-lined plate | Season with a pinch of salt immediately while hot | Arrange on a platter with sweet chili sauce in a small bowl and lime wedges | Serve immediately while hot and crispy

ingredients: 400g paneer (cut into 1-inch cubes), 2 tbsp butter, 1 tbsp oil, 1 large onion (finely diced), 1 tbsp ginger-garlic paste, 1 can (400g) crushed tomatoes, 1/4 cup heavy cream, 1 tbsp kasuri methi (dried fenugreek leaves), 1 tsp garam masala, 1/2 tsp turmeric, 1 tsp Kashmiri red chili powder, 1 tsp ground coriander, 1 tsp sugar, salt to taste, fresh cilantro, naan or steamed rice for serving
instructions: Cut paneer into 1-inch cubes and soak in warm water for 10 minutes â€” this keeps it soft and prevents it from drying out during cooking | Heat 1 tbsp butter and oil in a large pan over medium heat | Lightly fry paneer cubes for 1-2 minutes until just golden in spots â€” do not over-fry or they become rubbery | Remove paneer and set aside | In the same pan, add remaining butter and sautÃ© diced onion for 8 minutes until deeply golden brown | Add ginger-garlic paste and cook for 1-2 minutes until raw smell disappears | Add crushed tomatoes, turmeric, chili powder, coriander, and salt | Cook the tomato mixture for 12-15 minutes, stirring occasionally, until it thickens, darkens in color, and the oil starts separating at the edges | Add sugar to balance acidity | Reduce heat to low, pour in heavy cream, and stir until the sauce turns a rich orange color | Add garam masala and crushed kasuri methi by rubbing it between your palms â€” this releases its fragrance | Simmer sauce for 5 minutes | Gently add the fried paneer cubes and stir carefully to coat without breaking them | Simmer for 5-7 minutes, letting the paneer absorb the flavors | Taste and adjust seasoning | Garnish with fresh cilantro and a drizzle of cream | Serve hot with butter naan or steamed basmati rice

ingredients: 400g firm tofu, 1 head broccoli (cut into florets), 1 red bell pepper (sliced), 1 yellow bell pepper (sliced), 3 tbsp soy sauce, 1 tbsp hoisin sauce, 1 tsp cornstarch mixed with 2 tbsp water, 3 cloves garlic (minced), 1 tbsp grated ginger, 2 tbsp vegetable oil, 1 tsp sesame oil, 1 tbsp sesame seeds, 2 green onions (sliced), steamed jasmine rice for serving
instructions: Press tofu: wrap block in paper towels, place between two plates with a weight on top, and press for 20 minutes to remove excess moisture | Cut pressed tofu into 1-inch cubes | Heat 1 tbsp vegetable oil in a wok or large skillet over high heat | Fry tofu cubes for 5-6 minutes, turning occasionally, until golden and crispy on all sides | Remove tofu and set aside on a plate | Add remaining vegetable oil to the wok | Add broccoli florets and stir-fry for 3 minutes â€” they should still be bright green and tender-crisp | Add sliced bell peppers, minced garlic, and grated ginger, tossing for 2 more minutes | In a small bowl, mix soy sauce, hoisin sauce, and cornstarch slurry | Return tofu to the wok | Pour sauce over everything and toss vigorously for 1-2 minutes until sauce thickens and coats all ingredients evenly | Remove from heat and drizzle with sesame oil | Sprinkle with sesame seeds and sliced green onions | Serve immediately over steamed jasmine rice

ingredients: 2 large eggplants (sliced into 1/2-inch rounds), salt, 1 cup all-purpose flour, 3 large eggs (beaten), 2 cups Italian breadcrumbs, 1/2 cup Parmesan cheese (grated), 1 tsp dried oregano, 1 tsp garlic powder, olive oil for frying, 3 cups tomato sauce, 400g fresh mozzarella (sliced), 1/2 cup Parmesan (for layers), fresh basil leaves
instructions: Slice eggplants into 1/2-inch rounds â€” do not peel | Lay slices on baking sheets and sprinkle both sides generously with salt | Let sit for 30-45 minutes â€” salt draws out moisture and bitterness | Pat eggplant slices completely dry with paper towels, removing salt and released liquid | Preheat oven to 375Â°F (190Â°C) | Set up breading station: flour in first bowl, beaten eggs in second bowl (seasoned with a pinch of salt), breadcrumbs mixed with grated Parmesan, oregano, and garlic powder in third bowl | Dredge each eggplant slice in flour, dip in egg, then press into breadcrumb mixture on both sides | Heat a generous layer of olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat | Fry breaded eggplant in batches for 2-3 minutes per side until golden brown and crisp | Drain on paper towels | Spread a thin layer of tomato sauce on the bottom of a 9x13 baking dish | Arrange a single layer of fried eggplant over the sauce | Top each round with a spoon of tomato sauce, a slice of fresh mozzarella, and a sprinkle of Parmesan | If you have more eggplant, create a second layer stacked on top | Pour any remaining tomato sauce around (not completely covering) the eggplant â€” you want edges to stay crispy | Bake for 25-30 minutes until cheese is melted, bubbly, and golden | Let rest for 5-10 minutes before serving | Garnish with fresh torn basil and serve with spaghetti or crusty bread

ingredients: 1 1/2 cups old-fashioned rolled oats, 1 cup all-purpose flour, 1/2 tsp baking soda, 1/2 tsp baking powder, 1/2 tsp salt, 1 tsp ground cinnamon, 1/2 cup unsalted butter (softened), 3/4 cup brown sugar (packed), 1/4 cup granulated sugar, 1 large egg, 1 tsp vanilla extract, 1/2 cup raisins or chocolate chips (optional)
instructions: Preheat oven to 350Â°F (175Â°C) and line two baking sheets with parchment paper | In a medium bowl, whisk together rolled oats, flour, baking soda, baking powder, salt, and cinnamon | In a large bowl, cream softened butter with brown sugar and granulated sugar using an electric mixer for 3-4 minutes until light and fluffy | Beat in egg and vanilla extract until fully incorporated | Gradually add the dry oat mixture to the wet ingredients, mixing on low speed until just combined â€” do not overmix | Fold in raisins or chocolate chips if using | Chill dough in the refrigerator for 20 minutes â€” this prevents cookies from spreading too much | Scoop rounded tablespoons of dough onto prepared baking sheets, spacing them 2 inches apart | Flatten each cookie slightly with the palm of your hand or a fork | Bake for 10-12 minutes until edges are golden brown but centers look slightly underdone â€” they will firm up as they cool | Let cookies cool on the baking sheet for 5 minutes before transferring to a wire rack | Store in an airtight container once fully cooled | Serve with a glass of cold milk

ingredients: 2 tbsp olive oil, 500g ground lamb (or beef for Cottage Pie), 1 large onion (diced), 2 carrots (diced), 2 celery stalks (diced), 3 cloves garlic (minced), 2 tbsp tomato paste, 1 tbsp Worcestershire sauce, 1 cup beef broth, 1 cup frozen peas, 1 tsp fresh thyme (or 1/2 tsp dried), 1 tsp fresh rosemary (chopped), salt and black pepper. For topping: 1 kg potatoes (peeled and cubed), 4 tbsp butter, 1/2 cup warm milk, 1/4 cup sour cream, 1/2 cup cheddar cheese (grated), salt and pepper, fresh parsley
instructions: Preheat oven to 400Â°F (200Â°C) | Boil peeled potatoes in salted water for 15-18 minutes until fork-tender | While potatoes boil, heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat | Brown ground lamb, breaking it apart, for 8 minutes until cooked through â€” drain excess fat | Add diced onion, carrots, and celery to the meat, cooking for 6-7 minutes until vegetables soften | Add minced garlic, tomato paste, Worcestershire sauce, thyme, and rosemary, stirring for 2 minutes | Pour in beef broth and bring to a simmer | Cook for 10 minutes until the broth reduces and thickens slightly | Stir in frozen peas and season with salt and pepper | Drain cooked potatoes and return to the pot over low heat for 1 minute to steam off excess moisture | Mash potatoes thoroughly with butter, warm milk, and sour cream until smooth and creamy | Season mashed potatoes with salt and pepper â€” they should be well seasoned | Transfer meat filling to a 9x13 baking dish or deep pie dish, spreading evenly | Spoon mashed potatoes over the meat filling in dollops, then spread gently with a spatula to cover completely | Use a fork to create ridges on the potato surface â€” these will crisp up beautifully | Sprinkle grated cheddar evenly over the top | Place baking dish on a foil-lined baking sheet to catch any overflow | Bake for 25-30 minutes until the filling is bubbling around the edges and the potato topping is golden brown | For extra browning, broil for the final 2-3 minutes | Let rest for 10 minutes before serving | Garnish with fresh parsley and serve portions with a spoon, scooping down through the potato to the savory filling below

ingredients: 1 kg chicken pieces (bone-in thighs and drumsticks), 3 tbsp vegetable oil, 2 large onions (thinly sliced), 4 cloves garlic (minced), 2 tbsp ginger (grated), 3 tbsp chili paste (or rehydrated dried chilies blended), 2 tbsp tomato paste, 1 can (400g) crushed tomatoes, 1/2 cup coconut milk, 1 tbsp sugar, 1 tsp salt, 1 cinnamon stick, 2 star anise, 3 cloves, 3 cardamom pods, 1/2 cup water, 1 lime (juice), fresh cilantro for garnish, steamed white rice for serving
instructions: Season chicken pieces with salt and set aside | Heat vegetable oil in a large deep pan or wok over medium-high heat | Fry chicken pieces for 4-5 minutes per side until golden brown â€” do this in batches if needed | Remove chicken and set aside, leaving oil in the pan | Add sliced onions to the same oil and sautÃ© over medium heat for 8-10 minutes until soft and caramelized â€” this builds the sweet-savory base | Add minced garlic and grated ginger, cooking for 1-2 minutes until fragrant | Add chili paste and cook for 3 minutes, stirring constantly, until the oil separates and the paste darkens | Stir in tomato paste and crushed tomatoes, mixing well | Add cinnamon stick, star anise, cloves, and cardamom pods | Pour in water and bring to a simmer | Return chicken pieces to the pan, spooning sauce over them | Cover and simmer on low heat for 25-30 minutes until chicken is cooked through and tender | Pour in coconut milk and stir gently | Add sugar, salt, and lime juice â€” taste and adjust the balance of sweet, salty, and tangy | Continue simmering uncovered for another 10 minutes until the sauce reduces and thickens, clinging to the chicken | The finished dish should have a rich red sauce that coats the chicken | Remove whole spices (cinnamon stick, star anise, cardamom pods) before serving | Garnish with fresh cilantro and serve hot over steamed white rice

ingredients: 400g fresh laksa noodles or thick rice vermicelli, 500g large shrimp (peeled and deveined, shells reserved), 200g fish cakes (sliced), 2 cups bean sprouts, 4 hard-boiled eggs (halved), 400ml coconut milk, 4 cups shrimp or chicken broth, 8 dried red chilies (soaked), 4 shallots, 3 cloves garlic, 2 stalks lemongrass (bruised), 1-inch galangal (sliced), 1 tbsp dried shrimp (soaked), 1 tsp belacan (shrimp paste), 1 tbsp turmeric powder, 2 tbsp fish sauce, 1 tbsp sugar, 3 tbsp vegetable oil, fresh cilantro, fresh mint leaves, lime wedges, sambal for serving
instructions: Make shrimp stock: simmer reserved shrimp shells in 4 cups water for 20 minutes, then strain and set aside | Make laksa paste: blend soaked dried chilies, shallots, garlic, soaked dried shrimp, belacan, and turmeric in a food processor until smooth | Heat vegetable oil in a large pot over medium heat and fry the laksa paste for 8-10 minutes, stirring constantly, until the paste darkens and oil separates â€” this releases maximum flavor | Add bruised lemongrass and sliced galangal, cooking for 2 more minutes | Pour in the shrimp stock and bring to a gentle simmer | Add coconut milk, fish sauce, and sugar, stirring to combine | Add sliced fish cakes and simmer for 5 minutes | Add shrimp and cook for 2-3 minutes until they turn pink â€” do not overcook | Meanwhile, blanch laksa noodles in boiling water for 1 minute until just tender, then drain | Blanch bean sprouts briefly for 30 seconds and drain | Divide noodles among large serving bowls | Ladle the hot fragrant broth with shrimp and fish cakes over the noodles | Top each bowl with bean sprouts and hard-boiled egg halves | Garnish with fresh cilantro, mint leaves, and a lime wedge on the side | Serve immediately with extra sambal for those who like it spicier

ingredients: 2 cups jasmine rice, 1 cup coconut milk, 1 1/2 cups water, 1 pandan leaf (knotted), 1/2 tsp salt, 2 slices ginger, 4 large eggs, 1 cucumber (sliced into rounds), 150g dried anchovies (ikan bilis), 150g roasted peanuts, vegetable oil for frying. Sambal: 15 dried red chilies (soaked), 4 shallots, 3 cloves garlic, 1 tbsp belacan (shrimp paste), 2 tbsp tamarind paste, 1 tbsp sugar, 1/2 tsp salt, 1/2 cup water, 1 small red onion (sliced into rings)
instructions: Rinse jasmine rice in cold water 3-4 times until water runs clear, then drain well | Place rice in a rice cooker or pot with coconut milk, water, knotted pandan leaf, salt, and ginger slices | Cook until rice is tender and liquid is fully absorbed â€” the rice should be rich and fragrant | While rice cooks, make sambal: blend soaked dried chilies, shallots, garlic, and belacan with a splash of water into a smooth paste | Heat 2 tbsp oil in a pan and fry the chili paste over medium heat for 10-12 minutes, stirring constantly, until deeply fragrant and oil separates | Add tamarind paste, sugar, and salt | Pour in 1/2 cup water and simmer for 10 minutes until sambal thickens to a jam-like consistency | Add sliced red onion rings and cook for 2 more minutes â€” they should remain slightly crunchy | Heat vegetable oil in a small pan and fry dried anchovies until golden and crispy, about 2 minutes â€” watch carefully as they burn quickly | Remove anchovies and drain on paper towels, then fry peanuts in the same oil for 2 minutes until golden | Boil eggs for 10 minutes, then cool in ice water, peel, and cut in half | Slice cucumber into thin rounds | To serve: place a generous mound of coconut rice in the center of each plate | Arrange sambal, halved eggs, cucumber slices, crispy anchovies, and roasted peanuts around the rice in neat sections â€” this is the classic presentation | Serve immediately with extra sambal on the side | Traditionally eaten for breakfast but delicious at any time of day

ingredients: 2 tbsp olive oil, 2 large flour tortillas (cut into 1/2-inch squares), pinch of salt
instructions: Heat 2 tbsp olive oil in a medium-sized skillet over medium-high heat | Cut tortillas into 1/2-inch squares using a sharp knife or kitchen scissors | Once oil is shimmering, add tortilla squares in a single layer | Fry quickly for 1-2 minutes, tossing frequently, until golden brown and crisp | Remove with a slotted spoon and drain on paper towels | Sprinkle with a pinch of salt while still warm | Let cool completely before using as a crunchy topping on salads | Store any leftovers in an airtight container for up to 2 days

recipe_name: Sweet Blackened Salmon With Sherry Sauce
ingredients: 4 salmon fillets (150g each), 2 tbsp extra virgin olive oil, 1/4 cup dry sherry, 2 tbsp balsamic vinegar, 2 tbsp lemon juice, 2 tbsp light brown sugar, 1 shallot (finely diced), 1/4 cup blackening seasoning, 1 1/2 tbsp light brown sugar (for blackening mix), salt and pepper to taste
instructions: Use a cast iron pan or heavy skillet over medium-high heat and lightly coat the bottom with olive oil | Sprinkle lemon juice over salmon fillets and season with a pinch of salt and pepper on each side | In a bowl, mix blackening seasoning with 1 1/2 tbsp brown sugar to create sweet blackening seasoning | Press the top side of each salmon fillet firmly into the sweet blackening seasoning | Place salmon in the hot pan seasoned-side down and cook for 3-4 minutes until blackened but not burnt | Carefully flip and cook the other side for another 3-4 minutes until salmon is just cooked through | For the sauce: in a non-aluminum saucepan over medium-high heat, combine sherry, balsamic vinegar, diced shallots, and 2 tbsp brown sugar | Bring to a boil and reduce for 3-4 minutes until thickened to a glaze consistency | Remove sauce from heat and stir in a pinch of salt and pepper | Plate salmon and drizzle the sherry glaze on top and in a circular motion around the plate | Serve with truffle mashed potatoes or lemon-zested basmati rice

ingredients: 2 cups all-purpose flour, 2 tsp baking powder, 1/2 tsp salt, 2 tbsp sugar, 3 large eggs (separated), 1 1/2 cups whole milk, 4 tbsp unsalted butter (melted), 1/2 tsp ground cinnamon
instructions: Using a whisk or whisk attachment for a mixer, beat egg whites until they form stiff white peaks, then set aside | Sift together all dry ingredients (flour, baking powder, salt, sugar, cinnamon) in a large bowl | In a separate bowl, beat egg yolks and then add milk and melted butter, mixing well | Using paddle attachment or by hand, gently fold egg whites into the dry ingredients alternating with the yolk and milk mixture | Mix until just combined â€” batter should be slightly lumpy, do not overmix | Preheat waffle iron according to manufacturer's directions and grease lightly | Pour batter onto hot waffle iron and cook until golden brown and crisp | Serve immediately with butter, maple syrup, and fresh berries

ingredients: 200 grams warm water (85-95Â°F), 2 1/4 tsp active dry yeast, 625 grams warm water, 3 tbsp sugar, 2 tsp salt, 3 tbsp non-fat powdered milk, 3 tbsp shortening, 800-900 grams bread flour
instructions: Sprinkle yeast on 200 grams of warm water (about 85 to 95Â°F) and set aside for 5-10 minutes until foamy | In a large mixing bowl, combine 625 grams warm water, sugar, salt, dry milk, shortening, and about 420 grams of the flour (about 1/3 of the total) | Add activated yeast mixture once it has started to foam up | Mix using a digging or canoeing type motion, lifting the dough slightly to stretch the mixture and add air to activate the gluten, for 8 minutes | Start incorporating all but approximately 200 grams of the remaining flour, reserving some to dust the counter for kneading | When most of the flour is incorporated, pour onto a floured surface and knead the dough for about 2 minutes, adding more flour if the dough is still sticky | Place dough on a greased pan and cover with a kitchen towel | Let rise in a warm room for about an hour or until it has at least doubled its original size | Punch down the dough and rest for 15 minutes | Cut dough into three equal parts, stretch each part while tapping it firmly on the counter | Fold the left and right sides in to the center and press firmly starting at the top and working your way down to create a rectangle | Starting at the bottom, roll the dough up to form a log | Place into greased loaf tins and let rise for 45 minutes to an hour or until it just starts to rise above the pan edge | Bake at 350Â°F for 30 to 35 minutes | Turn out onto a wire rack immediately when removed from the oven to prevent sweating | Let cool slightly before slicing

ingredients: 2 cups all-purpose flour, 2 tsp baking powder, 1/2 tsp salt, 1/4 tsp ground mace, 1/2 cup unsalted butter (softened), 1 cup granulated sugar, 1 large egg, 1 cup whole milk. For topping: 1/2 cup granulated sugar, 1 tsp ground cinnamon, 1/2 cup unsalted butter (melted)
instructions: Preheat oven to 350Â°F and grease a mini muffin pan | In a large bowl, combine flour, baking powder, salt, and mace, stirring well, then set aside | In a separate large mixing bowl, cream sugar and softened butter until light and fluffy | Add egg and mix well | Add reserved dry ingredients and milk alternately, mixing until just combined | Spoon mixture into greased mini muffin pan, filling each cup about halfway | Bake for 15 minutes until a toothpick inserted comes out clean | Remove from oven and let cool in pans for about 2 minutes | While muffins are still warm, dip each one in melted butter, then gently roll in cinnamon-sugar mixture until fully coated | For the topping: while muffins are baking, combine sugar and cinnamon in a bowl, stirring until well mixed | In a separate bowl, melt butter for dipping | Serve muffins warm

ingredients: 8 oz cream cheese (softened), 2 jars (about 100g) dried beef (finely chopped, divided), 3 green onions (finely chopped), 1 tsp accent seasoning (MSG), 1 tbsp Worcestershire sauce, 1/2 tsp garlic powder
instructions: Mix cream cheese, green onions, accent seasoning, Worcestershire sauce, garlic powder, and half of the chopped dried beef together in a bowl until well combined | Taste and add more accent seasoning a little at a time if needed | Form mixture into a ball shape using your hands | Roll the ball in the remaining chopped dried beef, pressing gently so it adheres to the outside | Wrap in plastic wrap and refrigerate until firm, about 1 hour | For easier rolling, let the ball firm up in the fridge for 30 minutes first before applying the outer coating of beef | Serve with crackers or vegetable sticks | Works very well with low-fat cream cheese

ingredients: 500g ground beef, 2 large eggs (beaten), 1/2 cup ketchup, 1/2 tsp MSG or accent seasoning, 1/4 cup warm water, 1 can (400g) tomato sauce, 1/2 cup breadcrumbs, 1 small onion (finely diced), salt and pepper to taste
instructions: Preheat oven to 350Â°F | In a large bowl, combine ground beef, beaten eggs, ketchup, MSG, warm water, breadcrumbs, diced onion, salt, and pepper â€” but do not add the tomato sauce yet | Mix thoroughly with your hands until all ingredients are evenly distributed | Shape mixture into a loaf and place in an ungreased baking pan | Pour tomato sauce evenly over the top of the loaf, letting it run down the sides | Bake for 1 hour until internal temperature reaches 160Â°F (71Â°C) | Let rest for 10 minutes before slicing | Serve with mashed potatoes and steamed vegetables

recipe_name: Spicy Asian Chicken and Shrimp Soup
ingredients: 6 cups chicken broth, 3 tbsp soy sauce, 2 tbsp brown sugar, 1/2 tsp red pepper flakes, 2 tbsp lime juice, 1 tbsp fresh ginger (grated), 2 boneless skinless chicken breasts (thinly sliced), 200g fresh shrimp (peeled and deveined), 2 tbsp cornstarch, 100g shiitake mushrooms (sliced), 1 red bell pepper (thinly sliced), 1 tsp lime zest, 1 cup bean sprouts, 1/4 cup fresh cilantro (chopped), 1 cup snap peas
instructions: In a large pot, combine chicken broth, soy sauce, brown sugar, red pepper flakes, lime juice, and grated ginger | Bring to a boil and cook for 5 minutes to allow flavors to meld | Meanwhile, toss thinly sliced chicken with cornstarch in a bowl until it is completely coated | Add coated chicken, shrimp, and sliced shiitake mushrooms to the simmering broth | Reduce heat and simmer for 15 minutes until chicken is cooked through and shrimp are pink | Remove pot from heat and stir in snap peas, sliced red bell pepper, bean sprouts, lime zest, and chopped cilantro | Cover and let the soup stand for 5 minutes before serving | Ladle into bowls and serve immediately

ingredients: 500g fresh green beans (washed, trimmed, and cut in half), 300g lamb stew meat (cut into cubes), 1 large onion (diced), 4 cloves garlic (minced), 2 cups water, 2 tbsp olive oil, 3 fresh tomatoes (chopped) or 1 can (400g) diced tomatoes, 1 tsp salt, 1/2 tsp black pepper, 1/2 tsp allspice, 1/4 tsp cinnamon
instructions: Wash green beans and trim off stems, then cut in half and rinse in cold water | In a large pot, heat olive oil over medium-high heat | SautÃ© lamb stew meat, diced onions, and minced garlic with salt, pepper, allspice, and cinnamon, stirring occasionally, until meat is browned on all sides | Add 2 cups of water, green beans, and chopped tomatoes (or canned diced tomatoes) | Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to medium and cook for about 10 minutes | Cover the pot and simmer on low heat for around 45 minutes or until green beans are tender and meat is cooked through | Stir occasionally and add a splash of water if it becomes too dry | Taste and adjust seasoning as needed | Serve hot over plain white rice with warm pita bread on the side

ingredients: 1 large onion (diced), 4 cloves garlic (minced), 2 jalapeÃ±os (seeded and minced), 6 cups low-sodium chicken broth, 1 can (400g) diced tomatoes, 1 can (400g) black beans (drained and rinsed), 2 boneless skinless chicken breasts, 2 limes (juiced), 1/2 tsp salt, 1/4 tsp black pepper, 1/4 cup fresh cilantro leaves (chopped), 4 corn tortillas (cut into strips and fried), 1 avocado (sliced), 1/2 cup Monterey Jack cheese (shredded), 2 tbsp vegetable oil
instructions: In a large saucepan, heat vegetable oil over medium heat | Add diced onions and cook for 2 minutes until softened | Add minced garlic and jalapeÃ±os and cook for another minute until fragrant | Pour chicken broth, diced tomatoes (with their juices), and black beans into the pot and bring to a boil | Once at a boil, lower heat to a gentle simmer and add the whole chicken breasts | Cook chicken for 20 to 25 minutes until fully cooked through | Once chicken is cooked, carefully remove it from the pot and set aside on a cutting board | When cool enough to handle, shred the chicken using two forks and set aside | Add fresh lime juice and chopped cilantro to the pot and stir | In each serving bowl, place a mound of shredded chicken in the center | Ladle the hot soup over the chicken | Top each bowl with crispy tortilla strips, sliced avocado, and shredded Monterey Jack cheese | Serve immediately with extra lime wedges on the side

ingredients: 3 boneless skinless chicken breasts (cooked and cubed), 2 cups mozzarella cheese (shredded), 1 cup cheddar cheese (shredded), 1 can (400g) cream of chicken soup, 1/2 cup sour cream, 1/4 cup sliced black olives, 2 cups corn chips (Fritos), 1/2 tsp garlic powder, 1/2 tsp onion powder
instructions: Preheat oven to 350Â°F | Boil chicken breasts until cooked through, about 15-20 minutes, then drain and chop into cubes | While chicken is boiling, in a large bowl mix together cream of chicken soup, sour cream, olives, garlic powder, onion powder, and half of the shredded cheese if desired | Add cubed chicken to the mixture and stir to combine | Pour the chicken mixture into a greased casserole dish and spread evenly | Top generously with corn chips and remaining shredded cheese | Bake for about 20 minutes or until cheese is melted and bubbly and chips are golden | Serve hot

ingredients: 2 cups cooked chicken (shredded), 1 cup cheddar cheese (shredded), 2 tbsp mayonnaise, 1 can refrigerated biscuits (8 count), 1 can (400g) cream of chicken soup, 1/2 cup milk, salt and pepper to taste
instructions: Preheat oven to 375Â°F and grease a 9x13 baking dish | Mix shredded chicken and shredded cheese together with enough mayonnaise to hold it together â€” usually about 2 tablespoons | Season with salt and pepper | Flatten each biscuit into a 4-inch round | Place a spoonful of chicken and cheese mixture in the center of each flattened biscuit | Fold the sides of the biscuit up and over the filling, pinching seams to seal completely | Place chicken rolls seam-side down in the greased baking dish | In a small bowl, mix cream of chicken soup and milk, then heat in microwave until warm throughout, about 1-2 minutes | Pour soup and milk mixture evenly over the rollups | Bake at 375Â°F for 20 minutes or until the biscuits are golden brown and cooked through | Serve hot

ingredients: 350g wide egg noodles (uncooked), 1/2 cup dark raisins, 4 large eggs, 1 cup sour cream, 1/2 cup unsalted butter (melted), 1/2 cup granulated sugar, 1 1/2 cups half-and-half or whole milk, 1/2 tsp vanilla extract. Topping: 1 cup cornflakes (crushed), 2 tbsp brown sugar, 1 tbsp butter (melted)
instructions: Set oven to 350Â°F and butter a 13 x 9-inch baking dish | Spread UNCOOKED noodles evenly over the bottom of the buttered dish | Sprinkle raisins evenly over the noodles | In a large bowl, whisk eggs, sour cream, melted butter, sugar, vanilla, and salt until smooth | Whisk in half-and-half until fully incorporated | Pour the egg mixture evenly over the noodles and raisins | Let kugel stand for 5 minutes so the noodles begin to absorb the liquid | Meanwhile, mix crushed cornflakes and brown sugar in a bowl, then stir in 1 tbsp melted butter until crumbly | Sprinkle cornflake topping evenly over the kugel | Bake until set in the center, about 1 hour â€” the top should be golden and the custard should not jiggle | Serve warm or at room temperature

ingredients: 600g boneless skinless chicken breasts (cut into strips), 3 tbsp soy sauce, 1 tbsp curry powder, 1 tsp turmeric, 2 tbsp brown sugar, 1 can (400ml) coconut milk (divided), 1 tbsp vegetable oil, 1/2 cup creamy peanut butter, 1 tbsp red curry paste, 1 tbsp lime juice, 1 tbsp fish sauce, wooden skewers (soaked in water), chopped peanuts and cilantro for garnish
instructions: Soak wooden skewers in water for at least 30 minutes to prevent burning | Cut chicken breasts into long thin strips | In a bowl, combine soy sauce, curry powder, turmeric, brown sugar, and 1/4 cup coconut milk to make the marinade | Add chicken strips and toss to coat, then refrigerate for at least 1 hour | While chicken marinates, make peanut sauce: in a small saucepan, combine remaining coconut milk, peanut butter, red curry paste, lime juice, and fish sauce | Heat gently, whisking until smooth and warmed through | Thread marinated chicken strips onto soaked skewers in a zigzag pattern | Heat vegetable oil on a grill pan or barbecue to high heat | Grill skewers for 3-4 minutes per side until charred and cooked through | Sprinkle with chopped peanuts and cilantro | Serve hot with peanut sauce on the side for dipping

ingredients: 12 large white mushroom caps (stems removed), 100g blue cheese (crumbled), 100g cream cheese (softened), 2 tbsp half-and-half, 12 pecan halves, 12 fresh basil leaves, salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Preheat oven to 375Â°F (190Â°C) and lightly grease a baking sheet | In a medium bowl, combine the crumbled blue cheese and softened cream cheese | Beat them together with an electric mixer until smooth and well combined | Add the half-and-half and beat it in until the mixture is light and fluffy | Season with a pinch of salt and black pepper | Using a small spoon, fill each mushroom cap generously with the cheese mixture, mounding it slightly | Top each stuffed mushroom with a pecan half and a fresh basil leaf | Arrange stuffed mushrooms on the prepared baking sheet | Bake for 15-18 minutes until mushrooms are tender and the cheese filling is hot and slightly golden | Serve warm as an appetizer

ingredients: 4 boneless skinless chicken breast halves, 2 large eggs (beaten), 1 cup Italian breadcrumbs, 2 tbsp olive oil, 2 tbsp unsalted butter, 1 cup marinara sauce, 1/2 cup whole milk, 4 slices Swiss cheese, 4 slices mozzarella cheese, 1/4 cup Parmesan cheese (grated), 2 tbsp unsalted butter (for dotting)
instructions: Preheat oven to 300Â°F (150Â°C) | Dip each chicken breast half in beaten egg, letting excess drip off | Roll chicken in breadcrumbs to coat all over evenly | Heat olive oil and half the butter in a large skillet over medium heat | Fry breaded chicken until golden brown on both sides, about 4-5 minutes per side | In a small bowl, dilute marinara sauce with milk and stir until smooth | Cover the bottom of a baking dish with the diluted sauce | Layer fried chicken breasts on top of the sauce | Top each chicken breast with slices of Swiss cheese and mozzarella cheese | Sprinkle grated Parmesan evenly over all and dot with approximately 2 tablespoons of butter | Cover dish with foil and bake for 30 minutes | Uncover and bake for 10 to 15 minutes more â€” for bubbly, browned cheese, increase oven temperature to 400Â°F for the last 10 to 15 minutes, watching carefully so it does not burn | Serve hot â€” can be cooked a day or two ahead and reheated for serving

ingredients: 2 cups all-purpose flour, 1 cup Rice Krispies cereal, 2 tbsp cornstarch, 2 tbsp sugar, 2 tsp baking powder, 1/2 tsp baking soda, 1/2 tsp salt, 2 large eggs (separated), 1 3/4 cups whole milk, 1 tsp vanilla extract, 3 tbsp vegetable oil
instructions: Preheat traditional waffle iron to medium heat | In a large bowl, stir together flour, Rice Krispies, cornstarch, sugar, baking powder, baking soda, and salt until well combined | In a medium bowl, whisk egg yolks, milk, vanilla extract, and vegetable oil together | Using an electric mixer or balloon whisk, beat egg whites in a separate bowl until they form soft peaks | Pour milk mixture over dry ingredients and whisk until just combined | Gently fold in beaten egg whites until just incorporated â€” do not overmix; a few streaks of whites should remain visible | Pour 2/3 cup batter into the center of the preheated waffle iron and use the back of a dinner spoon to spread batter toward outer edges (batter should reach about 1/2 inch from edges before closing lid) â€” make sure to fill the waffle iron as directed; insufficient batter can cause Rice Krispies to scorch | Close lid and cook until deep golden brown, 3 to 4 minutes | Serve immediately | To keep waffles warm: transfer cooked waffles to a wire rack set on a baking sheet in a 400Â°F oven and bake until crisp and hot, 3 to 5 minutes | To freeze: after cooling completely, wrap each waffle in plastic wrap, then freeze in a zipper-lock bag for up to one month. Reheat on a wire rack set on a baking sheet in a 400Â°F oven until crisp and hot, about 5 minutes

ingredients: 2 cooked chicken breasts (cut into 1-inch cubes), 1 large apple (cored and cut into 1/2-inch cubes), 1/2 cup raisins, 1/4 cup raspberry vinaigrette, 3 tbsp mayonnaise, 1/4 cup celery (diced, optional), salt and black pepper to taste, mixed salad greens for serving
instructions: Cut apple into 1/2-inch cubes, leaving the skin on for color and texture | Cut cooked chicken breasts into 1-inch cubes | In a large bowl, combine cubed apple, raisins, and chicken | In a separate small bowl, whisk together raspberry vinaigrette and mayonnaise until completely smooth and well combined | Pour the dressing over the chicken mixture | Toss gently to coat everything evenly | Season with salt and black pepper to taste | Serve on a bed of mixed salad greens or as a sandwich filling

ingredients: 1/4 cup all-purpose flour, 1 tsp salt, 1/2 tsp black pepper, 1 tsp paprika, 2 chicken leg quarters or 4 bone-in chicken thighs, vegetable oil for frying, 1 cup spaghetti sauce, 1 can (100g) mushroom stems and pieces (with liquid), 1 tsp instant minced garlic, 1 tsp dried parsley flakes, 1/4 cup pitted ripe olives (sliced), 200g spaghetti
instructions: Heat 1/8 inch of vegetable oil in a large skillet over medium heat | In a shallow bowl, mix flour, salt, pepper, and paprika | Coat chicken pieces thoroughly with the flour mixture, shaking off excess | Cook chicken in hot oil over medium heat until light brown on all sides, about 15 to 20 minutes | In a separate bowl, mix spaghetti sauce, mushrooms (with their liquid), garlic, parsley flakes, and sliced olives | Drain excess fat from the skillet | Pour the sauce mixture over the browned chicken | Heat to boiling, then reduce heat to low | Cover tightly and simmer until the thickest pieces of chicken are tender, about 30 minutes | While chicken simmers, cook spaghetti according to package directions until al dente, then drain | Serve the chicken and sauce over the cooked spaghetti

ingredients: 2 cups cold root beer, 6 maraschino cherries, 6 small scoops vanilla ice cream (about 1/4 cup each), 6 popsicle molds and sticks
instructions: Pour cold root beer into a pitcher and place it in the freezer for 10 minutes â€” this makes it very cold and reduces the ice cream melt factor | Place one maraschino cherry at the bottom of each popsicle mold | Pour root beer into each mold until it is about half full | Gently lower a small scoop of vanilla ice cream into each mold so it comes to about three-quarters full | Slowly add more root beer until the molds are full â€” the ice cream will float to the top creating the classic float look | Use a spoon to scoop off any foam from the surface | Insert popsicle sticks and freeze for at least 6 hours or overnight until solid | To serve: remove from freezer and let stand at room temperature for 5 minutes before gently pulling the pops from the molds

ingredients: 300g frozen chopped spinach (thawed), 200g sharp cheddar cheese (finely grated), 1/2 cup pecans (finely chopped), 1/3 cup mayonnaise, 2 packages (250g each) cream cheese (softened), 1/2 tsp salt, 1/4 tsp fresh ground black pepper, 3 tbsp mango chutney, 1/4 tsp ground nutmeg, extra pecans for garnish, crackers for serving
instructions: Line a 9 x 5-inch loaf pan with heavy-duty plastic wrap, leaving overhang on all sides | Press thawed spinach between layers of paper towels to remove as much excess moisture as possible, then set aside | In a medium bowl, stir together grated cheddar cheese, chopped pecans, and mayonnaise until well combined | Spread half of the cheddar mixture evenly into the bottom of the prepared pan | In another bowl, stir together the drained spinach, one package of cream cheese, salt, and pepper until smooth | Spread spinach mixture evenly over the cheddar layer | In a third bowl, stir together the remaining package of cream cheese, chutney, and nutmeg until smooth | Spread chutney mixture evenly over the spinach layer | Top with the remaining cheddar cheese mixture, spreading to the edges | Cover with the overhanging plastic wrap and freeze for up to 1 month if desired, or refrigerate for at least 4 hours | To serve: thaw in refrigerator overnight if frozen, then invert onto a serving plate, remove plastic wrap, and garnish with extra pecans | Serve with assorted crackers â€” this makes one large loaf or can be divided into mini loaf pans to make 2-3 smaller loaves

ingredients: 2 1/2 cups all-purpose flour, 1/2 tsp salt, 1/2 tsp baking powder, 1 cup unsalted butter (softened), 1 1/3 cups granulated sugar, 1 large egg, 1 tsp vanilla extract, 1/2 tsp peppermint extract, red food coloring, powdered sugar for dusting, lollipop sticks
instructions: Sift together flour, salt, and baking powder and set aside | In a large bowl, cream softened butter and sugar together until light and fluffy | Add egg and beat until fully incorporated | Add vanilla extract and peppermint extract, mixing well | Gradually add the dry mixture, beating until combined into a smooth dough | Remove half of the dough from the bowl | To the remaining half, add red food coloring a few drops at a time, beating until the color is fully combined and vibrant | On a sheet of waxed paper dusted with powdered sugar, roll out the red dough to form a large rectangle about 1/4-inch thick | Repeat with the uncolored dough on a separate sheet of waxed paper | Refrigerate both sheets of dough for 2 hours until firm | Tear out a fresh sheet of waxed or parchment paper and sprinkle with powdered sugar to prevent sticking | Very carefully slide the red dough on top of the white dough, using the waxed paper to help position it | Trim edges if uneven and patch gaps if necessary | Using the waxed paper to help, roll the stacked dough tightly into a log, creating a spiral swirl effect | Wrap the log in plastic wrap and chill in the refrigerator for another 2 hours until very firm | Preheat oven to 375Â°F and line baking sheets with parchment paper | Slice the chilled dough log into 1/2-inch thick rounds and place on prepared baking sheets about 1 inch apart | Insert a lollipop stick about 1 inch through the flat side of each cookie | Bake for 8 to 10 minutes until edges are just set but not browned | Remove from oven and let cool on a wire rack before serving

ingredients: 8 chicken thighs (bone-in, skin-on), 3 tbsp fresh ginger (grated), 4 cloves garlic (minced), 3 tbsp oyster sauce, 2 tbsp soy sauce, 2 tbsp brown sugar, 1 tbsp sesame oil, sliced green onions for garnish, steamed white rice for serving
instructions: In a large zip-lock bag, combine grated ginger, minced garlic, oyster sauce, soy sauce, brown sugar, and sesame oil | Add chicken thighs to the bag, seal, and massage the marinade into the chicken | Refrigerate overnight or for at least 4 hours, turning the bag occasionally | When ready to cook, preheat oven to 375Â°F (190Â°C) | Line a casserole dish with aluminum foil for easy cleanup | Arrange marinated chicken thighs skin-side up in the prepared dish, pouring any remaining marinade over them | Bake for 45 minutes until chicken skin is brown and crisp and internal temperature reaches 165Â°F (74Â°C) | Remove from oven and let rest for 5 minutes | Use the chicken renderings and pan juices to pour over steamed white rice | Serve chicken alongside the rice and garnish with sliced green onions

ingredients: 4 whole ayu fish or small trout (cleaned, about 200g each), 2 tbsp sea salt, 1 lemon, 2 citrons or yuzu (sliced), metal skewers
instructions: Rinse fish thoroughly under cold water and pat completely dry with paper towels | Generously rub each fish all over â€” including the fins â€” with sea salt, ensuring even coverage | Take a metal skewer and carefully thread it through the head and body of each fish, curving it slightly so the fish looks like it is swimming â€” this traditional technique helps with even cooking and presentation | Preheat a grill or broiler to medium-high heat | Place skewered fish on the grill or under the broiler | Cook for 5-7 minutes per side until the skin is crisp and blistered and the flesh is opaque and flakes easily | While fish cooks, slice lemon and citron | Serve immediately with citron or yuzu slices â€” the citrus is squeezed over the fish before eating | This dish is traditionally served with steamed rice and pickled vegetables

ingredients: 300g sushi-grade tuna (finely diced), 1 tbsp soy sauce, 1 tsp sesame oil, 1 tsp sriracha, 1 avocado (diced), 1 green onion (thinly sliced), 1 tsp toasted sesame seeds, wonton chips or cucumber slices for serving
instructions: Ensure tuna is sushi-grade and very fresh â€” it should be bright red and have no fishy odor | Using a very sharp knife, cut tuna into small uniform dice about 1/4-inch cubes | In a bowl, gently combine diced tuna with soy sauce, sesame oil, and sriracha â€” adjust sriracha to your spice preference | Gently fold in diced avocado and sliced green onion, being careful not to mash the avocado | Cover and refrigerate for 15 minutes to allow flavors to meld | Spoon tartare onto serving plates using a ring mold for a professional presentation if desired | Sprinkle toasted sesame seeds on top | Serve immediately with crispy wonton chips or cucumber slices for scooping

ingredients: 50ml silver tequila, 25ml fresh lime juice, 20ml Cointreau or triple sec, 1 tsp agave syrup (optional), lime wheel for garnish, salt for rimming glass, ice cubes
instructions: Chill a margarita glass or rocks glass in the freezer for 10 minutes | Run a lime wedge around the rim of the glass, then dip the rim into a plate of salt, rotating to coat evenly | Fill a cocktail shaker with ice cubes | Pour in tequila, fresh lime juice, Cointreau, and agave syrup if using | Shake vigorously for 15 seconds until the outside of the shaker feels very cold | Fill the salt-rimmed glass with fresh ice | Strain the margarita into the prepared glass | Garnish with a lime wheel on the rim | Serve immediately

ingredients: 1 large Vidalia onion, 2 tbsp unsalted butter, 1 beef bouillon cube (crumbled), 2 tbsp Worcestershire sauce, salt and black pepper to taste, fresh parsley for garnish
instructions: Preheat oven to 425Â°F (220Â°C) | Peel the outer skin off the onion and cut off just the very bottom roots â€” do not cut off the whole bottom core as this holds the onion together | Cut the top of the onion into a pointed cone shape, saving the cut-out portion to chop and use later | Set the onion in the center of a large piece of aluminum foil, bringing the sides up to create a loose pouch shaped kind of like a Hershey's Kiss | Place the crumbled bouillon cube into the opening at the top of the onion | Add butter and pour Worcestershire sauce over the top | Chop the saved core portion and add it on top | Bring the foil together and seal well, creating a tight packet | Place the foil packet on a baking sheet and bake for 1 hour and 30 minutes | Carefully open the packet (watch for hot steam) and place the onion in a serving bowl | Slice the onion into wedges and spoon any sauce from the foil over the top | Garnish with fresh parsley and serve as a side dish

ingredients: 4 cups whole milk, 2 tbsp cornstarch, 200g dark chocolate (70% cocoa, finely chopped), 3 tbsp granulated sugar (adjust to taste), pinch of salt, churros for dipping (optional)
instructions: Pour the milk into a medium saucepan and add the cornstarch | Whisk thoroughly to dissolve the cornstarch completely â€” there should be no lumps | Once the cornstarch is dissolved, heat the milk over medium heat just until it begins to boil, then immediately remove from heat | Add the chopped dark chocolate right away and begin stirring continuously until the chocolate is completely melted and incorporated | If the milk cools off too fast and the chocolate stops melting, place the pan back on the stove over low heat briefly | Return the pan to medium-low heat and stir slowly but constantly â€” do not cook over high heat as this may cause lumping | Taste the chocolate for sweetness and add more sugar if necessary, stirring to dissolve | The mixture should thicken quickly â€” as soon as you see it visibly thicken, remove the pan from the heat immediately so the cornstarch does not thin out from overcooking | Ladle immediately into small cups and serve piping hot | Note: use a clean spoon every time you taste the chocolate â€” enzymes from your mouth can cause a thickened cornstarch mixture to thin | Serve with churros for dipping for the authentic Spanish experience

ingredients: 6 green bananas (unripe, firm), 1 large onion (thinly sliced), 1 cup white vinegar, 6 cloves garlic (smashed), 1/2 cup green olives (pitted), 2 tsp salt (plus more for water), 1 tsp whole black peppercorns, 2 bay leaves, 1/3 cup olive oil, 1/3 cup light olive oil or vegetable oil, 1 cup water
instructions: Prepare the bananas: using a knife, cut off both ends of each banana and make a shallow cut along the outside curve of the banana skin, but DO NOT remove the skins â€” this slit helps them peel easier later | Bring a large pot of water to a boil and add 1 to 2 tablespoons of salt and 2 teaspoons of oil (this helps the bananas peel more easily) | Place bananas in the boiling water and cook for approximately 20 minutes on medium-low heat â€” do not boil too long or they will come apart | While bananas cook, make the escabeche sauce: place sliced onion, vinegar, smashed garlic, green olives, salt, peppercorns, bay leaves, both oils, and water into a separate pot | Stir well and bring to medium heat until the mixture gets hot | Reduce heat to low and simmer for approximately 1 hour, allowing the flavors to meld | Remove sauce from heat and set aside to cool to room temperature | Check bananas by lightly stabbing with a toothpick â€” they are done when tender but still firm | Drain bananas, peel off the skins, and cut into 1-inch thick rounds | Place banana rounds in a glass or plastic bowl (non-reactive container) | Pour the cooled escabeche sauce over the bananas | Stir and mix gently to coat evenly | Cover and marinate at room temperature for at least 24 hours â€” this is essential for the flavors to develop | You can refrigerate after marinating, but ensure they have cooled to room temperature first | Serve as a side dish or appetizer, either at room temperature or chilled

ingredients: 800g pork shoulder or pork loin, 6 cloves garlic (minced), 2 tsp ground cumin, 1 tsp dried oregano, 1/3 cup fresh lime juice, 1/4 cup orange juice, 3 tbsp olive oil, 8 slider rolls, 4 slices Swiss cheese (halved), 100g sliced ham, dill pickle slices, yellow mustard, salt and pepper
instructions: Lightly oil the inside of a crockpot or slow cooker | Place pork in the crockpot and sprinkle with half of the minced garlic, cumin, and oregano | In a small bowl, mix the remaining garlic, cumin, and oregano with lime juice, orange juice, and olive oil | Pour the juice mixture over the pork | Cover and cook on low for 6-7 hours or on high for 4-5 hours until pork is cooked through and fork-tender | Transfer cooked pork to a cutting board and shred with two forks or break into pieces | Skim excess fat from the cooking juices and reserve the juices | Preheat broiler | Split slider rolls and place the bottom halves on a baking sheet | Divide Swiss cheese among the bottom halves and broil until melted, about 1-2 minutes | On the cheese-topped bottom buns, layer sliced ham and shredded pork | Drizzle reserved cooking juices generously over the meat | Top with dill pickle slices and a spread of yellow mustard | Close with the top halves of the rolls | Serve immediately with extra juices on the side for dipping

ingredients: 500g jumbo shrimp (peeled and deveined, tails on), 1/3 cup ginger preserves or marmalade, 2 limes (juiced), 1/4 cup fresh cilantro (chopped), 2 tbsp olive oil, 2 cloves garlic (minced), salt and black pepper to taste, steamed rice for serving
instructions: Pat shrimp completely dry with paper towels â€” moisture prevents proper searing | In a large skillet or wok, heat olive oil over medium-high heat until shimmering | Add shrimp in a single layer and stir-fry until partially cooked, about 1 to 2 minutes â€” they should just start turning pink | Stir in ginger preserves and minced garlic, tossing to coat the shrimp evenly | Continue cooking until shrimp are fully pink and firm, about 2 minutes more â€” do not overcook or they will become rubbery | Remove skillet from heat immediately | Squeeze fresh lime juice over the shrimp and toss with chopped cilantro | Season to taste with salt and black pepper | Toss everything together one final time | Serve immediately over steamed white rice with extra lime wedges on the side

ingredients: 1 kg beef tenderloin fillet (whole), 1/4 cup soy sauce, 4 cloves garlic (minced), 3 tbsp Thai red curry paste, 1 tsp white pepper, 2 tbsp honey, 1 tbsp vegetable oil, 1 tsp coarse sea salt, 1/4 cup water (as needed for pan)
instructions: Using a sharp knife, cut into the tenderloin fillet about 2/3 of the way through, making five evenly spaced cuts to mark 5 equal serving portions â€” do not cut all the way through | Place the meat into a shallow glass dish | In a bowl, combine soy sauce, minced garlic, red curry paste, white pepper, honey, vegetable oil, and coarse sea salt, whisking until well blended | Pour the marinade over the meat, coating all sides thoroughly | Cover with plastic wrap and refrigerate overnight, or for at least 8 hours | Reserve the marinade from the dish for basting later | Bring the meat to room temperature for at least 1 hour before cooking â€” this ensures even cooking | Preheat oven to 500Â°F (260Â°C) | Place the tenderloin fillet in a shallow roasting pan and pour the reserved marinade around it | Bake for 20 to 25 minutes, basting every 5 minutes with the pan juices | If the sauce is drying up too quickly, add small amounts of water to the pan to maintain your desired consistency | Remove from oven and let the meat rest for 10 minutes before slicing | Drizzle the pan sauce over the sliced tenderloin and serve | This dish pairs beautifully with roasted mini potatoes, pan-fried whole small cremini mushrooms, and steamed asparagus with lemon

recipe_name: Rich and Creamy Garlic Mashed Potatoes
ingredients: 1 kg russet potatoes (peeled and cubed), 1/2 cup half-and-half, 6 cloves garlic (minced), 4 tbsp unsalted butter, 1/2 cup Parmesan cheese (freshly grated), salt to taste, white pepper to taste, fresh chives for garnish
instructions: Peel potatoes and cut into uniform 1-inch cubes | Place potatoes in a large pot and cover with cold salted water by 1 inch | Bring to a boil and cook until potatoes are very soft and easily pierced with a fork, about 15-18 minutes | While potatoes boil, place half-and-half, minced garlic, and butter in a small saucepan | Heat over medium setting until warmed through and butter is fully melted â€” do not let it boil | Drain potatoes thoroughly and return them to the hot pot for 1 minute to steam off excess moisture | Mash potatoes using a potato masher, ricer, or electric mixer until smooth and creamy â€” an electric mixer gives the creamiest results | Gradually pour in the warm cream, garlic, and butter mixture while mixing continuously | Add freshly grated Parmesan cheese and mix until fully incorporated and the potatoes are silky | Taste before adding salt â€” Parmesan cheese can be quite salty on its own | Add white pepper and additional salt only if needed | The potatoes will thicken slightly as they sit, so let them rest about 5 minutes before serving | Transfer to a serving bowl and garnish with fresh chopped chives

ingredients: 4 boneless skinless chicken breasts, 3 large eggs, 1/4 cup fresh flat-leaf parsley (finely chopped), 4 cloves garlic (minced), 1 tsp kosher salt, 1/2 tsp fresh ground black pepper, 2 cups panko breadcrumbs, 1 cup canola oil (for frying), lemon wedges for serving
instructions: Slice each chicken breast in half horizontally to create thin cutlets | Pound the thicker ends gently with a meat mallet to an even 1/4-inch thickness | Cut any very large pieces in half â€” you want sandwich-size pieces | Beat the eggs in a medium bowl until well combined | Stir in chopped parsley, minced garlic, kosher salt, and black pepper | Sprinkle one side of the chicken pieces lightly with salt and place them into the beaten egg mixture | Mix with your hands to coat every piece thoroughly | The chicken can be cooked right away, or covered and left to marinate in the refrigerator for up to overnight for deeper flavor | Sprinkle some panko breadcrumbs on a small rimmed baking sheet | Place a piece of egg-coated chicken on top and cover with more panko | Using your fist, pound the panko gently into the chicken to make it adhere â€” start slowly, then pound a little harder until the crumbs are firmly stuck | Repeat with all chicken pieces | Pour 1/4 inch of oil (about 1 cup) into a 10-inch nonstick skillet and heat over medium to medium-high heat | The oil is ready when a sprinkle of panko sizzles immediately | Fry 1 to 2 cutlets at a time without crowding the pan, flipping only once | Cook until nicely browned, about 3 minutes on the first side and 1 minute on the second | Transfer fried cutlets to a tray lined with paper towels to drain | Serve immediately with fresh lemon wedges for squeezing over the crispy cutlets

ingredients: 2 tbsp olive oil, 1 large onion (diced), 3 carrots (diced), 3 celery stalks (diced), 4 cloves garlic (minced), 1 1/2 cups dried brown lentils (rinsed), 1 can (400g) crushed tomatoes, 6 cups chicken or vegetable broth, 1 tsp ground cumin, 1/2 tsp dried thyme, 1 bay leaf, 3/4 cup quinoa (rinsed), 1 tbsp red wine vinegar, salt and black pepper to taste, fresh parsley for garnish
instructions: In a large heavy-bottomed pot, heat olive oil over medium heat | Add diced onion, carrots, and celery and sautÃ© for 6-7 minutes until vegetables begin to soften | Add minced garlic and cook for 1 minute until fragrant | Stir in rinsed lentils, crushed tomatoes, broth, cumin, thyme, and bay leaf | Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer covered for 35 minutes, stirring occasionally | Stir in rinsed quinoa and continue simmering for 15-20 minutes until quinoa is tender and lentils are fully cooked | Remove bay leaf | Stir in red wine vinegar â€” this brightens all the flavors | Season to taste with salt and black pepper | Ladle into bowls and garnish with fresh chopped parsley | Serve hot with crusty bread on the side

ingredients: 3 ripe bananas (peeled), 4 cups cold water, 1/2 cup fresh lime juice (about 4-5 limes), 1/3 cup sugar (adjust to taste), 1/4 cup fresh lemon juice, ice cubes for serving, lemon slices for garnish
instructions: Peel the bananas and place them in a microwave-safe bowl | Microwave on high for 30 to 60 seconds until the bananas are softened and half-mushy â€” this releases their natural sweetness | Transfer warm bananas to a blender | Add cold water, fresh lime juice, sugar, and lemon juice to the blender | Blend on high until completely smooth and no banana chunks remain | Taste and add more sugar if needed for desired sweetness | Pass the mixture through a fine mesh sieve into a large bowl or jug to remove any fibrous bits | Fill serving glasses generously with ice cubes | Pour the strained banana lemonade over the ice | Garnish with lemon slices on the rim | Serve immediately while cold and refreshing

ingredients: 1 large onion, 4 cloves garlic (minced), 2 tbsp olive oil, 1/4 tsp fresh ground black pepper, 1 can (400g) whole tomatoes (drained), 1 tsp dried basil, 1/2 tsp dried mint, 4 large eggs, 1/4 cup Parmesan cheese (freshly grated), salt to taste, thick slices of toasted garlic bread for serving
instructions: Cut the onion in half lengthwise, then place each half cut-side down on a cutting board and thinly slice into long strips | Finely mince the garlic cloves | Heat olive oil in a large frying pan over medium heat | When hot, add the sliced onion, minced garlic, and black pepper | Cook uncovered, stirring occasionally, just until the onion is soft, about 3 to 4 minutes â€” do not brown | Meanwhile, drain the canned tomatoes well, discarding the liquid | Place the drained tomatoes in a medium bowl and coarsely crush them using your hands or a potato masher | Stir dried basil and dried mint into the crushed tomatoes | Taste and add a pinch of salt if needed | Pour the tomato mixture into the pan with the onions and stir to combine, then spread into an even layer | Once the mixture begins to bubble, use a spoon to make 4 small wells in the sauce | Crack one egg into each well, trying not to break the yolks | Sprinkle grated Parmesan cheese over everything | Cover the pan and continue cooking over medium heat until the egg whites turn opaque and the yolks are still slightly runny, about 7 to 8 minutes | Using a large spoon, scoop out some of the tomato and onion mixture along with each egg | Serve immediately on top of thick slices of toasted garlic bread

ingredients: 1 large spaghetti squash (about 1.5 kg), 1 can (400g) black beans (drained and rinsed), 1 cup frozen corn (thawed), 1 can (400g) diced tomatoes with green chilies, 1 can (100g) diced green chilies, 1/4 cup sliced black olives, 1 tsp ground cumin, 1/4 cup fresh cilantro (chopped), 1/4 tsp cayenne pepper, 1 1/2 cups cheddar cheese (shredded), salt to taste, sour cream for serving
instructions: Preheat oven to 350Â°F (175Â°C) | Pierce the spaghetti squash all over with a sharp knife to allow steam to escape | Place whole squash in the microwave and cook for 10-12 minutes until the skin is soft to the touch â€” alternatively, roast in the oven at 400Â°F for 45 minutes | Remove squash and let cool until safe to handle | Cut squash in half lengthwise and scoop out the seeds and stringy pulp with a spoon | Use a fork to scrape the flesh into a large bowl, separating it into spaghetti-like strands | Add drained black beans, corn, diced tomatoes with green chilies, green chilies, sliced olives, cumin, chopped cilantro, and cayenne pepper to the bowl | Stir everything together until well combined | Season with salt to taste | Transfer mixture to a greased casserole dish and spread evenly | Top generously with shredded cheddar cheese | Bake in preheated oven for 30 minutes until the cheese is melted and bubbly | Let sit for 5-10 minutes before serving | Serve hot with a dollop of sour cream on top

ingredients: 1 kg winter squash (butternut or acorn, peeled and thinly sliced), 2 tbsp extra virgin olive oil (divided), 2 medium onions (thinly sliced), 4 cloves garlic (minced), 1 tsp dried sage, 1 tsp fresh thyme leaves, 1 tsp kosher salt, 1/2 tsp black pepper, 1/2 cup fresh parsley (chopped), 1 cup breadcrumbs (divided), 1 cup part-skim mozzarella cheese (shredded), 1/2 cup Parmesan cheese (grated)
