instructions: Preheat oven to 350Â°F (175Â°C) | Lightly coat a 2-quart square baking dish with nonstick cooking spray and set aside | In a large skillet, heat 1 tablespoon of the olive oil over medium heat | Add sliced onions and minced garlic and cook about 6 minutes until tender, stirring occasionally | Remove from heat and stir in sage, thyme, kosher salt, and pepper | Place half of the squash slices in the prepared dish, overlapping slightly | Sprinkle evenly with the onion mixture and half of the breadcrumbs | Top with remaining squash slices | Cover dish with foil and bake for about 45 minutes until squash is nearly tender | Meanwhile, in a small bowl, combine the remaining breadcrumbs, remaining 1 tablespoon olive oil, and chopped parsley â€” mix well and set aside | Remove foil from baking dish | Sprinkle squash with shredded mozzarella, grated Parmesan, and the breadcrumb-parsley mixture | Bake uncovered for 10 to 15 more minutes until crumbs are golden brown and squash is fully tender | Let stand for 10 minutes before serving â€” this allows the gratin to set | Serve warm as a side dish

ingredients: 120ml chilled champagne or sparkling wine, 30ml Hpnotiq liqueur, fresh blueberries for garnish, lemon twist for garnish
instructions: Chill a champagne flute in the freezer for 5 minutes | Pour Hpnotiq liqueur into the chilled flute first â€” its vibrant blue color creates the base of the drink | Slowly top with chilled champagne or sparkling wine, tilting the glass slightly to preserve the layering effect | Watch the bubbles rise through the blue liqueur for a beautiful visual effect | Garnish with a few fresh blueberries dropped into the glass and a lemon twist on the rim | Serve immediately while the champagne is still effervescent

ingredients: 1 cup water, 1/2 cup Arborio or short-grain white rice, 2 cups unsweetened rice milk (plus more for reheating), 1/3 cup maple syrup, 1/4 tsp salt, 1 tsp ground cinnamon (plus more for garnish), 1 tsp vanilla extract, 1/3 cup raisins, chopped nuts for topping (optional)
instructions: In a medium saucepan, bring water to a boil | Once boiling, add the rice, reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 15 minutes until water is mostly absorbed | Add rice milk, maple syrup, salt, and cinnamon | Cover and bring back to just barely boiling, then remove the lid and simmer uncovered until thick and creamy, about 15-20 minutes, stirring once in a while to prevent sticking | The rice should be tender and the mixture should have a creamy, porridge-like consistency | Remove from heat and stir in vanilla extract and raisins | Pour into serving dishes | Sprinkle the top with a dusting of ground cinnamon | Let cool for 5 minutes, then serve warm | If planning to serve later, the pudding will thicken with time â€” add a splash more rice milk when reheating to restore creaminess | Top with chopped nuts if desired for added texture

ingredients: 1 1/2 cups graham cracker crumbs, 1/4 cup powdered sugar, 6 tbsp unsalted butter (melted), 24 mini Hershey's chocolate bars, 12 large marshmallows (cut in half)
instructions: Preheat oven to 350Â°F (175Â°C) | In a bowl, mix crushed graham cracker crumbs, powdered sugar, and melted butter together until the texture resembles wet sand | Take a mini muffin tray and fill each cup less than halfway with the graham cracker mixture, pressing down firmly with your fingers or the back of a spoon to form a crust | Bake the crusts at 350Â°F for 4-5 minutes until they are set and slightly golden | Remove tray from oven and place one mini Hershey's chocolate bar on top of each warm crust | Top the chocolate with half a marshmallow (cut side down) | Return to oven and bake at 350Â°F for 2-4 minutes until marshmallows are puffed and golden â€” watch closely as they can burn quickly | Remove from oven and let cool in the pan for 5 minutes | Carefully remove each bite and serve warm for gooey, melted s'more goodness

ingredients: 300g Cheshire cheese (crumbled), 100g unsalted butter (softened), 1/4 tsp ground mace, 1/4 tsp ground allspice, 3 tbsp sweet sherry, 1 tbsp Madeira wine, 60g melted butter (for sealing)
instructions: In a mixing bowl, combine crumbled Cheshire cheese with softened butter and spices (mace and allspice) | Adjust the amount of butter depending on how dry the cheese is â€” the mixture should be spreadable but not loose | Beat thoroughly with a wooden spoon until smooth and well blended | Add sweet sherry and Madeira wine, mixing through until fully incorporated | Press the mixture firmly into small ramekins or pots, smoothing down the top with the back of a spoon | Pour a thin layer of melted butter over the top of each pot to seal â€” this preserves the cheese and forms a classic seal | Cover with plastic wrap and refrigerate for at least 24 hours to allow the flavors to blend and mature | Remove from refrigerator one hour before serving to bring to room temperature | Serve spread on crusty bread, toast, or crackers

ingredients: 500g white fish fillets (boneless, such as cod or tilapia), 1 small onion (finely chopped), 2 large eggs (beaten), 3 tbsp evaporated milk, 1/2 tsp salt, 1/4 tsp white pepper, vegetable oil for deep frying, sweet chili sauce or tartar sauce for serving
instructions: Steam or gently boil fish fillets until fully cooked and flaky, about 8-10 minutes | Drain fish thoroughly and let cool until easy to handle | Flake the fish finely with a fork, removing any remaining bones | Finely chop onion and mix with the flaked fish in a bowl | Add beaten eggs, evaporated milk, salt, and white pepper | Mix thoroughly until the mixture is well combined and holds together when squeezed | Shape mixture into golf ball-sized balls, squeezing out any surplus liquid as you form them â€” the balls should be firm enough to hold their shape | Heat vegetable oil in a deep pot to 350Â°F (175Â°C) | Carefully drop fish balls into the hot oil and fry in batches until golden brown on all sides, about 3-4 minutes | Remove with a slotted spoon and drain on paper towels | Serve hot with sweet chili sauce or tartar sauce, or enjoy them cold as a snack

recipe_name: Corn on the Cob With Lemon-Basil Butter
ingredients: 6 ears fresh corn (husks on), 1/2 cup unsalted butter (softened), 1/4 cup fresh basil leaves (packed), 1 tbsp lemon zest, 2 tbsp fresh lemon juice, 1 clove garlic (minced), 1/2 tsp salt, 1/4 tsp ground black pepper
instructions: Make the lemon-basil butter: place softened butter, fresh basil leaves, lemon zest, lemon juice, minced garlic, salt, and pepper in a food processor | Pulse until basil is finely incorporated and the butter turns a light green color | Transfer butter to a small serving bowl and set aside â€” can be made up to 3 days ahead and refrigerated | Prepare the corn: carefully pull off the dry outer husks, setting aside several to tear into 1/4-inch-wide strips to use as ties | Gently peel back the inner husks without detaching them from the cob | Remove all silk threads from the corn kernels | Lightly coat each ear of corn with a generous layer of lemon-basil butter | Lay the inner husks back in place around the corn, covering the kernels | Tie the top of each ear with the reserved husk strips to secure | Immerse tied corn in a large bowl of cold water and soak for 20 minutes â€” this prevents the husks from burning on the grill | Drain well | Place corn on a preheated hot grill and cook for 20 minutes, turning often with tongs, until husks are charred and corn is tender | Remove ties and husks, and serve immediately with extra lemon-basil butter on the side

ingredients: 2 cups raw walnut halves, 1 tbsp extra virgin olive oil, 2 tbsp agave syrup or maple syrup, 1/2 tsp sea salt, 1 vanilla bean (split lengthwise, seeds scraped), 1/4 tsp ground cinnamon (optional)
instructions: Place walnuts and olive oil in a cast iron skillet and turn heat to high | As soon as you hear the slightest sizzle, immediately turn heat down to medium or low â€” nuts burn quickly so monitor closely | Toast walnuts for 3-4 minutes, stirring frequently, until they smell nutty and fragrant | Add agave syrup and stir to distribute evenly around the pan, cooking for another 1-2 minutes | Sprinkle in sea salt and stir | Scrape the seeds from the vanilla bean and stir into the walnuts, ensuring even coating | Remove walnuts from pan and spread on parchment paper to cool â€” they will crisp up as they cool | Add just a dash of ground cinnamon if desired | Let cool completely before serving or storing in an airtight container

ingredients: For pastry: 4 oz cream cheese (softened), 1/2 cup unsalted butter (softened), 1 cup all-purpose flour. For filling: 2 large eggs, 3/4 cup granulated sugar, 2 tbsp unsalted butter (melted), 2 tsp lemon zest, 1/4 cup fresh lemon juice, pinch of salt
instructions: Blend together cream cheese and softened butter until smooth and creamy | Stir in flour gradually until a soft dough forms, then shape into a ball, wrap in plastic, and chill for at least 1 hour | Preheat oven to 350Â°F (175Â°C) | Divide chilled dough into 24 equal balls | Place each ball in an ungreased miniature muffin tin cup | Using your fingers, press dough evenly against the bottom and up the sides of each cup to form a tart shell | Prepare the filling: whisk together eggs, sugar, melted butter, lemon zest, lemon juice, and salt until smooth and well combined | Divide filling evenly among the 24 tart shells, filling each about 3/4 full | Bake for 25-30 minutes until filling is set and edges are lightly golden | Remove from oven and let tarts cool in the pan for several minutes | Gently run a knife around the edges and carefully remove tarts from tins | Transfer to a wire rack to cool completely | Dust with powdered sugar before serving if desired

recipe_name: Stuffed Green Pepper Soup For A Crowd
ingredients: 500g lean ground beef, 3 large green bell peppers (diced), 1 large onion (diced), 3 celery stalks (diced), 200g fresh mushrooms (sliced), 4 cloves garlic (minced), 2 cans (400g each) tomato sauce, 2 cans (400g each) diced tomatoes, 1 tbsp fresh basil (chopped), 1 tsp dried basil, 1 tsp salt, 1/2 tsp black pepper, 2 cups uncooked white rice, 4 cups water
instructions: In a 12-inch skillet, cook ground beef and diced onion for 10 minutes over medium-high heat until meat is browned and onion is no longer pink â€” drain excess fat | Add minced garlic and cook just until fragrant, about 1 minute, then set aside | In a medium saucepan, bring 2 cups water to a boil | Add uncooked rice, cover, and remove from heat | Let sit for 5 minutes, then fluff with a fork and set aside â€” the rice will finish cooking in the soup | In a 6-quart crockpot or large Dutch oven, combine the beef mixture, diced green peppers, diced celery, sliced mushrooms, tomato sauce, diced tomatoes with their juices, fresh basil, dried basil, salt, and pepper | Cook at low temperature, stirring occasionally, just until peppers are softened but still have a little crunch to them â€” about 2-3 hours on low in a crockpot or 45 minutes on the stovetop | Add the partially cooked rice to the soup and stir to combine | Let cook for another 10 minutes until rice is fully tender and has absorbed some of the soup liquid | Ladle into bowls and serve hot â€” this makes enough for a crowd

ingredients: 1 large loaf French or Italian bread, 8 oz cream cheese (softened), 2 tbsp ranch dressing mix (dry), 1 1/2 cups sharp cheddar cheese (shredded), 2 tbsp fresh parsley (chopped, for garnish)
instructions: Preheat oven to 450Â°F (230Â°C) | Slice the loaf of bread in half lengthwise and place both halves cut-side up on a baking sheet | Slice each half into 1-inch thick slices, BUT do not slice all the way through to the bottom crust â€” leave the slices attached so the loaf still holds together | In a bowl, blend softened cream cheese with dry ranch dressing mix until smooth and well combined | Spread cream cheese mixture generously on top of the sliced loaves, getting some between each cut | Sprinkle shredded cheddar cheese evenly over the top | Bake for 10 to 15 minutes until brown and bubbly, with the cheese fully melted and golden | Remove from oven and let cool for 2-3 minutes | Garnish with chopped parsley | Pull apart individual cheese fingers and serve warm

ingredients: 8 slices thick white bread (crusts removed), 1/2 cup unsalted butter (softened at room temperature), 1/2 cup icing sugar (powdered sugar), 2 tbsp black sesame seeds
instructions: Take butter out of the refrigerator and let it soften at room temperature for about 15 minutes before starting | Preheat oven to 150Â°C (300Â°F) | In a bowl, cream softened butter with icing sugar using a wooden spoon or electric mixer until smooth, pale, and fluffy â€” this is your buttercream icing | Spread the buttercream icing thinly and evenly over both sides of each slice of bread | Cut the crusts off the bread slices to neaten the edges | Cut each slice into quarters (triangles or squares) and place on a baking tray lined with parchment paper | Sprinkle a few black sesame seeds over the top of each piece | Bake in the low oven at 150Â°C (300Â°F) for 15 minutes â€” the low temperature allows the bread to dry out and crisp without burning | Remove from oven and let cool on the tray â€” the toast will crisp up further as it cools and the icing sugar and butter set | Serve once cooled and crisp, or store in an airtight container for up to 3 days

ingredients: For crust: 2 cups all-purpose flour, 1 cup unsalted butter (softened), 1/2 cup granulated sugar. For cream layer: 8 oz cream cheese (softened), 1 cup powdered sugar, 1 tsp vanilla extract. For filling: 1 can (600g) lemon pie filling. For topping: 1 package Dream Whip or 2 cups whipped topping, 1 cup cold milk, lemon zest for garnish
instructions: Preheat oven to 350Â°F (175Â°C) | In a medium mixing bowl, combine flour, softened butter, and sugar with a fork until crumbly and the mixture resembles coarse sand | Press crust mixture firmly into an ungreased 9 x 13 baking dish in an even layer | Bake crust for 20 minutes or until slightly golden brown | While crust is baking, beat softened cream cheese and powdered sugar together until smooth, then mix in vanilla extract | When crust is done baking, place it in the refrigerator for about 30 minutes to cool completely â€” this prevents the layers from melting | When the crust is cool to the touch, spread the cream cheese mixture evenly over the crust | Spoon lemon pie filling over the cream cheese layer and spread gently to the edges | Prepare Dream Whip according to package directions (whip with cold milk until peaks form) or use prepared whipped topping | Spread whipped topping over the lemon layer | Garnish with fresh lemon zest | Refrigerate for at least 2 hours before slicing and serving

ingredients: 2 large potatoes (peeled and finely diced), 1 medium onion (finely diced), 2 tbsp Worcestershire sauce, 2 tbsp fresh parsley (chopped), 2 tbsp milk (plus extra for brushing), 1 tsp salt, 1/2 tsp black pepper, 350g beef skirt steak or sirloin (finely diced), 2 sheets ready-rolled shortcrust pastry, beef gravy for serving
instructions: Add diced potato, diced onion, diced beef, Worcestershire sauce, and chopped parsley to a large bowl | Season generously with salt and pepper and mix everything well until thoroughly combined | Roll out pie crusts on a lightly floured surface | Cut into 12 rounds of about 4 inches diameter â€” a martini glass works perfectly as a template for cutting | Divide the filling evenly among 6 of the rounds, mounding it in the center | Cover each filled round with one of the remaining 6 rounds | Turn the edges of the bottom round up over the top round and crimp with your fingers or a fork to seal, making little sealed packages | Make 3 small slits in the top of each pasty with a sharp knife to allow steam to escape | Brush the tops lightly with milk for a golden finish | Place pasties on a baking sheet lined with parchment paper | Bake at 425Â°F (220Â°C) for about 30 minutes or until the pastry is lightly browned and crisp | Serve hot with beef gravy â€” adding a little extra chopped parsley to the gravy complements the filling beautifully

ingredients: 500g kielbasa or Polish sausage, 1 medium onion (diced), 1/2 cup ketchup, 1/3 cup brown sugar, 2 tbsp granulated sugar, 2 tbsp white vinegar, 2 tbsp molasses, 1 tbsp prepared yellow mustard, 2 cans (400g each) great northern beans (drained and rinsed), 1/2 tsp black pepper
instructions: Preheat oven to 350Â°F (175Â°C) | Cut kielbasa or Polish sausage in half lengthwise, then slice thinly into half-moons | In a saucepan, cook sliced sausage and diced onion in boiling water for 2 minutes, then drain well | In a large bowl, combine ketchup, brown sugar, granulated sugar, vinegar, molasses, and mustard â€” whisk until the sugars dissolve | Stir in the drained great northern beans and the sausage-onion mixture until everything is evenly coated | Transfer to a greased 2 1/2-quart baking dish and spread evenly | Cover dish with foil or a lid | Bake for 1 hour and 30 minutes or until the bean mixture reaches your desired thickness â€” the sauce should be rich and sticky | Check halfway through and stir gently | Alternatively, this can be cooked in a slow cooker on low for 6-8 hours | Serve hot as a hearty main dish or side

ingredients: 450g ground pork, 450g ground beef, 2/3 cup water, 1 large onion (finely diced), 3 cloves garlic (minced), 1 tsp salt, 1/2 tsp poultry seasoning, 1/2 tsp dried thyme, 1/2 tsp ground sage, 1/4 tsp ground mustard, 1/4 tsp ground cloves, 1 tbsp Worcestershire sauce, 1 tbsp soy sauce, 3 medium potatoes (peeled, boiled, and mashed), 2 double pie crusts (4 rounds total), 1 egg (beaten, for egg wash)
instructions: Preheat oven to 350Â°F (175Â°C) | In a large skillet over medium-high heat, brown ground pork and ground beef together, breaking apart with a spoon, until fully cooked â€” drain excess fat | Add water, diced onion, minced garlic, salt, poultry seasoning, thyme, sage, ground mustard, ground cloves, Worcestershire sauce, and soy sauce | Mix thoroughly with the browned meat, reduce heat, and simmer uncovered for 25 minutes, stirring occasionally, until most of the liquid has evaporated | While meat simmers, boil peeled potatoes in salted water until tender, then drain and mash until smooth with no lumps | Place two pie crusts into two pie pans as the bottom layers | Divide the meat mixture evenly between the two pie shells | Spread a layer of mashed potatoes evenly over the meat filling in each pie | Cover each pie with the remaining two crusts, crimping edges to seal | Cut a few small slits in the top crusts to vent steam | Beat the egg and brush generously over the top crusts of both pies for a glossy golden finish | Bake at 350Â°F (175Â°C) for 40 minutes until the crust is golden brown | Let pies rest for 10 minutes before slicing | Serve hot, traditionally enjoyed during the Christmas season

ingredients: 1 ripe peach (pitted and sliced), 1/2 cup peach yogurt, 1/2 cup vanilla ice cream, 1/4 cup fresh raspberries, 1/4 cup milk, 1 tsp honey (optional), fresh raspberries for garnish
instructions: Place peach slices, peach yogurt, vanilla ice cream, fresh raspberries, and milk in a blender | Add honey if you prefer extra sweetness | Process on high speed until completely smooth and no fruit chunks remain â€” about 30-45 seconds | Check consistency and add a splash more milk if the shake is too thick | Pour into a tall glass | Garnish with a few fresh raspberries on top | Serve immediately while cold and thick

recipe_name: Chicken Balsamico With Yukon Gold Potatoes
ingredients: 800g Yukon Gold potatoes (halved or quartered), 4 slices bacon (diced), 8 bone-in chicken thighs (skin-on), 1 1/2 tsp salt, 1/2 tsp fresh ground black pepper, 2 tbsp fresh rosemary (chopped), 4 cloves garlic (minced), 1/3 cup balsamic vinegar, 1 cup chicken broth
instructions: Place halved Yukon Gold potatoes in the insert of a 5 to 7-quart slow cooker | Cook diced bacon in a large skillet over medium heat until crisp, about 5-6 minutes | Remove bacon with a slotted spoon to paper towels to drain, leaving the bacon drippings in the pan | Sprinkle chicken thighs evenly on both sides with 1 1/2 teaspoons salt and 1/2 teaspoon pepper | Add seasoned chicken to the hot bacon drippings, skin-side down | Brown chicken on all sides until deep golden, about 12-15 minutes total â€” do this in batches if needed to avoid crowding | Add chopped rosemary and minced garlic to the skillet and sautÃ© for 1-2 minutes until fragrant | Deglaze the skillet by pouring in balsamic vinegar, scraping up all the browned bits from the bottom with a wooden spoon | Transfer the chicken and all pan contents to the slow cooker insert over the potatoes | Pour chicken broth into the slow cooker | Cover and cook on HIGH for 3 hours or on LOW for 5-6 hours until chicken is tender and potatoes are cooked through | Season with additional salt and pepper to taste | Sprinkle the reserved crispy bacon over the top of the chicken and potatoes just before serving

recipe_name: Quinoa Breakfast With Cranberries and Almonds
ingredients: 1 cup quinoa (rinsed), 2 cups water, 1/2 cup dried cranberries, 1/3 cup sliced almonds, 1/2 tsp ground cinnamon, 1 tbsp maple syrup (optional), pinch of salt, milk or yogurt for serving
instructions: Rinse quinoa thoroughly under cold water in a fine mesh strainer â€” this removes the natural bitter coating | Combine rinsed quinoa, water, dried cranberries, sliced almonds, and a pinch of salt in a medium saucepan | Bring to a boil over medium heat | Once boiling, reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 20 minutes until quinoa is tender and water is fully absorbed | Remove from heat | Stir in ground cinnamon and maple syrup if using | Cover again and let sit for 1 minute to allow the cinnamon flavor to bloom | Fluff with a fork and spoon into serving bowls | Serve hot with a splash of milk or a dollop of yogurt on top

ingredients: 4 medium yellow zucchini or summer squash, 2 tbsp canola oil, 1/4 cup unsweetened coconut flakes, 10 fresh curry leaves, 2 dried red chilies, 1 jalapeÃ±o (seeded and minced), 1 tsp mustard seeds, 1 tsp cumin seeds, 1/2 tsp turmeric, 1/2 tsp salt (adjust to taste), flatbread for serving
instructions: Cut zucchini lengthwise in half, then slice into 1/3-inch thick half-moons | Heat oil in a large pan or wok over moderate heat until shimmering | Add mustard seeds and cook for about 2 minutes until they begin to pop and splutter | Add coconut flakes, curry leaves, dried red chilies, minced jalapeÃ±o, cumin seeds, and turmeric to the pan â€” be careful, the curry leaves will pop and splutter when they hit the hot oil | Cook for about 2-4 minutes, stirring frequently, until the coconut begins to brown and becomes fragrant | Add sliced zucchini and mix thoroughly to coat with the spices | Turn the heat up to medium-high and cook, stirring occasionally, for about 8 minutes until zucchini is tender but still has a slight bite | Season with salt to taste and cook for one more minute | Serve hot with your choice of warm flatbread on the side

ingredients: 1 cup white rice, 2 cups low-sodium chicken broth, 1/4 cup fresh orange juice, 2 tbsp fresh lime juice, 2 tbsp olive oil, 4 tbsp fresh cilantro (chopped, divided), 4 cloves garlic (minced), 1 tsp sugar, 1 tsp salt, 1/2 tsp black pepper, 4 tilapia fillets (about 150g each), 1/2 cup salsa, 1 can (400g) black beans (drained and rinsed), 1 cup fresh pineapple (diced), 2 limes (thinly sliced)
instructions: Combine rice and chicken broth in a pot over medium heat and bring to a boil | Reduce heat to low, cover, and cook until rice is tender and has absorbed all the liquid, about 20 minutes | Preheat oven to 400Â°F (200Â°C) | In a mixing bowl, whisk together orange juice, lime juice, olive oil, 2 tablespoons of the chopped cilantro, minced garlic, and sugar | Season with salt and pepper | Add tilapia fillets to the marinade, turning to coat both sides | Marinate in the refrigerator for 20 minutes, turning occasionally | Stir together the cooked rice, salsa, drained black beans, diced pineapple, and remaining 2 tablespoons of chopped cilantro in a 2 or 3-quart baking dish | Remove tilapia from the marinade, reserving the marinade | Lay the fish fillets over the rice mixture, overlapping slightly if necessary | Pour the reserved marinade over the fish | Shingle thin lime slices over the top of the fish | Bake for 25 to 30 minutes until the fish flakes easily with a fork, is opaque throughout, and cooked through | Garnish with additional chopped cilantro before serving

ingredients: 1 block (400g) extra firm tofu (pressed and cubed), 3 tbsp sesame oil (divided), 1 medium onion (thinly sliced), 4 cloves garlic (minced), 1/3 cup honey, 3 tbsp soy sauce, 2 tbsp rice vinegar, 1/2 tsp ginger powder, 1/4 tsp cayenne pepper, 1/2 tsp sea salt, 1/3 cup water, 1 tbsp cornstarch or arrowroot powder, 1 tbsp sesame seeds, mixed stir-fry vegetables (broccoli, bell pepper, snap peas)
instructions: Press tofu for 20 minutes by wrapping in paper towels and placing a weight on top, then cut into 1-inch cubes | Make the honey garlic sauce: heat 1 tbsp sesame oil in a small pan over medium heat | SautÃ© sliced onion until translucent, about 3-4 minutes | Add minced garlic and continue cooking for 1 minute until fragrant | Add honey, stirring gently as it melts | Whisk in soy sauce, rice vinegar, ginger powder, cayenne, and sea salt | Add water and bring to a simmer | Taste and adjust seasoning, adding more honey or salt as desired | Whisk in cornstarch or arrowroot, stirring continuously, adding more as needed until the sauce thickens to a saucy consistency â€” it should coat the back of a spoon | Remove sauce from heat and set aside | Heat remaining 2 tbsp sesame oil in a large sautÃ© pan or wok over high heat | SautÃ© tofu cubes until golden and crispy on all sides, about 5-6 minutes | Add in mixed vegetables one at a time, heartiest ones first (broccoli, then bell pepper, then snap peas), stirring as you go until all vegetables are cooked but still crisp â€” this should take about 5 minutes total | Remove pan from heat | Pour the hot honey garlic sauce over the tofu and vegetables, tossing to coat evenly | Garnish with sesame seeds and serve immediately over steamed rice or noodles

ingredients: 4 ripe tomatoes, 2 green bell peppers (diced), 2 red bell peppers (diced), 2 medium eggplants (cubed), 2 medium zucchini (cubed), 4 cloves garlic (minced), 400g fresh tuna steaks (cut into 1-inch cubes), 5 tbsp olive oil (divided), 4 sprigs fresh thyme, 1 tsp dried oregano, 1 small hot chili pepper (minced), 1/2 tsp salt, 1/2 cup water if needed
instructions: Clean all the vegetables thoroughly | Bring a pot of water to a boil and briefly slip the tomatoes in boiling water for 30 seconds to loosen their peels, then remove and peel off the skins | Deseed the tomatoes and cut into chunks | Cut bell peppers, eggplants, and zucchini into uniform bite-sized pieces | Cut fresh tuna into 1-inch cubes and set aside | In a Dutch oven or heavy pot, heat 1 tablespoon olive oil over medium heat | Add bell peppers and cook over low heat for 10 minutes, stirring occasionally, until they begin to soften | Add cubed eggplant with 2 more tablespoons olive oil and continue cooking for another 10 minutes, stirring occasionally | Add cubed zucchini along with fresh thyme sprigs and dried oregano, plus the remaining olive oil | Let this simmer uncovered for 10 minutes, stirring occasionally | Add the peeled tomato chunks, minced hot chili pepper, minced garlic, and cubed tuna | Gently fold everything together with a long wooden spoon, being careful not to break up the tuna too much | Cover and cook over very low heat for 20 minutes, stirring very gently once or twice | If the mixture becomes too dry, add up to 1/2 cup of water as needed | Remove thyme sprigs before serving | This dish is delicious served hot, warm, or even cold â€” traditionally enjoyed at any temperature

recipe_name: California Walnut Breakfast and Snack Cookies
ingredients: 1/2 cup unsalted butter (softened), 3/4 cup brown sugar (packed), 1 tsp vanilla extract, 1/2 tsp maple extract, 1 can (230g) crushed pineapple (with juice), 1 1/2 cups all-purpose flour, 1/4 cup skim milk powder, 1/2 tsp baking soda, 1 tsp ground cinnamon, 1/4 tsp salt, 1 1/2 cups quick-cooking oatmeal, 1/2 cup raisins, 1/2 cup chopped dates, 1 cup California walnuts (chopped)
instructions: Preheat oven to 350Â°F (180Â°C) and lightly grease a baking sheet | In a large mixing bowl, use an electric mixer to cream together softened butter and brown sugar until light and fluffy, about 2-3 minutes | Beat in maple extract and vanilla extract until fully incorporated | Stir in crushed pineapple along with its juice until combined | In a separate bowl, mix together flour, skim milk powder, baking soda, cinnamon, and salt until well combined | Stir the dry ingredients into the pineapple mixture, mixing just until incorporated â€” do not overmix | Stir in oatmeal, raisins, chopped dates, and chopped walnuts until evenly distributed throughout the dough | Drop rounded spoonfuls of dough onto the greased baking sheet, spacing them about 2 inches apart | Bake for 12 to 15 minutes or until the cookies are golden brown around the edges | Remove from oven and let cookies cool on the baking sheet for 5 minutes before transferring to a wire rack to cool completely | Store in an airtight container for up to 1 week

ingredients: 2 cups rye flour, 1 cup white bread flour (plus extra for dusting), 2 tsp salt, 25g fresh yeast cake (or 2 1/4 tsp active dry yeast), 1 tbsp honey, 500ml warm water (divided into 100ml and 400ml)
instructions: Mix rye flour, white flour, and salt together in a large mixing bowl and set aside | In a separate small bowl, dissolve honey and fresh yeast in 100ml of warm water (about 85-95Â°F) | Let the yeast mixture stand for 10 minutes until it becomes frothy and activated | Add yeast mixture to the flour mixture | Gradually add the remaining 400ml of warm water, little by little, mixing continuously until a dough forms | Turn dough out onto a lightly floured surface and knead for 8-10 minutes until the dough is smooth, elastic, and pliable | Cover the dough with a clean kitchen towel and let it rise in a warm place for 30 minutes | Punch down the dough and knead once more, then cover again and let rise for another 40 minutes | Shape the dough into an oblong loaf and place on a baking sheet lined with parchment paper | Cover loosely and let rest while the oven preheats to 250Â°C (480Â°F) | Just before baking, pat the surface of the bread with water using your hands â€” this creates a crisp crust | Place in the oven on the second-lowest shelf | Bake for 10 minutes at 250Â°C, then lower the temperature to 190Â°C (375Â°F) and continue baking for approximately 45 minutes | The bread is done when it sounds hollow when tapped on the bottom | Transfer to a wire rack and let cool completely before slicing

ingredients: 2 tbsp peanut oil, 4 cloves garlic (minced), 3 green onions (sliced), 3 cups cooked brown rice (preferably day-old), 300g cooked shrimp (peeled and deveined), 1 can (200g) water chestnuts (drained and chopped), 1/4 cup vegetable broth or water, 2 tbsp soy sauce, 1 tsp sesame oil, 1/4 cup sliced almonds (toasted)
instructions: Heat peanut oil in a large nonstick pan or wok over medium-high heat | Add minced garlic and sliced green onions, sautÃ©ing until soft and fragrant, about 3 minutes | Add cooked brown rice, cooked shrimp, and chopped water chestnuts to the pan | SautÃ© for another 1 minute, tossing to combine with the garlic and onions | Pour in vegetable broth (or water), soy sauce, and sesame oil | Stir everything together to combine evenly | Cover the pan with a lid and cook until all ingredients are heated through, about 3 to 5 minutes | Remove lid and give it a final toss | Sprinkle toasted sliced almonds over the top | Serve immediately while hot

ingredients: 3 plum tomatoes (diced), 1 English cucumber (diced), 2 small cucumbers (diced), 1/2 red onion (thinly sliced), 1 yellow bell pepper (diced), 1/2 cup Kalamata olives (pitted and halved), 2 cups fresh arugula, 1/4 cup flat-leaf parsley (chopped), 100g soft goat cheese or herb-flavored cream cheese log (crumbled), 1/2 tsp fresh ground black pepper, 3 tbsp light salad dressing or vinaigrette, crusty bread for serving
instructions: Rinse and prepare all vegetables â€” dice tomatoes and cucumbers, thinly slice red onion, dice bell pepper, halve olives, and roughly chop parsley | Place arugula in a large plastic mixing bowl as the base | Add diced tomatoes, cucumbers, red onion, bell pepper, and Kalamata olives | Season with fresh ground black pepper | Pour salad dressing over the ingredients and toss gently to coat everything lightly â€” use just enough to moisten, not drown, the salad | Crumble the soft goat cheese or cream cheese log over the top â€” it will be very soft and will blend into the flavor mix when you toss | Carefully transfer the dressed salad into a pretty serving bowl, being gentle with the ingredients | This makes 4 generous side servings with dinner or 2-3 lunch servings with fresh, crusty continental-style bread on the side | Serve immediately at room temperature

ingredients: 1 cup quinoa (rinsed thoroughly), 2 1/2 cups water, 1/2 tsp salt, 1/3 cup fresh lemon juice, 3 tbsp olive oil (divided), 1 English cucumber (diced), 1/2 red onion (finely diced), 1 cup fresh parsley (chopped), 1/4 cup fresh mint (chopped), 1/2 cup crumbled feta cheese, 1/4 cup Kalamata olives (halved), salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Rinse quinoa thoroughly in a fine mesh strainer under cold water â€” this removes the natural bitter coating | Drain and place quinoa in a heavy dry pan | Heat over medium heat, stirring constantly, until the grains separate and begin to toast and turn lightly golden, about 3-4 minutes | Add water and 1/2 tsp salt, bring to a boil while stirring | Reduce heat to low, cover, and cook for 15 minutes or until all the liquid is absorbed | Transfer cooked quinoa to a large bowl and set aside to cool to room temperature | In a small bowl, whisk together fresh lemon juice and 1 tablespoon of olive oil to make the dressing â€” set aside | Place the remaining 2 tablespoons olive oil, diced cucumber, diced red onion, chopped parsley, and chopped mint in a separate larger bowl | Add the cooled quinoa and the lemon-oil dressing | Toss everything together gently but thoroughly to combine | Sprinkle crumbled feta cheese and halved Kalamata olives over the top | Season to taste with additional salt and fresh ground black pepper | Serve at room temperature or chilled, as a side dish or light meal

ingredients: 2 tbsp butter, 1 medium onion (diced), 3 cloves garlic (minced), 2 celery stalks (diced), 500g white meat chicken (cubed), 1 can (400g) cream of mushroom soup, 1 can (400g) cream of chicken soup, 1/2 tsp salt, 1/4 tsp black pepper, 1/2 cup sour cream, chow mein noodles or egg noodles for serving, fresh parsley for garnish
instructions: Melt butter in a large skillet over medium heat | SautÃ© diced onion, minced garlic, and diced celery in the butter until soft and transparent, about 5-6 minutes | Add cubed chicken to the pan and reduce heat to low | Simmer for 5 minutes, stirring constantly, until chicken is cooked through and no longer pink on the outside | Stir in cream of mushroom soup and cream of chicken soup until fully combined with the chicken mixture | Cook for an additional 5 minutes, stirring occasionally, until heated through and bubbling gently | Season with salt and black pepper to taste | Serve hot over a bed of crispy chow mein noodles or buttered egg noodles | Top each serving with a generous dollop of sour cream and garnish with fresh chopped parsley

ingredients: 2 cups cooked chicken (shredded), 1 can (400g) cream of chicken soup, 1/2 tsp black pepper, 2 cups cheddar cheese (shredded, divided), 8 large flour tortillas, salsa for serving, sour cream for serving
instructions: Preheat oven to 425Â°F (220Â°C) | In a bowl, mix cream of chicken soup, black pepper, 1/2 cup of the shredded cheese, and shredded chicken until well combined | Lay tortillas flat on a clean work surface | Spread about 1/4 cup of the chicken mixture onto one half of each tortilla, spreading to within 1/2 inch of the edge | Moisten the edges of the tortilla with a little water using your fingertip â€” this helps seal the quesadilla | Fold the empty half over the filled half, pressing edges gently to seal | Place folded quesadillas on 2 baking sheets, spacing them slightly apart | Bake for 10 minutes or until hot and starting to crisp | Remove from oven and sprinkle remaining cheese over the tops | Serve immediately with salsa and sour cream on the side | Makes 8 quesadillas

ingredients: For crust: 1 cup unsalted cashews, 1/3 cup light brown sugar, 1 cup all-purpose flour, 1/4 tsp salt, 1/2 cup unsalted butter (cold, cubed), 1 large egg, 2 tbsp candied ginger (finely chopped), ice water as needed. For filling: 3 ripe guavas, 3 packages (250g each) cream cheese (softened), 1 cup granulated sugar, 1 vanilla bean (seeds scraped), 3 large eggs, 1 cup mascarpone cheese. For glaze: 1/2 cup guava jelly, 2 tbsp water
instructions: Make the crust: pulse cashews and brown sugar in a food processor until finely ground | Add flour and salt, pulse to blend | Pulse in cold cubed butter until the largest pieces are ingredients: 2 tbsp olive oil, 1 whole head garlic (cloves separated and peeled, plus extra for roasting), 1 large leek (white and light green parts, sliced), 2 medium potatoes (peeled and diced), 4 cups chicken or vegetable stock, 1/2 tsp salt, 1/4 tsp white pepper, 2 tbsp fresh chives (chopped), crusty bread for serving

ingredients: 8 oz cream cheese (softened), 1 cup fresh strawberries (hulled and chopped), 1/4 cup granulated sugar, 1/4 cup sour cream, 1 tsp pure vanilla extract, 1 tbsp strawberry liqueur (optional), graham crackers, vanilla wafers, or fresh fruit for dipping

ingredients: 1 medium onion (thinly sliced), 200g mushrooms (sliced), 2 cups cheddar cheese (shredded), 4 large flour tortillas, 2 tbsp butter (for frying), 1 tbsp vegetable oil, salt and pepper to taste, sour cream and salsa for serving

ingredients: 6 large eggs, 1 1/2 cups granulated sugar, 2 tbsp instant coffee powder, 2 tbsp unsweetened cocoa powder, 1 can (354ml) evaporated milk, 1 tbsp vanilla extract, 1 cup chopped almonds (toasted), whole milk (enough to fill 1-gallon freezer)

ingredients: 1 cup blue cheese (crumbled, divided), 1/2 cup sour cream, 4 oz cream cheese (softened), 2 green onions (finely chopped), 1 tsp lemon zest, 1 tbsp fresh lemon juice, 1/4 tsp garlic powder, 1 small garlic clove (minced), salt and pepper to taste, fresh vegetables or chips for serving

ingredients: 1/4 cup coconut oil, 1/4 cup unsalted butter, 1/2 cup unsweetened cocoa powder, 1/4 cup honey, 1/4 cup maple syrup, 1/2 tsp liquid stevia (optional), 2 large eggs, 1 tsp vanilla extract, 2 tbsp ground flax seeds, 1/2 cup all-purpose flour, 1/4 tsp salt, 1/2 cup chocolate chips

ingredients: 4 slices bacon (diced), 1 medium onion (diced), 1/2 cup ketchup, 1/4 cup brown sugar, 1 tbsp Worcestershire sauce, 2 cans (400g each) cut green beans (drained), salt and pepper to taste

ingredients: 2 cups plain flour, 2 tbsp ghee (plus extra for cooking), 1/2 tsp salt, 2/3 cup warm water, cooking oil for handling, curry or dhal for serving

ingredients: 2 cups all-purpose flour, 3/4 cup granulated sugar, 1 1/2 tsp baking powder, 1/2 tsp salt, 1/2 tsp baking soda, 1/4 cup margarine or butter (cold), 1 large egg, 3/4 cup orange juice, 1 tbsp orange zest, 1 cup fresh or frozen cranberries (roughly chopped), 1/2 cup chopped walnuts or pecans, 1/2 cup chocolate chips (optional)

ingredients: 6 bone-in chicken thighs (skin-on), 1 medium onion (diced), 4 cloves garlic (minced), 2 tbsp margarine or butter, 300g frozen chopped spinach, 1/2 tsp salt, 1 tsp dried basil leaves, 400g spaghetti, 2 cups tomato pasta sauce, 1/4 cup Parmesan cheese (grated)

ingredients: 500g ground beef, 3 tbsp buffalo wing sauce, 1/4 cup breadcrumbs, 1/2 tsp garlic powder, 1/2 tsp onion powder, 2 tbsp butter (melted), 4 hamburger buns, 4 slices blue cheese, 4 lettuce leaves, extra buffalo sauce for drizzling

ingredients: 4 boneless skinless chicken breasts (cut into chunks), 2 red bell peppers (diced), 1 large onion (diced), 3 cloves garlic (minced), 1 can (400g) unsweetened pineapple chunks (with juice), 2 tbsp curry powder, 1/3 cup sweet chili sauce, 2 tbsp soy sauce, 1 tbsp rice vinegar, salt and pepper to taste, steamed rice for serving

ingredients: For dry rub: 1/4 cup brown sugar, 1 tbsp dry mustard, 1 tsp cayenne pepper, 1 tbsp paprika, 1 tbsp garlic powder, 1 tbsp onion powder, 1 tbsp salt, 1 tsp fresh ground black pepper. For sauce: 1 tbsp vegetable oil, 1 small onion (diced), 1 cup ketchup, 1/3 cup water, 2 tbsp tomato paste, 1/4 cup brown sugar, 1/4 cup apple cider vinegar, 2 tbsp molasses, 1/2 tsp cayenne pepper, salt and black pepper to taste. 2 racks pork spare ribs
instructions: Prepare the dry rub: remove the thin white membrane from the bone-side of the ribs by loosening a corner with a knife and pulling it off with a paper towel for better grip | In a small bowl, mix together brown sugar, dry mustard, cayenne, paprika, garlic powder, onion powder, salt, and pepper | Massage the dry rub thoroughly into both sides of the ribs | Let ribs sit for at least 1 hour at room temperature or overnight in the refrigerator | Make the Kansas City barbecue sauce: heat vegetable oil in a small saucepan over medium-high heat | Add diced onion and cook until translucent, about 3-4 minutes | In a bowl, combine ketchup, water, tomato paste, brown sugar, apple cider vinegar, molasses, cayenne, salt, and pepper | Add mixture to the saucepan with the onions, stir, and let simmer for 30 to 45 minutes until thickened and flavors meld, stirring occasionally â€” makes about 3 cups of sauce | For grilling: place ribs meat-side down next to medium-hot coals at about 225Â°F using indirect heat | Cook for 1 hour, then turn ribs every half hour, basting with sauce each time | Cook until ribs are tender, about 3 to 4 hours total | For oven cooking: preheat oven to 350Â°F (175Â°C) | Place ribs on a rack in a roasting pan, slather with sauce, and tent with aluminum foil | Bake, basting with sauce every 30 minutes and removing the foil for the final 30 minutes | Cook until fork-tender, about 2 1/2 to 3 hours | Let ribs rest for 10 minutes before slicing between the bones | Serve with remaining sauce on the side

ingredients: 3 tbsp butter, 3 tbsp all-purpose flour, 2 cups whole milk, 1/2 cup Parmesan cheese (grated), 1/2 cup American cheese (shredded), 1/2 cup Colby cheese (shredded), 2 egg yolks, 1/4 tsp hot sauce, 4 thick slices bread (toasted), 200g sliced cooked chicken or turkey, 200g sliced ham, 2 medium tomatoes (sliced), 8 slices bacon (cooked crisp), 1/2 tsp paprika
instructions: Preheat oven to 400Â°F (200Â°C) | In a heavy 4-quart saucepan, melt butter over medium heat | Whisk in flour and cook until smooth and bubbling, about 1 minute | Slowly add milk, whisking constantly, and continue cooking until thickened and smooth, about 3-4 minutes | Add hot sauce and grated Parmesan cheese, then remove from heat | Place 1/2 cup of the sauce in a small bowl and set the remaining sauce aside | Whisk egg yolks into the 1/2 cup of reserved sauce, mixing well | Stir the egg mixture back into the main saucepan of sauce and return to heat, stirring constantly (do not let it boil or the eggs may curdle) | Add shredded Colby and American cheeses, stirring until fully melted and smooth | Remove from heat | Place toasted bread slices on individual heat-resistant plates or in oven-safe dishes | Cover each slice of bread with slices of chicken or turkey and ham | Pour a generous amount of cheese sauce over each serving, covering completely | Top each with a tomato slice and two pieces of crispy bacon | Sprinkle paprika over the top | Bake for 10 to 15 minutes until bubbly and lightly browned on top | Serve immediately while hot

ingredients: 3 cups water (for infusing), 1/4 cup fresh ginger (peeled and thinly sliced), 1/3 cup honey or pure maple syrup, 2 tbsp molasses, 1/4 cup fresh lemon juice, 2 tbsp apple cider vinegar, 6 cups cold water, fresh berries, mint sprigs, and lemon slices for garnish, ice cubes for serving
instructions: Combine 3 cups water with sliced fresh ginger in a small saucepan | Bring to a boil over medium-high heat and boil for 2 minutes | Remove from heat, cover, and let the ginger infuse for 15 minutes | Strain the ginger-infused water through a fine mesh sieve into a large pitcher, pressing on the ginger solids to extract all the liquid | Add honey or maple syrup and molasses to the warm liquid, stirring until completely dissolved | Stir in fresh lemon juice, apple cider vinegar, and the remaining 6 cups of cold water | Chill until very cold, at least 2 hours or overnight | Stir the switchel well and serve in tall glasses over ice cubes | Garnish with fresh berries, mint sprigs, or lemon slices if desired | Can be covered and refrigerated for up to 2 days

ingredients: 1/2 cup brown sugar (packed), 1/4 cup unsalted butter, 2 tbsp corn syrup, 1 large apple (peeled and finely chopped), 1 can refrigerated biscuits (8 count), 1/4 cup granulated sugar mixed with 1 tsp ground cinnamon
instructions: Preheat oven to 375Â°F (190Â°C) | In a deep dish baker or oven-safe skillet, melt butter, brown sugar, and corn syrup together over medium heat, stirring until smooth and bubbly | Remove from heat and sprinkle the finely chopped apple evenly over the caramel mixture in the bottom of the dish | Separate the biscuits and coat each one generously in the cinnamon-sugar mixture, pressing gently to adhere | Arrange the coated biscuits on top of the apples in a single layer, with biscuits touching slightly | Bake for 18 to 20 minutes until the biscuits are golden brown and the caramel is bubbling around the edges | Remove from oven and let cool for 2-3 minutes | Carefully invert the dish onto a serving plate so the caramel apple topping is on top | Serve warm

ingredients: 300g cooked baby shrimp, 1 cup green seedless grapes (halved), 2 celery stalks (diced), 1/2 cup sliced almonds (toasted), 1 can (200g) water chestnuts (drained and chopped), 1 can (200g) lychees (drained and halved), 1 cup fresh pineapple (diced), 4 large lettuce leaves. For dressing: 1/3 cup mayonnaise, 1 tbsp honey, 1 tbsp reduced-sodium soy sauce, 1 tsp mild curry powder, 2 tbsp fresh lime juice
instructions: In a large bowl, mix together cooked shrimp, halved grapes, diced celery, toasted almonds, chopped water chestnuts, and halved lychees | Gently stir in diced fresh pineapple, being careful not to break up the fruit | In a separate small bowl, whisk together mayonnaise, honey, soy sauce, curry powder, and fresh lime juice until smooth and well combined | Pour the dressing over the salad and toss gently to coat all ingredients evenly | Set out 4 serving plates and line each with a clean crisp lettuce leaf | Portion the salad into neat mounds on top of the lettuce leaves | Drizzle any remaining dressing from the bowl over each serving | Serve immediately with extra dressing on the side

ingredients: 2 tbsp reduced-sodium soy sauce, 2 tbsp cold water, 1 tbsp cornstarch, 1 tsp sambal oelek (chili paste), 400g boneless pork loin chops (cut into thin strips), 1 tsp vegetable oil, 1 green onion (sliced), 3 cloves garlic (minced), 1 carrot (julienned), 100g fresh mushrooms (sliced), 1 tbsp fresh ginger (grated), 1 can (300g) mandarin oranges in light syrup (drained), 2 packs ramen noodles, 2 tsp sesame oil, 1 tbsp toasted sesame seeds
instructions: In a small bowl, whisk together soy sauce, cold water, cornstarch, and sambal oelek until smooth; set aside | Coat a cool nonstick wok with cooking spray and preheat over high heat | Add 1 teaspoon vegetable oil | When oil is hot, add pork strips and stir-fry for 3-4 minutes until browned and cooked through, stirring constantly | Remove pork from wok and set aside | Add sliced green onion, minced garlic, and julienned carrot to the wok and cook for 2-3 minutes until vegetables are crisp-tender, stirring constantly | Add sliced mushrooms and cook an additional 2-3 minutes, stirring constantly | Return the cooked pork back to the wok | Stir the soy sauce mixture well and pour it over the ingredients in the wok | Add grated ginger and stir constantly for 1 minute until the sauce thickens and bubbles | Add drained mandarin oranges and toss gently to coat without breaking them | Cook ramen noodles according to package directions, drain, and toss with sesame oil | Serve the stir-fry over the sesame noodles and garnish with toasted sesame seeds

ingredients: 4 boneless skinless chicken breasts, 2 cans (400g each) cream of chicken soup, 1 cup sour cream, 2 tbsp poppy seeds, 2 sleeves Ritz crackers (crushed), 1/2 cup unsalted butter (melted), salt and pepper to taste
instructions: Preheat oven to 350Â°F (175Â°C) | Place chicken breasts in a pan and cover with water | Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer until tender and no longer pink, about 10 minutes | Once cool enough to handle, cut chicken into bite-size pieces | In a 13x9-inch rectangular pan, mix the two cans of cream of chicken soup with sour cream until smooth and well combined | Sprinkle the cut chicken evenly over the soup mixture | Place Ritz crackers in a large plastic bag and gently crush them with a rolling pin until coarse crumbs form | Add poppy seeds to the bag and shake to combine | Pour melted butter into the bag and shake again until the crumbs are evenly coated | Sprinkle the buttery cracker mixture evenly over the chicken and soup layer | Bake for 30-40 minutes until the casserole begins to bubble around the edges and the crackers are golden brown | Let rest for 5 minutes before serving

ingredients: 1 large head green cabbage, 500g ground beef, 1 large egg, 1/4 cup fresh parsley (chopped), 1 medium onion (finely diced), 3 cloves garlic (minced), 1 cup cooked white rice, 1 tsp salt, 1/2 tsp black pepper, 2 cans (400g each) tomato soup, 2 tbsp sugar, 2 tbsp white vinegar, 1/2 cup water
instructions: Bring a large pot of water to a boil | Carefully place the whole head of cabbage in the boiling water and boil for 10-15 minutes until outer leaves are softened | Remove cabbage and let cool slightly, then carefully peel off the leaves one at a time, keeping them intact | In a large bowl, mix ground beef, egg, chopped parsley, diced onion, minced garlic, cooked rice, salt, and pepper until well combined | Take a portion of the meat mixture and form it into an oval-shaped ball | Place each meatball near the base of a cabbage leaf, fold the sides inward, and roll up tightly | Line the bottom of a 5-quart Dutch oven with any torn or extra cabbage leaves to prevent sticking | Arrange the cabbage rolls seam-side down in the pot in snug layers | In a separate bowl, mix together tomato soup, sugar, vinegar, and water until smooth | Pour the tomato mixture over the cabbage rolls, covering them completely | Cover the pot and cook over medium heat for 1 hour and 30 minutes, checking occasionally to ensure the liquid is simmering gently | Serve hot with a spoonful of the tomato sauce from the pot

ingredients: 1 tbsp sesame oil, 2 tbsp fresh ginger (grated), 1 red chili (finely chopped), 3 tbsp soy sauce, 3 tbsp honey, 2 tbsp dry sherry, 2 boneless pork fillets (about 300g each, halved), steamed white rice and green vegetables for serving
instructions: Place sesame oil, grated ginger, and chopped chili in a frying pan over high heat and cook for 1 minute until fragrant | Add soy sauce, honey, and dry sherry, stirring to combine, and cook for 2 minutes until the sauce is bubbling and slightly thickened | Cut each pork fillet in half crosswise to create 4 portions | Add the pork pieces to the pan, turning to coat them in the sauce | Reduce heat to medium and cook the pork in the pan sauce for 10-15 minutes, turning occasionally, until cooked to your liking and the sauce is thick and caramelized | If the sauce reduces too quickly, add a splash of water | Remove pork from the pan and let rest for 2-3 minutes before slicing | Slice the pork and arrange on serving plates | Spoon the remaining caramelized pan sauce over the top | Serve with plain steamed white rice and stir-fried or steamed green vegetables

ingredients: 3 cups all-purpose flour, 2 cups granulated sugar, 1 tsp baking soda, 1/2 tsp salt, 1 package unsweetened drink powder (such as Kool-Aid, for flavored cake), 1 cup vegetable shortening. For baking: 1 package cake mix (about 1/3 cup), 4 tsp water, 1/4 tsp vanilla extract (for white cake)
instructions: In a medium bowl, combine flour, sugar, baking soda, salt, and drink powder (if making flavored cake) | Stir with a wire whisk until thoroughly blended | Using a pastry blender or two knives, cut in vegetable shortening until evenly distributed and the mixture resembles coarse cornmeal | Spoon about 1/3 cup of the mix into each of 10 small containers or Ziploc bags | Seal containers tightly and label with date and contents | Store in a cool, dry place and use within 12 weeks | Makes 10 individual packages of cake mix | To use one package: if using a child's play oven, follow manufacturer's directions, or preheat a standard oven to 375Â°F (190Â°C) | Grease and flour a 4-inch miniature cake pan | In a small bowl, combine 1 package cake mix and 4 teaspoons water (add a drop of vanilla for white cake) | Stir with a fork or spoon until blended and smooth | Pour mixture into the prepared pan | Bake for 12 to 13 minutes in a standard oven or as directed for a play oven | Remove from oven and cool in pan on a wire rack for 5 minutes | Invert cake onto a small plate and remove the pan | Cool completely before frosting if desired | Serves 2 children

ingredients: 4 salmon steaks or fillets (about 150g each), 1 tsp garlic powder, 1/2 tsp salt, 1/4 tsp black pepper, 2 tbsp extra virgin olive oil, 3 tbsp fresh lime juice, 1/4 cup fresh cilantro (chopped), 1 tsp sugar or sugar substitute, lime wedges for serving
instructions: Sprinkle garlic powder, salt, and black pepper evenly over the top of each salmon steak or fillet | In a small bowl, whisk together olive oil, fresh lime juice, chopped cilantro, and sugar (or sugar substitute) until well combined | Place salmon in a nonstick skillet over medium-high heat, seasoned side down | Cook for 4-5 minutes until the bottom is golden and the salmon is about halfway cooked through | Turn the salmon over and pour the cilantro-lime mixture evenly over the top | Continue cooking for another 4-5 minutes until the salmon is cooked through and flakes easily with a fork | Spoon any pan sauce over the salmon before serving | Serve immediately with lime wedges on the side

ingredients: 400g spaghetti, 4 ripe tomatoes (chopped), 2 cups fresh arugula (roughly chopped), 1/4 cup fresh basil (torn), 1 tsp dried oregano, 1/4 cup Kalamata olives (pitted and sliced), 3 tbsp olive oil, 1 tbsp red wine vinegar, salt and black pepper to taste, Parmesan cheese for serving, crusty Italian bread for serving
instructions: Bring a large pan of generously salted water to a boil | Add spaghetti and cook until al dente, approximately 10 minutes | While pasta cooks, prepare the sauce: chop tomatoes into bite-size chunks, roughly chop fresh arugula, tear basil leaves, and slice olives â€” whatever size and shape you prefer | Place chopped tomatoes, arugula, basil, and olives in individual serving bowls | Add olive oil, red wine vinegar, salt, and black pepper to each bowl | Taste and adjust seasoning until the balance is right | The pasta should be ready by now â€” drain the spaghetti quickly, reserving a splash of pasta water | Immediately add the hot drained spaghetti to the serving bowls over the fresh ingredients | Stir everything together thoroughly â€” the heat from the pasta will slightly wilt the arugula and release the tomato and herb flavors | Serve immediately with freshly grated Parmesan cheese and warm crusty Italian bread on the side | Any type of pasta can be used, though spaghetti works beautifully

ingredients: For crust: 1/2 cup unsalted butter (softened), 1/4 cup granulated sugar, 1 tbsp honey, 1/4 tsp salt, 2 large egg yolks, 1 1/4 cups all-purpose flour. For filling: 1 can (400g) sweetened condensed milk, 1/2 cup sour cream, 1/2 cup key lime juice, 1 tbsp lime zest, 3 large egg yolks, 1 tbsp honey. For topping: whipped cream, tuile cookies (optional)
instructions: Make the short dough crust: cream butter with sugar, honey, and salt until uniform | Add egg yolks one at a time until completely mixed | Add flour and mix just until incorporated â€” do not overmix | Roll out the dough on a lightly floured surface, then cover and chill for 3-4 hours until very firm and easy to handle | Preheat oven to 350Â°F (175Â°C) | Press chilled dough into a 9-inch pie pan and trim edges | Bake the crust for 15 minutes until lightly golden | Make the filling: in a bowl, gently fold together sweetened condensed milk, sour cream, key lime juice, lime zest, egg yolks, and honey until smooth and well combined â€” do not overbeat | Pour filling into the pre-baked crust | Bake for about 8 minutes until the filling is just set but still slightly wobbly in the center | Remove from oven and let cool completely, then refrigerate for at least 2 hours until fully set | Top with whipped cream and tuile cookies for decoration if desired | Slice and serve chilled

ingredients: 500g boneless skinless chicken breasts (diced into cubes), juice of 1/2 lemon, 2 tbsp vegetable oil, 4 cloves garlic (minced), 1 serrano pepper (minced), 1 medium onion (diced), 2 tbsp curry powder, 1 tbsp Thai red curry paste, salt and pepper to taste, fresh cilantro for garnish, steamed rice for serving
instructions: Butterfly the chicken breasts first to make them thinner, then cut into bite-size cubes | Rinse chicken under cold water and drain well | Squeeze the juice of half a lemon over the chicken and set aside | In a sautÃ© pan over medium heat, warm vegetable oil | SautÃ© minced garlic, minced serrano pepper, and diced onion for about 2 minutes or until softened and fragrant | Add curry powder to the pan and cook for 2 more minutes, stirring constantly to bloom the spices | Add Thai red curry paste and stir in well, cooking for a few more minutes until the paste is evenly distributed | Add the diced chicken along with the lemon juice to the curry mixture | Stir until chicken is completely coated with the curry | SautÃ© for 10-12 minutes, stirring occasionally, until chicken is fully cooked through | Season with salt and pepper to taste | Serve hot over steamed rice and garnish generously with fresh cilantro

ingredients: 2 beef steaks (filet mignon or ribeye, about 200g each), salt and black pepper, 8 jumbo shrimp (peeled and deveined, tails on), 200g lump crabmeat (checked for shells), 3 tbsp butter, 3 cloves garlic (minced), 2 tbsp fresh lemon juice, 1/3 cup dry white wine. For bearnaise sauce: 2 egg yolks, 1 tbsp lemon juice, 1/2 cup melted butter, 1 tbsp fresh tarragon, salt
instructions: Season steaks generously with salt and pepper on both sides | Allow steaks to sit at room temperature for at least 30 minutes before cooking | Prepare bearnaise sauce: whisk egg yolks and lemon juice in a double boiler until thick, then slowly drizzle in melted butter while whisking constantly until emulsified | Stir in fresh tarragon and season with salt, then set aside and keep warm | Ensure shrimp are peeled and deveined with tails left on | Check crabmeat carefully for any bits of shell | Grill or broil steaks to just under desired doneness, allowing for warming time while preparing the topping | In a sautÃ© pan, heat butter and minced garlic over medium-high heat | Add prepared shrimp and lemon juice, sautÃ© for 2 minutes | Add white wine and crabmeat, sautÃ© until wine has reduced and shrimp are no longer pink, about 2-3 more minutes | Spread about 1/4 cup bearnaise sauce on each serving plate | Place steaks on the sauce and top generously with the shrimp and crab mixture | Double the ingredients for 4 servings | Serve immediately

ingredients: 1 medium onion (diced), 1 Granny Smith apple (peeled and diced), 2 cups cooked ham (diced), 1 tsp dry mustard, 2 cans (400g each) baked beans, 1/4 cup chili sauce, 2 tbsp brown sugar, 1 tbsp Worcestershire sauce
instructions: Preheat oven to 350Â°F (175Â°C) | Combine diced onion, diced apple, diced ham, dry mustard, baked beans, chili sauce, brown sugar, and Worcestershire sauce in a 1 1/2-quart buttered casserole dish | Stir everything together until well mixed | Cover the dish with a lid or foil | Bake for 45 to 60 minutes or until the mixture is hot and bubbly throughout | Remove cover during the last 10 minutes if you prefer a slightly thicker consistency | Serve hot as a hearty side dish

ingredients: 4 shortcake cups (store-bought or homemade), 1 cup fresh strawberries (sliced), 4 large marshmallows, chocolate sauce for drizzling (optional)
instructions: Fill two shortcake cups with sliced fresh strawberries, mounding them slightly | Roast marshmallows over an open flame or under a broiler until golden brown and gooey, watching carefully | Quickly assemble: top the strawberries with one or two hot roasted marshmallows | Invert the remaining shortcake cups so the cup side is facing down and place on top of the marshmallows, pressing down gently | The heat from the marshmallows will warm the strawberries slightly | Drizzle with chocolate sauce if desired | Serve immediately while the marshmallows are still warm and gooey

ingredients: 3 tbsp olive oil, 1 medium onion (diced), 1 tsp dried oregano or Greek seasoning, 4 large pita breads (cut into 1-inch pieces and toasted), 1 cup reduced-sodium chicken broth, 1/2 cup ready-made bruschetta spread, 1/4 cup Kalamata black olives (sliced), 1 tbsp fresh lemon juice, 1/4 cup Italian parsley (chopped), salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Preheat oven to 400Â°F (200Â°C) | Place pita bread pieces in a single layer on a large sheet pan and bake for 5 to 8 minutes until lightly toasted | Meanwhile, heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat | Add diced onion and cook, stirring, until lightly browned, about 5 minutes | Add oregano or Greek seasoning, toasted pita bread, and chicken broth | Stir until the bread is uniformly moistened and the broth is mostly absorbed | Stir in bruschetta spread, sliced olives, lemon juice, salt, pepper, and chopped parsley | Heat through, stirring gently to combine all ingredients | Keep warm or reheat immediately before serving | Serve as a flavorful stuffing alongside roasted meats or as a standalone side dish

ingredients: For dough: 1 cup warm milk, 2 large eggs, 1/3 cup margarine (softened), 4 cups all-purpose flour, 1 tsp salt, 1/2 cup white sugar, 2 1/4 tsp active dry yeast. For filling: 1 cup brown sugar (packed), 2 tbsp ground cinnamon, 1/3 cup margarine (softened). For icing: 4 oz cream cheese (softened), 1/4 cup margarine (softened), 1 1/2 cups icing sugar, 1/2 tsp vanilla extract, pinch of salt
instructions: Place all dough ingredients into a mixing bowl and mix until a smooth dough forms â€” using a dough hook with a stand mixer works best, or knead by hand for 8-10 minutes | Cover dough and set aside in a draft-free area and allow to double in size, about 1 hour | In a small bowl, combine brown sugar and cinnamon for the filling, mixing well | After dough has doubled, punch it down and roll out on a lightly floured surface into a 16x21 inch rectangle | Spread softened margarine over the dough, then sprinkle the cinnamon-brown sugar filling evenly across the entire surface | Starting from the long edge, roll up the dough tightly into a log | Cut the log into 12 equal buns using a sharp knife or dental floss | Place buns cut-side up in a greased 9x13 baking pan, spacing them slightly apart | Cover and let rise until doubled, about 30-45 minutes | Preheat oven to 400Â°F (200Â°C) | Place buns in the oven and bake for approximately 15 minutes until golden brown | While buns are baking, beat together cream cheese, softened margarine, icing sugar, vanilla, and a pinch of salt until smooth to make the icing | Spread the icing generously over warm buns immediately after removing from the oven | Serve warm â€” leftovers reheat nicely in the microwave

ingredients: 1 cup fresh parsley (finely chopped), 1/2 cup water, 1/2 cup unsalted butter, 1/4 tsp salt, pinch of white pepper, 1 tsp lemon juice (optional)
instructions: Bring water to a boil in a small saucepan | Add finely chopped parsley and cook for 2-3 minutes until the parsley is bright green and tender | Do not drain â€” the water should be mostly absorbed | Add butter and stir gently until completely melted and hot throughout | Season with salt and a pinch of white pepper | Add a squeeze of fresh lemon juice if desired for brightness | Serve immediately as a warm sauce over fish, boiled potatoes, or vegetables

ingredients: 1 unbaked 9-inch pie crust, 8 oz cream cheese (softened), 4 large eggs (divided), 1 tsp vanilla extract, 1 1/2 cups pecan halves, 3/4 cup corn syrup, 1/2 cup brown sugar (packed)
instructions: Prepare or thaw pie crust according to package directions for a one-crust pie | Preheat oven to 425Â°F (220Â°C) | Beat softened cream cheese, 1 egg, and vanilla extract until smooth and creamy | Spread the cream cheese mixture evenly in the bottom of the pie shell | Sprinkle pecan halves evenly over the cream cheese layer | In a separate bowl, beat the remaining 3 eggs with corn syrup and brown sugar until well combined and smooth | Pour the egg mixture evenly over the pecans | Bake in the preheated oven for 10 minutes | Reduce heat to 375Â°F (190Â°C) and continue baking for 25-30 minutes longer until the filling is set in the center and the top is golden | Cool completely on a wire rack before slicing â€” the cheesecake layer needs time to set | Refrigerate for at least 2 hours before serving for cleanest slices

ingredients: 1 cup sour cream, 1/4 tsp salt, 1/4 tsp fresh ground black pepper, 2 tbsp fresh dill (chopped), 1 tsp lemon zest, 1 tbsp fresh lemon juice, 1/2 tsp sugar (adjust to taste)
instructions: Combine sour cream, salt, black pepper, chopped fresh dill, lemon zest, and lemon juice in a mixing bowl | Stir everything together until well blended | Before adding sugar, taste the sauce â€” the natural sweetness of the sour cream and dill may be sufficient | Add sugar a little at a time to suit your taste, balancing the tangy and sweet flavors | Cover and refrigerate until ready to serve, at least 30 minutes for the flavors to meld | Serve chilled as a dipping sauce for vegetables, a topping for fish, or alongside potatoes

ingredients: For crust: 1 1/2 cups whole wheat pastry flour, 1/2 tsp salt, 1/3 cup vegetable oil, 3 tbsp cold water, 1 egg white (for brushing). For filling: 6 medium apples (peeled, cored, and sliced), 1 tbsp lemon juice, 1 tbsp lemon zest, 1 tsp ground cinnamon, 1/4 tsp ground nutmeg, 1/4 tsp ground coriander, 1/4 cup apple juice concentrate, 1/4 tsp cream of tartar. For meringue: 2 egg whites, 1/2 tsp lemon zest, 1/4 tsp cream of tartar
instructions: Sift flour and salt together in a large bowl | Stir in vegetable oil and cold water, mixing until a dough forms | Knead dough 3-4 times until moist and elastic, then form into a ball | Cover and refrigerate for 10 minutes | Place chilled dough between 2 sheets of wax paper and roll into a 12-inch circle | Carefully transfer to an 8-inch pie plate, trim edges, and press with a fork to crimp | Poke a few holes in the bottom of the pie shell with a fork | Brush the crust with beaten egg white and bake at 350Â°F (175Â°C) for 5 minutes, then remove from oven | While crust bakes, peel, core, and slice apples | Drop apple slices into a bowl of cold water with 1 tablespoon lemon juice to prevent browning | Drain and pat dry before using | Mix apple slices with half the lemon zest, cinnamon, nutmeg, coriander, and apple juice concentrate | Turn the apple mixture into the pre-baked pie shell | Bake at 350Â°F for 12-15 minutes until apples are tender | While pie bakes, whip 2 egg whites until stiff peaks form | Add remaining lemon zest and cream of tartar, continuing to beat until thick and glossy | Remove pie from oven, pile the meringue on top in decorative swirls, and sprinkle with remaining lemon zest | Return to oven and bake for 5-7 minutes longer or until meringue is golden brown | Cool before slicing

ingredients: 500g lump crabmeat, 2 large eggs, 1/4 cup mayonnaise, 1 tsp Worcestershire sauce, 1 tsp Dijon mustard, 1/2 tsp baking powder, 1 cup panko breadcrumbs, 2 tbsp fresh parsley (chopped), 1 tsp Old Bay seasoning, lemon wedges for serving
instructions: Preheat oven to 350Â°F (175Â°C) and spray a baking sheet with non-stick spray | In a large bowl, mix together eggs, mayonnaise, Worcestershire sauce, Dijon mustard, baking powder, panko breadcrumbs, chopped parsley, and Old Bay seasoning until well combined | Gently fold in the lump crabmeat, being very careful not to break up the lumps â€” the cakes should have visible chunks of crab | Form the mixture into cakes using a 2-tablespoon measuring spoon to scoop out heaping portions, gently shaping into patties about 2 1/2 inches in diameter | Place formed crab cakes on the prepared baking sheet, spacing them slightly apart | Bake for 15 minutes or until golden on top and cooked through | Serve immediately with lemon wedges and tartar sauce or remoulade on the side

ingredients: 2 tbsp olive oil, 2 tbsp all-purpose flour, 2 tsp Cajun seasoning, 2 cups bottled clam juice, 1 can (400g) diced tomatoes with sweet onions, 3 cups fresh spinach leaves, 1 tbsp fresh thyme leaves, 2 cloves garlic (minced), 250g lump crabmeat, salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Whisk olive oil and flour together in a heavy large saucepan over medium-high heat until smooth and golden brown, about 3 minutes | Add Cajun seasoning to taste and stir for 30 seconds until fragrant | Add clam juice and stir until smooth and well incorporated | Add diced tomatoes with their juices | Reduce heat to medium-low and simmer for 3 minutes | Add fresh spinach, thyme leaves, and minced garlic | Simmer until spinach is just wilted, about 1 minute | Gently add lump crabmeat and simmer until heated through, about 1-2 minutes, stirring very gently to avoid breaking up the crab | Season to taste with salt and black pepper | Ladle soup into warm bowls and serve immediately

ingredients: 2 cups almond flour, 1 cup granulated sugar, 2 large egg whites, 1 tsp almond extract, 1/4 cup whole amarena cherries in syrup (drained), powdered sugar for dusting
instructions: Preheat oven to 300Â°F (150Â°C) and line a baking sheet with parchment paper or a silicone mat | In a mixing bowl, stir together sugar and egg whites until the sugar has mostly dissolved | Stir in almond flour and almond extract â€” this mixture is very thick and may be too tough for a hand mixer; use a rubber spatula or pulse in a food processor until the dough is evenly mixed | Spoon the mixture into a cookie press to shape small round cookies, or use a small ice cream scoop to form little balls | Place cookies about 1/2 inch apart on the prepared baking sheet | Gently press one amarena cherry into the center of each cookie | Bake for approximately 30 minutes on the lowest rack setting for the first 10 minutes, then move to the middle rack | Cookies are done when they start to turn lightly golden around the edges | Remove from oven and let cool on the baking sheet â€” they will be slightly chewy right after baking but will become very crisp as they cool overnight | Dust with powdered sugar before serving | Store in an airtight container

ingredients: 1 unbaked 9-inch pie crust, 1 cup light corn syrup, 3/4 cup granulated sugar, 1/4 cup unsalted butter (melted), 1 tsp vanilla extract, 3 large eggs, 1 cup semi-sweet chocolate chips, 1 1/2 cups pecan halves (plus extra for garnish), whipped topping for serving
instructions: Preheat oven to 325Â°F (160Â°C) and place pie crust in a 9-inch pie plate | In a large bowl, combine corn syrup, sugar, melted butter, vanilla, and eggs â€” beat well until smooth and fully combined | Stir in chocolate chips and pecan halves until evenly distributed | Pour the filling into the unbaked pie crust, spreading evenly | Bake at 325Â°F for 55 to 65 minutes until the filling is set and deep golden brown â€” the center should have a slight jiggle but not be liquid | Cool for 1 hour or until completely cool to room temperature | Top with whipped topping and garnish with additional pecan halves if desired | Keep refrigerated until ready to serve | Slice and serve chilled or at room temperature

ingredients: For apple mixture: 3 tbsp butter, 2 medium apples (peeled and diced), 1 tsp ground cinnamon. For dry ingredients: 1 cup all-purpose flour, 1 cup whole wheat flour, 1/2 cup rolled oats, 2 tsp baking powder, 1/2 tsp baking soda, 1 cup Swiss cheese (diced). For wet ingredients: 1/2 cup unsalted butter (softened), 3/4 cup brown sugar, 2 large eggs, 3/4 cup milk, 1 tsp vanilla extract
instructions: Preheat oven to 375Â°F (190Â°C) | Butter and flour a loaf pan, or line with parchment paper | In a frying pan over medium heat, melt 3 tbsp butter and cook diced apples until soft, about 5-6 minutes | Sprinkle with cinnamon, stir, and set aside to cool | In a large bowl, combine all-purpose flour, whole wheat flour, rolled oats, baking powder, baking soda, and diced Swiss cheese â€” make a well in the center | In a separate bowl, cream 1/2 cup softened butter with brown sugar until light and fluffy | Beat in eggs one at a time | Gradually add milk, vanilla extract, and the cooled apple mixture, stirring to combine | Pour the wet ingredients into the well of dry ingredients and stir with a wooden spoon until just combined â€” do not overmix | Spread batter evenly in the prepared loaf pan | If desired, arrange a few additional thin apple slices on top | Bake in the center of the oven for 1 hour or until a toothpick inserted in the center comes out clean | Let cool in the pan for 10 minutes, then turn out onto a wire rack | Sprinkle with powdered sugar after cooling if desired | Can also be baked as muffins for 15-20 minutes | Batter may be prepared the day before, refrigerated, and baked in the morning â€” add 10-15 minutes extra baking time if cold | Freezes very well

ingredients: For crust: 1 cup all-purpose flour, 1/2 cup pecans (finely crushed), 1/2 cup unsalted butter (melted). For middle layer: 8 oz cream cheese (softened), 1 cup powdered sugar, 1 cup whipped topping (thawed). For top layer: 2 packages instant chocolate pudding mix, 3 cups cold milk, 2 cups whipped topping (for spreading), 1/4 cup pecan pieces (for garnish)
instructions: Preheat oven to 350Â°F (175Â°C) | Make the crust: combine flour, crushed pecans, and melted butter in a bowl, mixing until crumbly | Press the mixture firmly into the bottom of a 9x13-inch pan | Bake for 10-12 minutes until lightly golden | Allow crust to cool completely before layering | Make the middle layer: beat softened cream cheese and powdered sugar in a large bowl with an electric mixer on medium speed until well blended and smooth | Gently stir in 1 cup of whipped topping until incorporated | Spread the cream cheese mixture evenly over the cooled crust | Make the top layer: combine cold milk and instant chocolate pudding mix in a large bowl | Beat with a wire whisk for 2 minutes or until well blended and beginning to thicken | Spoon the pudding over the cream cheese layer and spread evenly | Refrigerate until set, at least 2 hours | Just before serving, spread remaining whipped topping over the top and sprinkle with pecan pieces | Refrigerate any leftovers | Chocolate pudding can be substituted with lemon pudding for a different variation

ingredients: For topping: 1 cup rolled oats, 1/2 cup dark brown sugar (packed), 1/3 cup all-purpose flour, 1/2 cup unsalted butter (cold, cubed), 1/2 cup gingersnap cookie crumbs, 1 egg yolk, 1/4 cup chopped nuts. For filling: 6 medium apples (peeled and sliced), 1 1/2 cups fresh cranberries, 1/2 cup granulated sugar, 1 tsp ground cinnamon, 1 tbsp lemon juice
instructions: Preheat oven to 350Â°F (175Â°C) and butter a 2-quart baking dish | Prepare the topping: mix together rolled oats, brown sugar, and flour in a bowl | Blend in cold butter with your fingers until coarse crumbs form | Add gingersnap crumbs, egg yolk, and chopped nuts, blending well until the mixture is crumbly | In a separate bowl, combine sliced apples, fresh cranberries, granulated sugar, cinnamon, and lemon juice â€” toss to coat evenly | Spoon the fruit filling into the buttered baking dish | Sprinkle the topping evenly over the filling, covering completely | Bake for 30 minutes or until golden and bubbly | If the topping browns too quickly, cover loosely with foil for the last 10 minutes of baking | Serve warm with vanilla ice cream or a drizzle of warm caramel sauce

ingredients: 4 medium zucchini (sliced into rounds), 2 tbsp olive oil, 1/2 cup Parmesan cheese (grated), 1 tsp Italian seasoning, 1/2 tsp salt, 1/4 tsp black pepper, 1/4 cup breadcrumbs (optional, for extra crunch)
instructions: Preheat oven to 350Â°F (175Â°C) | Coat the bottom of a glass baking dish or metal pan with 1 tablespoon olive oil | Arrange sliced zucchini rounds in the dish in overlapping rows | Drizzle remaining olive oil evenly over the top of the zucchini | Sprinkle grated Parmesan cheese generously over all | Sprinkle Italian seasoning, salt, and black pepper on top | For extra crunch, add a light layer of breadcrumbs | Bake for 30 minutes until zucchini is tender and the cheese is golden and bubbly | Serve hot as a side dish

ingredients: 400g spaghettini or thin spaghetti, 1/4 cup olive oil, 3 large sweet onions (thinly sliced), 4 cloves garlic (minced), 1/2 cup chicken broth, 1/2 tsp dried thyme, 1/4 tsp black pepper, 1 cup frozen peas (thawed), 1 cup Swiss cheese (shredded), 1/4 cup fresh parsley (chopped), salt to taste
instructions: In a large skillet, heat olive oil over medium heat | Add sliced onions and minced garlic, tossing to coat with oil | Reduce heat to low, cover, and cook, stirring occasionally, until onions are very tender and a deep golden color, about 15 minutes | Stir in chicken broth, dried thyme, and black pepper, cooking for 2 more minutes | Meanwhile, cook spaghettini in a large pot of salted boiling water until al dente | Drain pasta and place in a large serving bowl | Add thawed peas and the smothered onions to the pasta | Toss everything together to combine evenly | Add shredded Swiss cheese and chopped parsley, tossing again until the cheese begins to melt | Season to taste with salt and additional pepper | Serve immediately in warm bowls

ingredients: 500g chicken tenders, 1 cup yellow cornmeal, 1 tbsp chili powder, 1 tsp dried oregano, 1 tsp salt, 1/4 tsp black pepper, 2 large eggs, 1/4 cup vegetable oil (for frying), ranch or honey mustard for dipping
