instructions: In a shallow bowl, combine cornmeal, chili powder, oregano, salt, and pepper | In another shallow bowl, beat the eggs until well combined | Working with one at a time, coat each chicken tender in the cornmeal mixture, dip into the beaten egg, then coat again with the cornmeal mixture â€” this double-coating ensures maximum crispiness | Transfer coated tenders to a large plate | For a healthier version: preheat oven to 450Â°F (230Â°C), place coated tenders on a greased baking sheet, and bake for 12 minutes, turning once | For pan-frying: heat 1/4 cup vegetable oil in a large skillet over medium heat | Add half the chicken tenders and cook, turning once, until golden brown and cooked through, about 5 to 6 minutes total | Transfer to a plate and tent with foil to keep warm | Repeat with remaining chicken tenders | Serve immediately with ranch dressing or honey mustard for dipping

ingredients: 500g minced beef, 1 medium onion (finely diced), 2 large eggs, 3 cloves garlic (minced), 1 tsp dried basil, 1 tsp salt, 1/2 tsp black pepper, 4 medium potatoes (peeled), vegetable oil for frying, lettuce leaves for serving, fresh dill and parsley (chopped), cucumber slices for garnish
instructions: Mix minced beef with one beaten egg, diced onion, minced garlic, basil, salt, and pepper until well combined | Form the meat mixture into small thin patties and set aside | Peel potatoes and grate them using the large holes of a box grater | Add a pinch of salt to the grated potatoes and mix well | Roll the grated potatoes into small balls â€” each latke requires two potato balls and one meat patty | Flatten one potato ball with a fork or spoon on a clean surface, place a meat patty on top, then cover with another flattened potato ball, sealing the edges | Heat vegetable oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat | Fry each potato and meat latke for 3-4 minutes per side until golden brown and crispy on both sides | Drain on paper towels | Serve on lettuce leaves and garnish with cucumber slices and chopped fresh dill and parsley

ingredients: 16 oz cream cheese (softened), 3/4 cup granulated sugar, 1 tsp vanilla extract, 3 large eggs, 1 prepared graham cracker crust (9-inch), fresh fruit purÃ©e or pie filling for topping
instructions: Preheat oven to 350Â°F (175Â°C) | With an electric mixer at medium speed, beat softened cream cheese, sugar, eggs, and vanilla extract until well blended and smooth â€” do not overbeat | Pour the filling into the prepared graham cracker crust and spread evenly | Bake for 40 minutes or until the center is almost set but still slightly jiggly | Turn off oven and let cheesecake cool inside with the door slightly open for 30 minutes | Remove from oven and cool completely at room temperature | Refrigerate for at least 3 hours or overnight until fully set | Top with your favorite purÃ©e of seasonal fruit or pie filling before serving | Slice and serve chilled

ingredients: 2 lbs pickling cucumbers (sliced into 1/4-inch thick rounds), boiling water, 1 cup cider vinegar, 1 cup water, 1 cup sugar substitute, 1 tsp canning salt, 1 tsp mustard seeds, 1 tsp whole allspice, 1 tsp celery seed, 2 cinnamon sticks
instructions: Wash and rinse pint canning jars and keep hot until ready to use | Prepare lids according to manufacturer's directions | Wash cucumbers and slice 1/16-inch off the blossom ends, then discard | Slice cucumbers into 1/4-inch thick rounds | Pour boiling water over the cucumber slices and let stand for 5 to 10 minutes | Drain off the hot water and run cold water over the cucumbers until they are completely cooled | Drain slices well | In a 10-quart Dutch oven or stockpot, mix vinegar, 1 cup water, sugar substitute, and all spices | Bring to a boil and carefully add drained cucumber slices to the boiling liquid | Return to a boil | Place one cinnamon stick in each jar if desired | With a slotted spoon, fill hot pickle slices into clean hot pint jars, leaving 1/2-inch headspace | Cover with boiling hot pickling brine, leaving 1/2-inch headspace | Remove air bubbles and adjust headspace if needed | Wipe rims of jars with a dampened clean paper towel and apply two-piece metal canning lids | Process in a boiling water canner for 10 minutes | Let cool undisturbed for 12 to 24 hours and check for seals

ingredients: 2 tbsp olive oil, 3 cloves garlic (minced), 1 tsp lemon zest, 1 tsp dried herbs (thyme or rosemary), 200g green beans (trimmed), 200g asparagus spears (trimmed), 1/2 cup breadcrumbs, 1/2 cup mozzarella cheese (shredded), 1/4 cup Swiss cheese (shredded), 1 tbsp olive oil (for topping)
instructions: Preheat oven to 425Â°F (220Â°C) | Line a baking sheet with parchment paper | In a small bowl, combine 2 tablespoons olive oil, minced garlic, lemon zest, and dried herbs | Spread trimmed green beans and asparagus spears evenly on the prepared baking sheet | Toss vegetables with the oil mixture until evenly coated | Roast for 15 minutes, turning vegetables halfway through | Meanwhile, combine breadcrumbs, mozzarella, Swiss cheese, and remaining 1 tablespoon olive oil in a small bowl | Remove vegetables from oven and set broiler to high | Transfer roasted vegetables to an ovenproof gratin dish | Sprinkle the cheese and breadcrumb mixture evenly over the top | Broil until the cheese melts and bubbles, about 1-2 minutes â€” watch carefully to prevent burning | Serve immediately

ingredients: 2 cups cooked chicken (shredded), 8 oz cream cheese (softened), 1 cup salsa (red or green), 1 cup shredded Mexican blend cheese, 1/4 cup red onion (diced, optional), 1/4 cup black beans (optional), 2 tbsp fresh cilantro (chopped), tortilla chips for serving
instructions: In a microwave-safe bowl, microwave the cooked chicken until it is heated through, about 1 to 2 minutes | Shred the hot chicken with two forks until finely pulled | Add cream cheese on top of the chicken and microwave in 10-second intervals until the cream cheese is softened and easy to stir | Stir in the salsa until well combined | Stir in the shredded cheese until melted and fully incorporated | Stir in any additional ingredients you choose â€” diced red onion, black beans, cilantro, or whatever you like | You can serve this dip hot or cold | Serve with sturdy tortilla chips or scoops for dipping | This makes a small batch of appetizer portions â€” double or triple the recipe if feeding a crowd

ingredients: 8 oz cream cheese (softened), 1 tbsp prepared horseradish, 1 clove garlic (minced), 1/4 tsp kosher salt, 1/4 tsp cracked black pepper (plus extra for garnish), 200g sliced turkey pastrami, green leaf lettuce leaves (cut into small strips), toothpicks for securing
instructions: Mix the softened cream cheese, horseradish, minced garlic, salt, and pepper together until well blended and smooth | Lay the pastrami slices on a flat surface | Spread a small amount of the cheese mixture evenly on each pastrami slice | Cut the pastrami slices into approximately 1-inch by 3-inch strips (or similar size depending on what your deli provides) so that when rolled they will be bite-size pieces | Cut small pieces of green leaf lettuce to fit one side of each pastrami strip | Place the lettuce on the cream cheese mixture so that when rolled, a small portion of the curly lettuce extends beyond the pastrami | Roll up each pastrami strip from the opposite end of the lettuce and secure with a toothpick | You should have a roll of pastrami with the leaf lettuce peeking out | Arrange on a serving plate and sprinkle with freshly cracked black pepper | Serve immediately or refrigerate until ready to serve

ingredients: 200g dark chocolate (70% cocoa, broken into pieces), 1 tsp instant coffee or espresso powder, 3 tbsp boiling water, 4 large eggs (separated), pinch of salt, whipped cream for serving (optional)
instructions: Break up the chocolate into a small heavy saucepan | Dissolve the coffee or espresso powder in the boiling water and pour it over the chocolate | Place over low heat and stir occasionally with a small wire whisk until the mixture is completely smooth | Remove from heat and set aside for about 5 minutes to cool slightly | In the bowl of an electric mixer at high speed, beat the egg yolks for 3 to 4 minutes until pale lemon-colored and thick | With a spatula, add the chocolate mixture to the yolks and mix until smooth â€” do not overmix | In a separate clean bowl, add a pinch of salt to the egg whites and beat until they hold a definite shape but are not dry | Gently fold the beaten whites into the chocolate mixture in thirds, folding only until no white streaks remain | Pour gently into serving glasses or bowls, filling about 3/4 full | Cover with plastic wrap and refrigerate for 3 to 6 hours â€” can be refrigerated for up to 24 hours though the texture becomes more spongy over time | Serve with whipped cream on top if desired

ingredients: 1 1/2 cups icing sugar, 1/2 cup unsalted butter (softened), 1 tsp lemon zest, 1 vanilla bean (seeds scraped) or 1 tsp vanilla extract, 1/4 tsp salt, 1 cup all-purpose flour, 1/2 cup ground hazelnuts, 1 tsp baking powder, 1/2 cup raisins, 1 1/2 cups carrots (grated), 1/4 cup heavy cream (whipped), 1/2 cup walnuts (whole, for topping)
instructions: Preheat oven to 180Â°C (350Â°F) | In a large bowl, whip together icing sugar, softened butter, vanilla, and lemon zest until light and fluffy | Sift the flour and baking powder together in a separate bowl | Add the ground hazelnuts to the flour and mix well | Mix the flour-hazelnut mixture into the butter mixture until just combined | Fold in the whipped cream (this replaces eggs for moisture) and mix well | Stir in the raisins and grated carrots until evenly distributed | Grease and flour a 7-inch cake tin, or use well-greased and dusted individual muffin molds | Pour the prepared batter into the tin and spread evenly | Arrange whole walnuts over the top of the cake | Bake for 25 minutes or until a wooden toothpick inserted in the center comes out clean | Turn out onto a wire rack and allow to cool completely | Dust with icing sugar before serving | If using muffin molds, you can dip the cooled tops in melted chocolate to retain moisture

ingredients: 3 large eggs, 1/4 cup shredded cheese (cheddar, Swiss, or GruyÃ¨re), 1 tbsp butter, salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Whisk the eggs in a bowl until light and fluffy â€” the more air incorporated, the fluffier the omelette | Stir in shredded cheese and season with salt and pepper | Mix well | Heat a 7-inch non-stick skillet over medium heat and add butter | As the butter begins to foam but before it browns, lower the heat to medium-low | Pour the beaten egg mixture into the pan, tilting to spread evenly | Cook covered for 1 minute until the eggs are set on the bottom but still slightly glossy on top | Using a spatula, gently fold one half of the omelette over the other | Slide onto a warm plate and serve immediately

ingredients: 4 paua (New Zealand abalone, cleaned and shucked), 3 tbsp butter, 1 Spanish onion (diced), 1 tbsp fresh ginger (grated), 1/2 tsp fresh ground black pepper, 1 cup champagne or sparkling wine, 1/2 cup fish stock, 1/4 cup heavy cream, 1 tsp balsamic vinegar, steamed white rice for serving
instructions: Drown paua in fresh water for a minimum of 6 hours and a maximum of 8 hours until the flesh is limp to the touch | Shuck the flesh from the shells and trim off the skirt and gut, placing the cleaned flesh to one side | Heat butter in a large frypan over medium heat | SautÃ© diced onion and grated ginger until golden brown, about 6-8 minutes | Add black pepper at the last minute and sautÃ© for a further 30 seconds | Pour in champagne with the heat at a very very low simmer â€” do not allow to boil at any time, this is critical for tender paua | Add the paua, cover, and cook at a very low simmer for 1 to 1 1/2 hours â€” remember, do not let it boil or the paua will toughen | Remove paua and place to one side, covered to keep warm | Add fish stock and cream to the remaining liquid in the pan | Bring to a boil and reduce the liquid to a warm honey consistency â€” this should take only a minute | Add balsamic vinegar and stir | Turn off the heat, return the warm paua to the pan, and stir to coat in the sauce | Serve arranged over steamed plain white rice with a lettuce and tomato salad

ingredients: 4 boneless skinless chicken breasts, 1/2 cup mayonnaise (or Italian dressing, or honey mustard), 1 1/2 cups breadcrumbs (Italian or panko), 1/2 tsp salt, 1/4 tsp black pepper
instructions: Preheat oven to 425Â°F (220Â°C) and lightly grease a baking sheet | Thaw chicken breasts if frozen and pat completely dry with paper towels | Coat each raw chicken breast generously with your chosen base â€” mayonnaise, Italian dressing, or honey mustard all work beautifully | Roll the coated chicken in breadcrumbs, pressing firmly so the crumbs adhere evenly on all sides | Season with salt and pepper | Place coated chicken on the prepared baking sheet | Bake for 20 minutes or until the chicken is golden brown and the internal temperature reaches 165Â°F (74Â°C) | Let rest for 3-5 minutes before serving | Serve with a side salad or steamed vegetables

ingredients: 450g dried navy beans (soaked overnight), 6 slices bacon (diced), 1 medium onion (diced), 2 celery ribs (diced), 2 carrots (diced), 1 tsp salt, 1/2 tsp black pepper, 6 cups water
instructions: Soak dried navy beans in plenty of water overnight, then drain and rinse | The next day, cook diced bacon in a large pot over medium heat until crisp | Remove bacon with a slotted spoon and drain on paper towels, then slice into small pieces and set aside | Put 1/2 cup of the soaked beans aside | Add the remaining beans to a large pot of fresh water along with diced onion, carrots, and celery | Place the reserved 1/2 cup of beans in a blender with a splash of water and blend for 30-60 seconds until smooth | Add the blended beans to the pot â€” this acts as a natural thickener | Bring to a boil, then add the crispy bacon pieces | Reduce heat and cook on medium for 1 hour and 15 minutes, or until the beans are soft and tender | For a thicker soup, use a potato masher to mash some of the beans during cooking | Season with salt and black pepper to taste | Serve hot in bowls

ingredients: 200g turkey sausage, 200g pork sausage, 2 tbsp extra virgin olive oil, 2 potatoes (peeled and diced, or 2 cups frozen hash browns), salt and black pepper, 2 tbsp butter (divided), 4 scallions (sliced, white and green parts separated), 2 tbsp all-purpose flour, 2 cups low-fat milk, 2 tomatoes (diced), 6 large eggs (beaten), 1/2 cup sharp cheddar cheese (shredded)
instructions: In a large nonstick skillet, cook turkey and pork sausage over medium-high heat, breaking it up with a wooden spoon, until browned, about 5 minutes â€” remove from heat and set aside | In a medium cast-iron skillet, heat olive oil over medium heat | Add diced potatoes or frozen hash browns, season with 1/4 teaspoon salt and pepper, and cook, turning infrequently, until browned, about 15 minutes | Meanwhile, in a small saucepan, melt 1 tablespoon butter over medium heat | Add white parts of scallions and cook until softened, about 2 minutes | Stir in flour and cook for 1 minute, then gradually whisk in milk | Cook until thickened, season with salt and pepper, cover, and keep warm | Return the nonstick skillet with sausage to medium-high heat and add remaining 1 tablespoon butter | Add diced tomatoes and beaten eggs with a couple pinches of salt and pepper | Cook, scrambling, until eggs are just set, about 2-3 minutes | Divide the egg mixture among 4 plates | Top with the browned potatoes, drizzle with white sauce, and sprinkle with cheddar cheese | Garnish with reserved scallion greens and serve immediately

recipe_name: Chicken with White Beans and Spinach
ingredients: 3 boneless skinless chicken breasts (cut into strips), 1 tsp dried thyme, 1/2 tsp fresh ground black pepper, 2 tbsp butter (divided), 1/2 medium onion (diced), 3 cloves garlic (minced), 1/2 cup chicken broth, 1/4 cup dry white wine, 1 can (400g) cannellini beans (rinsed and drained), 3 cups baby spinach leaves, salt to taste
instructions: Cut chicken breasts into strips and season with dried thyme and black pepper | Melt 1 tablespoon butter in a large skillet over medium-high heat | Add chicken strips and brown over medium-high heat, about 3 to 4 minutes, stirring occasionally | Move chicken to one side of the skillet and add remaining 1/2 tablespoon butter | Add minced garlic and diced onion and sautÃ© for 1 minute until fragrant | Pour in chicken broth and white wine | Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer for 5 minutes | Stir in rinsed and drained cannellini beans and baby spinach leaves | Simmer for 5 more minutes until chicken is cooked through and spinach is wilted | Season with salt to taste | Serve immediately in shallow bowls

ingredients: 400g sushi-grade ahi tuna (cut into 1/2-inch cubes), 3 tbsp soy sauce, 1 tbsp sesame oil, 1 tsp sriracha, 2 green onions (thinly sliced), 1 tbsp toasted sesame seeds, 1 avocado (diced), 1 tsp grated ginger, steamed white rice or wonton chips for serving
instructions: Ensure tuna is sushi-grade and very fresh â€” it should be bright red with no fishy odor | Cut tuna into uniform 1/2-inch cubes using a very sharp knife | In a bowl, gently combine diced tuna with soy sauce, sesame oil, and sriracha | Add grated ginger and sliced green onions, folding gently to combine | Gently fold in diced avocado, being careful not to mash it | Cover and refrigerate for 15 minutes to allow flavors to meld | Sprinkle with toasted sesame seeds | Serve immediately over steamed white rice or with wonton chips for scooping

recipe_name: Scallops with Crumb Topping and Herb Butter
ingredients: For crumb topping: 1/3 cup yellow cornmeal, 2 tbsp pine nuts, 1 clove garlic, 1 1/2 tsp lemon peel (divided). For herb butter: 3 tbsp butter (softened), 2 tbsp fresh cilantro (chopped), 2 tbsp fresh parsley (chopped), 1 tsp fresh lemon juice. For scallops: 12 large sea scallops, 2 plum tomatoes (sliced), olive oil, salt and pepper. For salad: 1/4 cup olive oil, 1 tbsp fresh lime juice, 1 tsp honey, 1 tsp lime zest, 4 cups arugula, 1/4 cup fresh mint leaves
instructions: Finely grind cornmeal, pine nuts, garlic, and 1 teaspoon lemon peel in a food processor; set crumb mixture aside | In a small bowl, mix softened butter, cilantro, parsley, lemon juice, and remaining 1/2 teaspoon lemon peel | Season herb butter to taste with salt and pepper | Preheat oven to 450Â°F (230Â°C) | Brush a rimmed baking sheet with oil and place scallops on the sheet | Sprinkle scallops with salt and pepper | Top each scallop with a tomato slice, then divide the crumb mixture equally among them | Top each scallop with 1 teaspoon of herb butter | Bake until scallops are just opaque in the center, about 8 minutes | Meanwhile, whisk 1/4 cup olive oil, lime juice, honey, and lime zest in a small bowl to make the dressing | Season with salt and pepper | Toss arugula and mint in a bowl, adding dressing to taste | Divide dressed greens among 4 salad plates | Top with the baked scallops and serve immediately

ingredients: 4 boneless skinless chicken breasts, 2 cans (400g each) condensed cream of chicken soup, 1 can (400g) condensed cream of mushroom soup, 1/2 cup milk, 1/2 tsp garlic powder, 1/2 tsp black pepper, steamed rice, noodles, or mashed potatoes for serving
instructions: Preheat oven to 350Â°F (175Â°C) | Mix condensed soups together with milk, garlic powder, and black pepper in a baking dish large enough to hold the chicken | Add chicken breasts on top of the mixed soups, pressing them down slightly into the sauce | Bake at 350Â°F for about 45 minutes or until chicken juices run clear when pricked with a fork | If using bone-in chicken pieces, cooking time will be longer and you may want to cover the dish with foil so the sauce doesn't reduce too much | Serve the creamy sauce over steamed rice, buttered noodles, or mashed potatoes alongside the chicken

ingredients: 1 cup white chocolate baking bars (chopped), 1/4 cup nonfat milk, 2 tbsp light corn syrup, 12 large pretzel rods, assorted decorations (sprinkles, crushed candy canes, chopped nuts)
instructions: Line a baking sheet with waxed paper and set aside | Melt white chocolate baking bars in a small saucepan over low heat, stirring constantly until smooth | Stir in nonfat milk and corn syrup until well combined â€” do not remove saucepan from heat | Holding each pretzel rod with a fork, dip one side of the pretzel into the melted mixture to coat | Place coated side up on the prepared baking sheet and immediately sprinkle with desired decorations | Repeat with remaining pretzel rods | Refrigerate for 15 to 20 minutes or until firm | Once set, serve or store in an airtight container | For chocolate twisters: substitute 1 cup semisweet chocolate chips for the white baking bars | For caramel dipping sauce: heat 1 cup fat-free caramel sauce with 1/3 cup finely chopped pecans until warm and serve alongside for dipping

ingredients: 3 tbsp extra virgin olive oil, 4 cloves garlic (minced), 1/2 tsp crushed red pepper flakes, 1 kg littleneck clams (scrubbed and rinsed), 1/2 cup dry white wine, 1 cup tomato sauce, 3 scallions (thinly sliced), 1/4 cup fresh basil leaves (torn), salt to taste, crusty bread for serving
instructions: In a large wide heavy casserole or Dutch oven, heat 3 tablespoons olive oil over a medium flame | Add minced garlic and cook until golden brown, stirring for approximately 2 minutes | Add crushed red pepper flakes and stir briefly | Add clams and white wine | Place a lid on the pot, turn flame to high, and cook shaking the pot occasionally for approximately 7 minutes or until clams begin to open | Pour in tomato sauce, add sliced scallions and torn basil | Stir well and bring the mixture to a boil | Using a slotted spoon, transfer clams to a serving platter and discard any clams that did not open | Spoon the sauce over the clams and serve immediately with crusty bread on the side for dipping

ingredients: For dressing: 2 tbsp Dijon mustard, juice of 2 lemons, 1/3 cup olive oil, 1/4 tsp cayenne pepper, 1/2 tsp salt. For salad: 500g red potatoes (scrubbed), 300g asparagus spears (trimmed), 2 tbsp fresh chives (chopped)
instructions: Make the dressing: in a small bowl, combine Dijon mustard and fresh lemon juice | Whisk in olive oil gradually until smooth and emulsified | Season with salt and cayenne pepper, then set aside | Clean potatoes and asparagus very well | Cook potatoes in a large pot of boiling salted water until just tender, about 20-30 minutes depending on size | Strain and rinse with cool water, then set aside to cool | Cook asparagus in a large pot of boiling salted water until just crisp-tender, about 5 minutes | Strain and rinse with cool water to stop the cooking process | Once cool, cut potatoes in half and asparagus into bite-sized pieces | Toss potatoes and asparagus together in a large bowl and add chopped chives | Pour the dressing over the mixture and toss gently to coat evenly | Serve at room temperature

ingredients: 1 pizza dough (12-14 inch), 1/2 cup ricotta cheese, 1/4 cup prepared Italian marinade (divided), 1 red bell pepper (sliced), 1 yellow bell pepper (sliced), 1/2 red onion (sliced), 1 medium zucchini (sliced), 2 tbsp olive oil, 1 1/2 cups mozzarella cheese (shredded, divided)
instructions: Mix ricotta cheese with 1 tablespoon of the prepared marinade in a small bowl | Refrigerate until ready to use | Place sliced bell peppers, red onion, and zucchini in a large resealable plastic bag or glass dish | Add remaining marinade and toss to coat well | Refrigerate for 15 minutes or longer for extra flavor | Remove vegetables from marinade, reserving the marinade | Grill vegetables over medium-high heat for 2 to 4 minutes per side until tender-crisp, brushing with reserved marinade halfway through | Cut grilled vegetables into bite-size pieces | Stretch or roll pizza dough on a floured baking sheet to a 12 to 14-inch round, about 1/4-inch thick | Brush the top of the dough with olive oil | Place oiled-side down on the grill and close the lid | Grill over medium heat for 1 to 2 minutes until grill marks appear on the bottom | Carefully flip crust over using tongs or a spatula | Layer crust with the ricotta mixture, half of the mozzarella, grilled vegetables, and remaining mozzarella | Close the lid and grill for 3 to 4 minutes longer until cheese is melted and crust is browned, checking frequently to avoid burning | Slide pizza onto a baking sheet, slice, and serve immediately

ingredients: 500g breakfast sausage, 1 green bell pepper (diced), 1 medium onion (diced), 100g fresh mushrooms (sliced), 1/2 tsp garlic powder, 1/4 tsp black pepper, 8 large eggs, 1 cup Monterey Jack and cheddar cheese blend (shredded), 4 large flour tortillas, 2 packets country gravy mix (prepared), 2 tbsp vegetable oil
instructions: Prepare gravy mixes as directed on package in a medium saucepan and keep warm | In a medium skillet, brown breakfast sausage over medium-high heat, crumbling while cooking | Remove sausage with a slotted spoon and set aside | Pour off excess fat, reserving 2 tablespoons in the skillet and adding 2 tablespoons to the gravy if desired for extra sausage flavor | SautÃ© diced peppers, onions, and mushrooms in the reserved fat until tender, about 5-6 minutes | Stir in garlic powder, black pepper, and the cooked sausage | Separate the mixture into 4 sections in the pan, turn off the burner, and cover with a lid to keep warm | To prepare eggs: whisk 2 eggs at a time and cook each set in an omelet pan sprayed with cooking spray to form a thin crepe-like omelet â€” you should have 4 thin omelets | Warm tortillas as directed on package to make them pliable | To assemble: place one omelet on each tortilla | Spread the sausage mixture down the center of each tortilla on top of the eggs | Sprinkle each with shredded cheese | Roll into burritos and place one on each plate seam-side down | Cover with warm gravy and serve immediately

ingredients: 1 tbsp olive oil, 2 medium yellow onions (diced), 6 medium carrots (peeled and chopped), 1 tbsp curry powder, 1 tsp garam masala, 1/2 tsp ground cumin, 1/4 tsp ground cinnamon, 1/2 tsp salt, 4 cups vegetable broth, 1 cup light coconut milk, 1 red bell pepper (roasted and diced, optional), cooked chickpeas or rice for serving (optional)
instructions: In a medium or large stock pot, heat olive oil over medium heat | SautÃ© diced onions until they become translucent, about 5 minutes | Add chopped carrots, salt, curry powder, cumin, garam masala, and cinnamon | Continue to sautÃ© until onions are soft, about 5 more minutes | Stir vegetable broth into the onion, carrot, and spice mixture | Bring to a boil, then cover and simmer until carrots are tender, about 20-25 minutes | Add roasted red peppers to the pot if using and simmer on low until peppers are tender, about 5 minutes | Remove from heat and blend with an immersion blender until smooth, or carefully transfer to a blender in batches | Add coconut milk and continue to blend until silky smooth and creamy | Serve hot with garbanzo beans or rice added to the soup for extra heartiness

ingredients: 1 can (354ml) evaporated milk (well chilled), 1/3 cup granulated sugar, 1 packet unsweetened Kool-Aid drink mix (any flavor), 1 prepared graham cracker crust (9-inch), vanilla wafer cookies for lining (optional), whipped topping for garnish
instructions: Pour very cold evaporated milk into a small metal or glass mixing bowl and add beaters to the bowl | Cover and chill in the refrigerator for at least 2 hours â€” the milk must be extremely cold to whip properly | Coat a 9-inch pie plate with cooking spray and line the bottom and sides with vanilla wafers if desired | Beat the chilled evaporated milk with an electric mixer until soft peaks form, about 5 minutes | Add sugar and Kool-Aid drink mix | Beat until thoroughly mixed and the color is uniform, about 2 more minutes | Spoon the mixture over the prepared crust or wafers and spread evenly | Freeze for at least 4 hours until firm | Garnish with whipped topping if desired before serving | Slice and serve frozen

ingredients: 1 kg pickling cucumbers (small, scrubbed), 4 sprigs fresh dill (divided), 4 cloves garlic, 2 tbsp pickling salt, 2 cups white vinegar, 2 cups boiling water
instructions: Sterilize canning jars and keep hot until ready to use | Place 1/2 sprig of fresh dill and 1 clove of garlic at the bottom of each jar | Fill the jars tightly with whole pickling cucumbers, packing them in vertically | Place remaining 1/2 sprig of dill on top of the cucumbers in each jar | Combine pickling salt, vinegar, and boiling water in a large pot, stirring until salt is fully dissolved | Pour the hot brine over the cucumbers, filling each jar to within 1/2-inch of the top | Remove air bubbles, wipe rims clean, and seal with sterilized lids and bands | Process in a boiling water bath for 10 minutes | Let cool undisturbed for 12-24 hours and check for proper seals before storing

ingredients: 1 pound cake (store-bought or homemade, sliced 1/2-inch thick), 2 cans (400ml each) coconut milk, 1/2 cup unsalted butter, 1/2 cup granulated sugar, 4 large eggs, 1 tsp vanilla extract, 3 tbsp cornstarch mixed with 3 tbsp water, 1 cup sweetened shredded coconut, 1/2 tsp ground cinnamon
instructions: Slice pound cake into 1/2-inch thickness | Line the entire bottom of a 9 x 13-inch dish with cake slices, cutting pieces to fit around corners and between larger slices | Pour coconut milk into a large pot over medium-high heat | Add butter and sugar, stirring occasionally, and bring to a gentle boil | Lower heat slightly if necessary to maintain a gentle bubble | While waiting for the milk to heat, beat eggs and vanilla in a medium bowl and set aside | Mix cornstarch and water in a small bowl and set aside | When the milk comes to a boil, pour the egg mixture a little bit at a time into the milk, whisking quickly and constantly | Stir continuously and let the egg and milk mixture come back to a gentle boil | Stir the cornstarch slurry again, then pour into the gently boiling custard | Add shredded coconut â€” be careful as the custard will splatter | Stir vigorously and cook for two minutes until thickened | Pour the hot custard evenly over the pound cake layer | Sprinkle with ground cinnamon | Cool uncovered at room temperature for 30 minutes, then continue cooling uncovered in the refrigerator | This coconut latiya is exceptional after two days of refrigeration

ingredients: 2 cups all-purpose flour, 1 1/2 cups white sugar, 1/2 cup powdered sugar, 1 tsp baking soda, 1 tsp baking powder, 1/2 tsp salt, 3 large eggs, 1/4 cup amaretto liqueur, 1 cup coconut milk, 1/2 cup buttermilk, 1/2 cup vegetable oil, 1 tsp vanilla extract. For frosting: cream cheese frosting with a splash of coconut milk
instructions: Preheat oven to 350Â°F (175Â°C) | Grease and flour two 9-inch round cake pans or one 9x13-inch pan | In a large bowl, combine flour, white sugar, powdered sugar, baking soda, baking powder, and salt | Make a well in the center of the dry ingredients | Add eggs, amaretto liqueur, coconut milk, buttermilk, oil, and vanilla extract | Beat for 2 minutes on medium speed â€” batter will be thin | Pour batter into prepared pans | Bake for 30 to 40 minutes until a toothpick inserted into the center of the cake comes out clean | Cool for 10 minutes in the pans, then remove from pans and finish cooling on a wire rack | Fill and frost as desired â€” cream cheese frosting with a splash of coconut milk works beautifully | Slice and serve at room temperature

ingredients: 4 large eggs, 200g breakfast sausage, 1 cup water, 1 cup half-and-half, 1 cup stone-ground corn grits, 1/2 cup GruyÃ¨re cheese (grated), 1 tbsp rendered sausage fat (for greasing), salt and black pepper to taste, fresh chives for garnish
instructions: Preheat oven to 400Â°F (200Â°C) | Brown sausage in a pan over medium heat, crumbling as it cooks | Drain sausage on paper towels and reserve the grease | While sausage is browning, bring 3 cups of water and 1 cup of half-and-half to a boil in a medium saucepan | Pour 1 cup of grits into a bowl of water and tilt the bowl to pour off any floating bits into the sink | Scoop drained grits into the boiling milk mixture | Whisk boiling grits for 5 minutes, then reduce to a simmer for 20 minutes, continuing to whisk occasionally | Season with salt and several grinds of black pepper | Use the rendered sausage fat to grease 4 large individual ramekins or gratin dishes and arrange them on a rimmed sheet tray | Divide creamy grits between the prepared baking dishes | Top each with crumbled sausage and grated GruyÃ¨re | Make a small divot in the center of the mixture to nest the egg | Crack one egg into a small bowl, then carefully slide it into the divot | Repeat with remaining eggs | Bake until the egg whites are almost but not fully set, about 10 to 15 minutes â€” for more well-done eggs, bake until whites are fully set | Garnish with fresh chives and serve immediately

ingredients: 500g asparagus spears (trimmed), 3 tbsp unsalted butter, 1/2 tsp kosher salt, 1/4 tsp fresh ground black pepper, 1 tbsp fresh tarragon (chopped)
instructions: Bring a large saucepan of water to a boil | Add asparagus and cook for 3 minutes until crisp-tender and bright green | Drain and immediately rinse under cold water to stop cooking | Drain well and set aside | Melt butter in a large skillet over medium heat | Cook the butter for 3 minutes, swirling the pan occasionally, until it turns golden brown and gives off a nutty fragrance | Stir in salt and black pepper | Add the blanched asparagus and chopped tarragon | Cook for 1 minute, tossing to coat the asparagus evenly in the browned butter | Transfer to a serving plate and serve immediately

ingredients: 6 medium apples (peeled, cored, and sliced), 1/3 cup maple syrup, 1/4 tsp salt, 1/4 tsp ground nutmeg, 1/2 tsp ground cinnamon, 1 tbsp cornstarch mixed with 2 tbsp apple juice or water
instructions: Place sliced apples, maple syrup, salt, nutmeg, and cinnamon in a medium saucepan | Bring to a simmer over medium heat, then cover and simmer until apples are tender, about 10-15 minutes, stirring occasionally | In a small bowl, combine cornstarch and apple juice (or water) and stir until smooth | Pour the cornstarch mixture into the stewed apples and stir gently | Continue cooking for 1-2 minutes until the sauce thickens and coats the apples | Remove from heat and serve warm over pancakes, oatmeal, ice cream, or on their own

ingredients: 8 cups sweet apple cider, 1/4 cup fresh lemon juice, 1/4 cup granulated sugar, 3 cinnamon sticks, 1 tsp whole cloves, 1 orange (sliced into rounds, optional), 1/4 tsp ground nutmeg
instructions: Combine apple cider, fresh lemon juice, sugar, cinnamon sticks, whole cloves, orange slices (if using), and nutmeg in a large pot | Bring to a boil over medium-high heat, stirring to dissolve the sugar | Reduce heat to low and simmer for 15-20 minutes to allow the spices to infuse | Strain through a fine mesh sieve to remove whole spices if desired, or ladle directly into mugs leaving spices behind | Serve hot in heatproof mugs or glasses

ingredients: 4 boneless skinless chicken breast halves, 1/2 tsp salt, 1/4 tsp black pepper, 4 slices Swiss cheese, 1 can (400g) cream of chicken soup, 1 can (400g) cream of mushroom soup, 1/2 cup milk, 1 cup chicken broth, 2 cups Stove Top stuffing mix (dry), 1/4 cup unsalted butter (melted)
instructions: Place chicken breasts in the bottom of a crock pot or slow cooker | Pour chicken broth over the chicken breasts | Season chicken with salt and pepper | Place one slice of Swiss cheese on top of each chicken breast | In a separate bowl, combine both cans of soup and milk, mixing well | Pour the soup mixture evenly over the chicken breasts | Sprinkle the dry stuffing mix over the entire top of the dish | Drizzle melted butter evenly over the stuffing | Cover and cook on low for 6-8 hours or on high for 4 hours until chicken is cooked through | Serve hot, scooping down through the layers

ingredients: For sauce: 1/2 cup Swiss cheese (shredded), 1/4 cup Parmesan cheese (grated), 1/2 cup half-and-half, 1/4 cup whole milk, 1 tbsp butter, 1 tbsp all-purpose flour, pinch of nutmeg. For chicken: 2 boneless skinless chicken breast halves (flattened slightly), 1 tbsp butter, 200g broccoli florets (steamed), salt and pepper
instructions: Make the Mornay sauce: melt 1 tbsp butter in a saucepan over medium heat | Whisk in flour and cook for 1 minute | Gradually whisk in half-and-half and milk | Heat over low heat, stirring frequently, until the sauce is hot and begins to thicken | Add Swiss cheese and Parmesan cheese, stirring until fully melted and smooth | Season with a pinch of nutmeg, salt, and pepper, then keep warm | Meanwhile, flatten chicken breasts slightly to an even thickness | Season with salt and pepper | Melt 1 tbsp butter in a skillet over medium heat and sautÃ© chicken until golden brown and cooked through, about 8 to 10 minutes | While chicken cooks, steam broccoli florets until crisp-tender, about 3-4 minutes | Arrange cooked chicken and steamed broccoli on serving plates | Spoon the warm Mornay sauce generously over all | Serve immediately

ingredients: 6 Bartlett pears (peeled, cored, and finely chopped), 1 orange (peel reserved and slivered, fruit chopped), 1 lemon (peel reserved and slivered, fruit chopped), 1 can (400g) crushed pineapple in juice, 1/4 cup maraschino cherries (chopped), 5 cups granulated sugar, 1 package (57g) fruit pectin, 1 tsp butter
instructions: Peel and core pears, then finely chop or grind the fruit | Measure 4 cups of chopped pears into an 8-quart saucepan | Remove the colored part of the peel from the orange using a vegetable peeler and set aside | Remove and discard the remaining white pith from the orange | Chop the orange fruit, reserving any juice, and add to the saucepan | Repeat the procedure with the lemon and add to the saucepan | Cut the reserved orange and lemon peels into thin slivers or finely chop and add to the saucepan | Add crushed pineapple with its juice and chopped maraschino cherries to the saucepan and mix thoroughly | Measure sugar into a separate bowl | Mix 1/4 cup of the measured sugar with the pectin in a small bowl | Stir the pectin-sugar mixture into the fruit in the saucepan and add butter | Place over high heat and bring to a full boil, stirring constantly | Immediately stir in the remaining sugar | Bring back to a full rolling boil and boil for exactly 1 minute, stirring constantly | Remove from heat and ladle quickly into hot sterilized jars, filling to within 1/8 inch of the tops | Wipe jar rims and threads clean | Cover with two-piece lids and screw bands tightly | Place jars in a boiling water bath and process for 10 minutes | Makes about 7 one-cup jars

ingredients: 2 packages (85g each) strawberry jelly crystals, 2 cups boiling water, 2 cups cold water (divided), 2 cups fresh strawberries (halved), cream or ice cream for serving
instructions: Place jelly crystals in a large heatproof bowl | Pour 2 cups boiling water over the crystals | Whisk until the crystals have completely dissolved | Stir in 1 cup cold water | Pour 1/2 cup of the liquid jelly into a 7cm-deep rectangular dish | Place in the freezer for 5 to 10 minutes or until set | Arrange a single layer of halved strawberries, cut side down, onto the set jelly | Pour over another 1 cup of liquid jelly | Return to the freezer for 10 minutes or until set | Repeat the layering process twice more with remaining strawberries and liquid jelly | Refrigerate for 30 minutes or until completely firm | To serve, dip the base of the dish into hot water for 30 seconds and invert onto a serving platter | Serve with cream or ice cream

ingredients: 1 cup Parmesan cheese (freshly grated), 1 red apple (thinly sliced), 4 cups rocket (arugula), 2 tbsp olive oil, 1 tbsp balsamic vinegar, 1/2 tsp sea salt, 1/4 tsp black pepper, 100g goat cheese (crumbled, optional)
instructions: Preheat oven to 180Â°C (355Â°F) | Line a baking tray with non-stick baking paper | Arrange 8 portions of Parmesan cheese (about 1 1/2 tablespoons each) in circles on the prepared tray, spacing them apart | Bake for 10 minutes or until the cheese is melted, golden, and crispy | Remove from oven and set aside to cool â€” the wafers will crisp up as they cool | In a large bowl, whisk together olive oil, balsamic vinegar, salt, and pepper | Toss sliced apple and rocket (arugula) in the dressing until lightly coated | Arrange the dressed salad on serving plates | Top with crumbled goat cheese if using and the crispy Parmesan wafers | Serve immediately

ingredients: 2 cups all-purpose flour, 2 tsp baking powder, 1/2 tsp salt, 1 tsp ground cinnamon, 1/4 tsp ground nutmeg, 3/4 cup nonfat milk, 3 tbsp canola oil, 1/4 cup honey, 3/4 cup raisins
instructions: Preheat oven to 425Â°F (220Â°C) and coat baking sheets with cooking spray | In a large bowl, combine flour, baking powder, salt, cinnamon, and nutmeg â€” stir well | In a small bowl, combine milk, canola oil, and honey | Add the wet ingredients to the dry ingredients and stir just until moistened â€” do not overmix | Gently stir in raisins | Drop the batter by tablespoonfuls onto the prepared baking sheets, spacing them about 2 inches apart | Bake for 8-10 minutes or until lightly browned on top | Remove from baking sheets and transfer to wire racks to cool slightly | Serve warm or at room temperature

ingredients: 400g spaghetti or fettuccine, 3 tbsp butter, 1 medium onion (diced), 4 cloves garlic (minced), 200g fresh mushrooms (sliced), 2 cups cooked chicken or turkey (diced), 1 can (400g) cream of mushroom soup, 1 can (400g) cream of chicken soup, 1 can (400g) cream of celery soup, 1/2 cup heavy cream, 1/2 cup sour cream, 1/2 cup Parmesan cheese (grated), 2 1/2 cups cheddar cheese (shredded, divided), 1 cup frozen peas (optional), 1 jalapeÃ±o (minced, optional), salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Preheat oven to 350Â°F (175Â°C) and butter a 13 x 9-inch casserole dish | Cook pasta in a large pot of boiling water until al dente â€” do not overcook as it will cook more in the oven | Drain pasta and transfer to a large bowl | Add heavy cream, all three canned soups, cooked chicken or turkey, sour cream, Parmesan cheese, 1 1/2 cups of the cheddar cheese, and frozen peas if using | Toss well to combine | In a large skillet, melt butter over medium heat | Add sliced mushrooms and cook until all the liquid is released and evaporated, about 10 minutes | Add diced onions, minced garlic, and jalapeÃ±o if using | SautÃ© until onions are soft, about 5 minutes | Add the mushroom mixture to the pasta mixture | Using a wooden spoon, mix all ingredients together until well combined | Season with salt and pepper | Transfer to the prepared baking dish and spread evenly | Cover with foil and bake for 30-35 minutes until hot and bubbly | Uncover and sprinkle with the remaining 1 cup cheddar cheese | Return to oven and bake until cheese is melted, about 5-8 minutes | Serve hot

ingredients: 400g short pasta (fusilli or penne), 1/2 cup mayonnaise, 2 tbsp fresh lemon juice, 1 tsp lemon zest, 2 cans (200g each) tuna in olive oil (drained and flaked), 1 can (400g) white beans (drained and rinsed), 1/4 cup fresh basil (torn), 1/4 cup red onion (thinly sliced), salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Cook pasta in a large pot of salted boiling water until al dente | Drain and rinse under cold water to cool, then drain well | In a large bowl, whisk together mayonnaise, fresh lemon juice, and lemon zest until smooth | Add the cooled pasta, flaked tuna, white beans, torn basil, and sliced red onion | Toss gently to combine all ingredients evenly | Season with salt and black pepper to taste | Serve at room temperature or chilled

ingredients: 1 1/2 cups wheat flour, 1/2 cup flax seed meal, 1/2 cup oat bran, 1/2 cup brown sugar, 2 tsp baking powder, 1/2 tsp baking soda, 1/2 tsp salt, 1 tsp ground cinnamon, 1/2 cup grated carrot, 1/2 cup chocolate chips, 1/2 cup raisins, 3/4 cup milk, 1 large egg (beaten), 1 tsp vanilla extract
instructions: Preheat oven to 350Â°F (175Â°C) and line a muffin tin with paper liners | In a large bowl, mix together all the dry ingredients: wheat flour, flax seed meal, oat bran, brown sugar, baking powder, baking soda, salt, and cinnamon | Stir in grated carrot and raisins until evenly distributed | In a separate small bowl, combine milk, beaten egg, and vanilla extract | Pour the liquid ingredients into the dry ingredients and mix gently until just combined | Stir in chocolate chips and fold until all ingredients are incorporated â€” do not overmix | Divide batter evenly among the muffin cups, filling each about 3/4 full | Bake for 15 minutes until a toothpick inserted in the center comes out clean | Let cool in the pan for 5 minutes before transferring to a wire rack | Serve warm or at room temperature

ingredients: 12 vanilla wafer cookies, 16 oz cream cheese (softened), 1/2 cup granulated sugar, 2 tbsp amaretto liqueur or 1 tsp almond extract, 2 large eggs, 1/2 cup mini chocolate chips, 1/2 cup white chocolate chips
instructions: Preheat oven to 350Â°F (175Â°C) | Line 12 medium muffin cups with paper baking cups | Place one vanilla wafer flat side down in the bottom of each cup | In a medium bowl, beat softened cream cheese and sugar with an electric mixer on medium speed until light and fluffy | Beat in amaretto liqueur or almond extract until combined | Beat in eggs one at a time, mixing well after each addition | Fill each cup about 3/4 full with the cream cheese mixture | Sprinkle chocolate chips and white chocolate chips over the tops to your taste | Bake for 20-25 minutes or until the centers are set and firm | Immediately remove cheesecakes from the muffin pan to a wire rack | Cool for 15 minutes | Cover and refrigerate for at least 2 hours before eating â€” but no longer than 48 hours | Serve chilled

ingredients: For topping: 2 slices white bread (pulsed into crumbs), 2 tbsp unsalted butter (melted), 1/2 tsp salt, 1/4 tsp black pepper, 1 cup crispy fried onions. For casserole: 800g green beans (trimmed and cut), 2 tbsp salt (for blanching water), 3 tbsp unsalted butter, 250g white button mushrooms (sliced), 3 cloves garlic (minced), 3/4 tsp salt, 1/8 tsp black pepper, 3 tbsp all-purpose flour, 1 1/2 cups low-sodium chicken broth, 1 1/2 cups heavy cream
instructions: Make the topping: pulse bread, melted butter, salt, and pepper in a food processor until mixture resembles coarse crumbs, about ten 1-second pulses | Transfer to a large bowl and toss with crispy fried onions â€” set aside | Preheat oven to 425Â°F (220Â°C) and adjust oven rack to middle position | Fill a large bowl with ice water | Bring 4 quarts of water to a boil in a large Dutch oven | Add 2 tablespoons salt and green beans | Cook beans until bright green and crisp-tender, about 6 minutes | Drain beans in a colander and plunge immediately into the ice water to stop cooking | Spread beans on a paper towel-lined baking sheet to drain | Add butter to the now-empty Dutch oven and melt over medium-high heat until foaming subsides | Add sliced mushrooms, minced garlic, 3/4 teaspoon salt, and 1/8 teaspoon pepper | Cook until mushrooms release their moisture and the liquid evaporates, about 6 minutes | Add flour and cook for 1 minute, stirring constantly | Stir in chicken broth and bring to a simmer, stirring constantly | Add heavy cream, reduce heat to medium, and simmer until sauce is thickened and reduced to about 3 1/2 cups, about 12 minutes | Season with salt and pepper to taste | Add green beans to the sauce and stir until evenly coated | Arrange in an even layer in a 3-quart or 13 x 9-inch baking dish | Sprinkle with the topping and bake until top is golden brown and sauce is bubbling around the edges, about 15 minutes | Serve immediately

ingredients: 3 cups sushi rice (short-grain Japanese rice), 3 1/3 cups cold water, 1/2 cup rice vinegar, 1/4 cup granulated sugar, 1 tsp salt, 1 tbsp powdered dashi (optional)
instructions: Rinse the rice: put the rice in a large bowl and add enough cold water to half fill the bowl | Swirl the water around with the rice, scrunching the rice gently with your hands | Drain and repeat the rinsing process 3 or 4 times until the water runs mostly clear | Transfer the rinsed rice to a large saucepan | Pour in 3 1/3 cups of cold water and leave to soak for at least 30 minutes â€” the rice will become whiter and the water clear | Prepare the sushi vinegar: combine rice vinegar, sugar, salt, and powdered dashi (if using) in a small saucepan | Heat gently, stirring to dissolve the sugar and salt | Do not let the mixture boil as it will impair the flavor | Remove from heat and let cool completely | Cook the rice: place the lid securely on the saucepan and turn the heat to high | When the rice begins to boil, reduce the heat to low and simmer for 15 minutes â€” do not lift the lid at any point | After 15 minutes, turn off the heat and leave the rice to stand covered for another 15 minutes | Transfer the hot rice into a large wooden or glass bowl | Pour the cooled sushi vinegar evenly over the rice | Use a flat spatula in a cutting motion to gently fold the mixture into the rice â€” do not stir or mash | While folding, use your other hand to fan the rice to help it cool to room temperature | The finished rice should be shiny and sticky, with each grain separated | Use immediately or cover with a damp cloth to prevent it from drying out

ingredients: 400g penne pasta, 1 red bell pepper (diced), 1/2 medium onion (diced), 1 tbsp olive oil, 3 cups fresh spinach leaves, 4 slices bacon (cooked and crumbled), 1/2 cup feta cheese (crumbled), 1/4 cup sun-dried tomatoes in oil (drained and chopped), 1/4 cup olive oil, 2 tbsp cider vinegar, 1/4 tsp black pepper, 1/4 tsp salt
instructions: Cook pasta according to package directions until al dente | Meanwhile, in a large skillet, heat 1 tablespoon olive oil over medium heat | SautÃ© diced red pepper and onion for 3-4 minutes until tender | Drain pasta and place in a large serving bowl | Add the red pepper mixture, fresh spinach, crumbled bacon, feta cheese, and sun-dried tomatoes | In a jar with a tight-fitting lid, combine the 1/4 cup olive oil, cider vinegar, pepper, and salt â€” shake well to emulsify | Drizzle the dressing over the pasta and spinach mixture | Toss everything together until well coated and the spinach begins to wilt slightly from the heat of the pasta | Serve immediately

ingredients: 150g dried pasta (any shape), 1/2 medium onion (diced), 3 cloves garlic (minced), 1 tbsp light olive oil, 1/4 cup white wine, 1/4 cup chicken or vegetable broth, 1 cup broccoli florets, 2 tbsp Parmesan cheese (grated), 1 tbsp Romano cheese (grated), salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Cook pasta in salted boiling water until al dente, then drain and set aside | In a skillet, heat olive oil over medium heat | SautÃ© diced onion and minced garlic until soft and fragrant, about 3-4 minutes | Add white wine and broth, then add broccoli florets | Cover and cook for 3 minutes until broccoli is bright green and tender-crisp | Add the cooked pasta to the skillet with the broccoli mixture | Toss everything together and cook until both are heated through, about 1-2 minutes | Season with salt and pepper to taste | Transfer to a serving plate and sprinkle generously with Parmesan and Romano cheeses | Serve immediately

ingredients: 4 ripe Hass avocados, 1/2 cup sweet onion (finely diced), 1/4 cup fresh cilantro leaves (chopped), 2 tbsp mayonnaise, 2 tbsp sour cream, 2 tbsp fresh lime juice, 2 Roma tomatoes (diced), 1/2 tsp kosher salt, 1/4 tsp black pepper, 1/4 tsp ground cumin, 1/4 tsp chili powder, 1/4 tsp garlic powder, 1/4 tsp onion powder, 1/4 tsp sweet Hungarian paprika (plus extra for garnish), tortilla chips for serving
instructions: In a mortar and pestle or small bowl, grind together salt, black pepper, cumin, chili powder, garlic powder, onion powder, and paprika | Cut avocados in half, remove pits, and scoop the flesh into a large bowl | Add the ground spice mixture to the avocados | Add diced onion, chopped cilantro, mayonnaise, sour cream, and fresh lime juice | Mash together partially with a fork, leaving at least half of the avocado in good-sized chunks for texture | Gently fold in diced Roma tomatoes | Cover tightly with plastic wrap pressed directly onto the surface of the guacamole to prevent browning | Refrigerate overnight to allow flavors to meld | Before serving, taste and adjust seasonings | Sprinkle with a bit more paprika and garnish with fresh cilantro leaves and diced red onion on top | Serve with tortilla chips

ingredients: 500g frozen edamame in pods, 1 tbsp coarse sea salt, 2 tbsp reduced-sodium soy sauce, 1 tbsp rice vinegar, 1 tsp sesame oil, 1 tsp honey, 1 clove garlic (minced), 2 scallions (thinly sliced)
instructions: Place the coarse sea salt into a small ungreased skillet | Set over medium heat and cook, tossing occasionally, until the salt turns tan-colored, about 6-7 minutes | Set aside to cool | Bring a pot of water to a boil | Add frozen edamame and cook until tender, about 4 minutes â€” cook out the raw taste but do not let them get mushy | Immediately transfer edamame with a slotted spoon to a bowl of ice water to stop cooking | Drain well and pat completely dry with paper towels | Toss the edamame with the prepared toasted salt | Make the dipping sauce: whisk together soy sauce, rice vinegar, sesame oil, honey, minced garlic, and sliced scallions until well combined | Serve edamame in a bowl with the dipping sauce in a small bowl on the side

ingredients: For crust: 1 package (250g) Lorna Doone shortbread cookies (finely crushed), 1/4 cup unsalted butter (melted). For filling: 4 packages (250g each) cream cheese (softened), 1 1/2 cups granulated sugar, 3 tbsp all-purpose flour, 5 large eggs, 2 large egg yolks, 1 tsp vanilla extract, 1/4 cup heavy cream, 1 tsp orange zest (optional), 1 tsp lemon zest (optional)
instructions: Preheat oven to 400Â°F (200Â°C) | Make the crust: finely crush the entire package of cookies, then mix in melted butter â€” this can be done in a food processor on pulse | Butter the sides of a 9-inch springform pan | Press the cookie mixture firmly into the bottom of the pan â€” do not bake the crust | Make the filling: beat together softened cream cheese, sugar, flour, and zests (if using) until smooth | Add the 5 eggs and 2 egg yolks one at a time, beating well after each addition | Add vanilla to the heavy cream, then add the cream to the cheese mixture | Beat on low speed until all ingredients are incorporated â€” do not overbeat | Place the springform pan in the center of a shallow baking pan to catch any drips | Pour filling into the crust â€” it will be very full | Place in the middle of the oven and bake for 12 minutes at 400Â°F | Reduce oven temperature to 250Â°F (120Â°C) and continue baking for approximately 1 hour to 1 hour 15 minutes until the center is mostly firm but still has a slight jiggle | A slight jiggle is good â€” overbaking causes cracks | After removing from oven, run a knife around the edge of the pan and cool on a wire rack for 6 hours | Remove the side of the springform pan and transfer to a flat plate | Refrigerate for up to 2 weeks, but best served after returning to room temperature

ingredients: 6 cups beef broth, 3 tbsp hoisin sauce, 2 tbsp barbecue sauce, 2 tbsp crushed peanuts, 1 stalk lemongrass (bruised and chopped), 2 tbsp tomato paste, 400g beef sirloin (thinly sliced), 1 English cucumber (julienned), 2 cups shredded cabbage, 1 cup bean sprouts, 3 green onions (sliced), 200g rice noodles, fresh cilantro and lime wedges for serving
instructions: In a large pot, combine beef broth, hoisin sauce, barbecue sauce, crushed peanuts, lemongrass, and tomato paste | Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer for 15 minutes to allow flavors to meld | Add thinly sliced beef and cook for 2-3 minutes until just cooked through | Meanwhile, prepare the vegetables: toss together shredded cabbage, julienned cucumber, and bean sprouts | Cook rice noodles in hot water according to package directions, then drain | Divide the vegetable mixture among individual serving bowls | Place cooked noodles on top of the vegetables in each bowl | Ladle the hot soup with beef over the noodles and vegetables | Sprinkle with sliced green onions, fresh cilantro, and serve with lime wedges on the side

recipe_name: Pork Ribs with Red Wine Vinegar Sauce
ingredients: For sauce: 1/2 cup red wine vinegar, 1/3 cup ketchup, 2 tbsp soy sauce, 2 tbsp honey, 3 cloves garlic (minced), 1 tsp dried thyme, 1/2 tsp Tabasco sauce, 1/4 tsp fresh ground black pepper, 1/2 tsp chili powder. For ribs: 1.5 kg country-style pork ribs, 1 tsp kosher salt, 1/2 tsp fresh ground black pepper
instructions: Make the sauce: in a medium saucepan, combine red wine vinegar, ketchup, soy sauce, honey, minced garlic, dried thyme, Tabasco sauce, black pepper, and chili powder | Bring to a boil, then decrease heat and simmer for 15 minutes, stirring occasionally | Remove from heat and let cool to room temperature | Pour some of the sauce into a small bowl to use for basting the ribs | Let the ribs stand at room temperature for 20-30 minutes before grilling | Season ribs generously with kosher salt and black pepper | Prepare your grill for indirect medium heat (about 350Â°F / 175Â°C) | Grill ribs over indirect heat for 1 to 1 1/2 hours until the meat is tender, turning once halfway through grilling time | During the last 20 minutes of grilling, baste the ribs with the reserved small bowl of sauce, turning and basting several times | Serve warm with the remaining sauce on the side

ingredients: 400g rotini pasta, 1 1/2 cups milk, 1 jar (400g) Alfredo sauce, 3 tbsp fresh basil (chopped, divided), 1 1/2 cups provolone cheese (shredded), 1 cup cherry tomatoes (halved, divided), 1/4 tsp red pepper flakes, 1/4 tsp fresh black pepper, 1/4 cup breadcrumbs
instructions: Preheat oven to 350Â°F (175Â°C) and grease a 2-quart casserole dish | Cook rotini pasta in a large pot of salted boiling water until al dente, then drain | In a medium bowl, stir milk into Alfredo sauce until smooth | Stir in 2 tablespoons of the chopped basil, shredded provolone cheese, and 1 cup of the halved cherry tomatoes | Add the cooked pasta and toss well to combine | Pour the mixture into the prepared casserole dish and spread evenly | Sprinkle the remaining tomatoes on top | Bake uncovered for 30 to 35 minutes until hot and bubbly | In a small bowl, mix breadcrumbs with the remaining 1 tablespoon basil | Sprinkle over the top and serve immediately

ingredients: 4 boneless skinless chicken breasts, 2 cups salsa (red or green), 1 can (400g) black beans (drained and rinsed), 1 cup frozen corn (optional), 1 cup shredded Mexican blend cheese (optional), steamed white rice for serving
instructions: Preheat oven to 350Â°F (175Â°C) | Place chicken breasts in a single layer in a baking dish | Pour salsa and drained black beans over the top of the chicken, spreading evenly | Add frozen corn if using | Cover with foil and bake for 45-60 minutes depending on the size of the chicken breasts, until chicken is cooked through and reaches 165Â°F (74Â°C) | If desired, uncover and sprinkle with cheese during the last 5 minutes of baking | Serve hot over steamed white rice with the salsa and bean sauce spooned over the top

ingredients: 4 cups whole milk, 2 tbsp brown sugar (divided), 2 tbsp Grand Marnier liqueur, peel of 2 oranges (removed in strips), 100g bittersweet chocolate (chopped), 1 tbsp instant espresso powder, 1 tbsp unsweetened cocoa powder, 1/2 cup heavy whipping cream
instructions: Make the Grand Marnier whipped cream: whisk heavy cream, 1 tablespoon brown sugar, and Grand Marnier in a medium bowl until soft peaks form | Cover and refrigerate until ready to serve | Using a vegetable peeler, remove the peel from the oranges in strips, reserving the oranges for another use | Add orange peel strips and milk to a medium saucepan | Bring just to a simmer over medium heat â€” do not boil | Add chopped chocolate, espresso powder, cocoa powder, and remaining 1 tablespoon brown sugar | Bring just back to a simmer, whisking constantly to melt the chocolate | Remove from heat and strain through a fine mesh sieve into a clean saucepan, discarding the orange peel | Reheat gently if needed | Ladle the hot mocha into 4 mugs | Top each with a generous dollop of the Grand Marnier whipped cream | Serve immediately

ingredients: 500g lean ground beef, 1/2 cup uncooked minute rice, 1/4 cup applesauce, 1/2 medium onion (finely diced), 1 tsp salt, 1/4 tsp black pepper, 1 cup ketchup, 1/2 cup water, steamed rice or mashed potatoes for serving
instructions: Preheat oven to 350Â°F (175Â°C) | In a large bowl, mix together ground beef, uncooked rice, applesauce, diced onion, salt, and pepper until well combined | Roll the mixture into 1 1/2-inch balls and place them in a single layer in a 9 x 13 baking dish | In a separate bowl, mix together ketchup and water until smooth | Pour the ketchup mixture evenly over the meatballs | Bake for 1 hour until meatballs are cooked through and rice is tender â€” the rice will poke out like little porcupine quills | Serve hot with steamed rice or mashed potatoes and spoon the pan sauce over the top

ingredients: For crust: 1 1/2 cups crushed tortilla chips, 1/4 cup unsalted butter (melted). For filling: 3 packages (250g each) cream cheese (softened), 3 large eggs, 1 tsp chili powder, 1/2 tsp ground cumin, 1 tsp Worcestershire sauce, 1/4 tsp salt, 3 green onions (minced), 1 cup cooked chicken (shredded), 1 can (200g) diced green chilies, 1 cup Monterey Jack cheese (shredded). For topping: 1 cup sour cream, 1/2 tsp seasoned salt, picante sauce for serving
instructions: Preheat oven to 350Â°F (175Â°C) | Combine crushed tortilla chips and melted butter, mixing well | Press the mixture on the bottom and 1 inch up the sides of a 9-inch springform pan | Set aside | Beat softened cream cheese with an electric mixer at high speed until light and fluffy | Add the eggs one at a time, beating well after each addition | Stir in chili powder, cumin, Worcestershire sauce, salt, and minced green onions | Pour half of the cream cheese mixture into the prepared crust | Sprinkle with shredded chicken, diced green chilies, and Monterey Jack cheese | Carefully pour the remaining cream cheese mixture on top | Bake for 10 minutes at 350Â°F, then reduce heat to 300Â°F (150Â°C) and bake for an additional hour or until set | Cool completely on a wire rack | Combine sour cream and seasoned salt, then spread evenly over the top of the cooled cheesecake | Cover and chill for at least 8 hours or overnight | Just before serving, slice and serve with picante sauce on the side

ingredients: 4 ripe bananas (sliced into rounds), 3 tbsp vegetable oil, 1 medium onion (diced), 1 cup wheat germ or toasted cassava flour (farofa), salt to taste, fresh parsley (chopped, for garnish)
instructions: In a large skillet, heat vegetable oil over medium heat | SautÃ© the banana slices until they turn golden on both sides, about 2-3 minutes per side â€” remove with a slotted spoon and set aside | In the same oil, sautÃ© the diced onion until translucent, about 4-5 minutes | Return the bananas to the pan with the onions | Reduce heat to medium-low and gently add the wheat germ (or farofa) to the mixture | Cook, stirring gently, until the wheat germ is lightly browned and toasted, about 3-4 minutes | If the mixture becomes noticeably dry, add a small amount of oil | Season with salt to taste | Garnish with fresh chopped parsley and serve hot as a side dish

ingredients: 1 large spaghetti squash, 500g boneless skinless chicken breasts (cut into 1/2-inch cubes), 1 tbsp cornstarch, 3 tbsp soy sauce (divided), 2 tbsp dry sherry, 1 tbsp sugar, 1 tbsp rice vinegar, 1/2 tsp red pepper flakes, 3 tbsp vegetable oil, 2 green onions (sliced), 1 leek (white part only, sliced), 1 tbsp gingerroot (grated), steamed rice for serving
instructions: Cut the spaghetti squash in half lengthwise and scoop out the seeds | Place cut-side down on a baking sheet and bake at 375Â°F (190Â°C) for 35-40 minutes until the fibers are tender and separate easily when scraped with a fork | Cut chicken into 1/2-inch cubes and mix in a bowl with 1 tablespoon soy sauce and cornstarch to marinate for 10 minutes | In a small bowl, mix together the remaining 2 tablespoons soy sauce, dry sherry, sugar, and rice vinegar â€” set aside | Heat oil in a wok over high heat (375Â°F if using a thermometer) | When hot, add red pepper flakes and stir until they turn dark, about 30 seconds | Add the marinated chicken and stir-fry for 2-3 minutes until almost cooked through | Remove chicken with a strainer and set aside | Add green onions, sliced leek, and grated gingerroot to the wok â€” stir-fry for about 1 minute | Return the chicken to the wok and stir-fry for another couple of minutes | Add the sherry-soy sauce mixture â€” bring to a low boil for about a minute | Remove from heat and serve immediately over steamed rice or with the baked spaghetti squash strands

ingredients: 500g salmon fillets (cut into 20 squares, about 2 inches each), 20 round rice paper sheets, 20 fresh cilantro leaves, 4 cloves garlic, 1/4 cup cashews, 1 cup fresh cilantro, 1/4 cup fresh basil, 1/4 tsp salt, 2 tbsp olive oil, vegetable oil for frying
instructions: Make the pesto: put garlic, cashews, cilantro, basil, salt, and olive oil in a food processor â€” process until a smooth paste forms | Cut salmon into 20 even squares, about 2 inches each | Fill a shallow bowl with warm water | Dip each rice paper wrapper into the warm water briefly to soften | Place a cilantro leaf in the center of each wrapper | Sandwich a piece of salmon with a small dollop of pesto | Place the salmon on top of the cilantro leaf | Fold the sides of the wrapper over to form a neat square packet, sealing the edges | Heat vegetable oil in a skillet over medium heat | Cook the packets in batches, sealed side down, for several minutes until golden brown on the bottom | Carefully flip and cook the other side until golden | Remove packets and place in a steamer â€” steam for 4 to 6 minutes until the salmon is cooked through | May be assembled ahead of time and steamed just before serving

ingredients: 1/2 cup boiling water, 1/4 cup sun-dried tomatoes (chopped), 2 tbsp butter, 1 tbsp olive oil, 1/2 medium onion (diced), 1 cup Arborio rice, 3 cups chicken broth, 1/2 tsp salt, 1/4 tsp black pepper, 1 can (100g) diced green chilies, 1/4 cup Parmesan cheese (grated)
instructions: Combine boiling water and sun-dried tomatoes in a small bowl â€” cover and let stand for 10 minutes, then drain and set aside | Combine butter and olive oil in an 8-inch square microwave-safe baking dish â€” microwave at HIGH for 2 minutes until melted | Stir in diced onion â€” microwave at HIGH for 3 minutes until softened | Stir in Arborio rice â€” microwave at HIGH for 2 minutes, stirring once | Stir in chicken broth, salt, and pepper â€” microwave at HIGH for 9 minutes, stirring once halfway through | Stir in the reserved sun-dried tomatoes and diced green chilies â€” microwave at HIGH for 8 minutes until rice is tender and creamy | Remove from microwave and stir in grated Parmesan cheese | Let stand for 2 minutes before serving

ingredients: 4 cups water (divided), 2 tbsp loose black tea leaves or 4 tea bags, 2 tbsp granulated sugar (divided), 2 tbsp fresh lemon juice, 6 fresh mint leaves (plus extra for garnish), 1 tbsp honey, ice cubes, lemon slices for garnish
instructions: Bring 2 cups of water to a boil in a small saucepan | Remove from heat and add tea leaves (or tea bags) and 2 teaspoons of the sugar | Cover and set aside to steep for 5 minutes | Strain the tea through a fine mesh sieve, discarding the tea leaves or bags | Add some cold water to the brew if needed to make about 3 cups | Add fresh lemon juice, mint leaves, honey, and the remaining sugar to taste | Stir until the sugar dissolves completely | Serve chilled in tall glasses over ice cubes | Garnish with lemon slices and a few fresh mint leaves

ingredients: For filling: 2 tbsp butter, 1 medium onion (diced), 2 carrots (diced), 2 celery stalks (diced), 2 cups cooked chicken (shredded), 1 cup frozen peas, 1/3 cup all-purpose flour, 2 cups chicken broth, 1/2 cup heavy cream, 1 tsp dried thyme, salt and pepper. For topping: 1 sheet puff pastry or double pie crust, 1 egg (beaten for egg wash)
instructions: Preheat oven to 400Â°F (200Â°C) | Melt butter in a large skillet over medium heat | SautÃ© diced onion, carrots, and celery for 6-8 minutes until softened | Sprinkle flour over the vegetables and stir for 1 minute | Gradually pour in chicken broth while stirring constantly | Add heavy cream and thyme, cooking until the sauce thickens, about 5 minutes | Stir in shredded chicken and frozen peas | Season with salt and pepper | Pour the filling into a 9-inch pie dish or casserole | Top with puff pastry or pie crust, crimping the edges and cutting several slits in the top to vent | Brush with beaten egg for a golden finish | Bake for 30-35 minutes until the crust is golden brown and the filling is bubbling | Let cool for 10 minutes before serving

ingredients: 12 large white mushrooms (stems removed, 4 stems reserved), 4 oz low-fat cream cheese (softened), 1/4 medium onion (finely diced), 3 slices bacon, salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Preheat oven to 350Â°F (175Â°C) | Remove stems from all mushrooms â€” reserve 4 of the stems and finely chop them | Clean mushroom caps and set aside | Finely chop the onion and the 4 reserved mushroom stems | Cook bacon in a skillet until crisp, then remove and drain on paper towels, reserving the bacon grease | Cook the chopped onion and mushroom stems in the bacon grease until tender, about 4-5 minutes | Crumble the crisp bacon into the softened cream cheese | Stir in the sautÃ©ed onion and stems until well combined | Season with salt and pepper | Scoop some of the mixture into each mushroom cap, mounding slightly | Place stuffed mushrooms on a baking sheet | Bake for about 10-15 minutes until mushrooms are tender | Switch to broil for the final 1-2 minutes to brown the tops | Serve warm

ingredients: 30ml Kahlua coffee liqueur, 30ml amaretto, 30ml Baileys Irish Cream, 120ml cold milk, ice cubes
instructions: Fill a rocks glass or highball glass halfway with ice cubes | Pour in Kahlua, amaretto, and Baileys Irish Cream over the ice | Fill the glass the rest of the way with cold milk | Stir gently to combine | Add more alcohol for desired strength â€” 3 tablespoons equals approximately 1 shot | Serve immediately and enjoy

ingredients: 500g cleaned honeycomb tripe (cut into strips), 2 tbsp sunflower oil, 2 medium onions (diced), 4 cloves garlic (minced), 2 carrots (diced), 1 celery root (diced), 1 bell pepper (diced), 100g bacon or pancetta (diced), 1 tbsp sweet red paprika, 2 tbsp tomato puree, 1 bay leaf, 2 cups beef broth, 1/4 cup Parmesan cheese (grated), salt and pepper to taste, crusty bread for serving
instructions: In a large saucepan, heat sunflower oil over medium heat | Add diced onion, minced garlic, diced celery root, diced carrots, diced bell pepper, and diced bacon â€” sautÃ© for about 3 minutes until softened | Add the tripe strips, sweet red paprika, tomato puree, and bay leaf â€” stir well to combine | Add beef broth, cover the pan, and bring to a boil | Lower the heat and simmer over low heat for 20 minutes until the tripe is tender | Remove the bay leaf and season with salt and pepper to taste | Serve hot in bowls sprinkled generously with grated Parmesan cheese | Serve with crusty bread on the side for dipping

ingredients: For steak: 500g flank steak, 3 tbsp fish sauce, 1 tbsp fresh ginger (grated), 3 cloves garlic (minced), 2 tbsp soy sauce, 1 tbsp sugar. For dressing: 1/4 cup fresh lime juice, 2 tbsp water, 1 tbsp sugar, 2 tbsp fish sauce, 1/2 tsp red pepper flakes, 2 shallots (thinly sliced). For salad: 200g thin rice noodles, 2 Granny Smith apples (cut into matchsticks), 4 cups Asian salad greens, 1/4 cup fresh mint leaves, 1/4 cup roasted peanuts (chopped)
instructions: Marinate the steak: whisk together fish sauce, grated ginger, minced garlic, soy sauce, and sugar until sugar dissolves | Pour marinade into a large sealable plastic bag | Pat steak dry and place in the bag, then press out excess air and seal | Turn bag to coat meat, then refrigerate at least 4 hours and up to 8 hours | Bring steak to room temperature 30 minutes before grilling | Prepare a grill for medium-hot charcoal or moderate heat for gas | Remove steak from marinade, discarding the marinade, and pat dry with paper towels | Grill over direct heat, turning once, until medium-rare, about 12 to 14 minutes total | Transfer steak to a cutting board and let rest uncovered for about 15 minutes | Make the dressing: whisk together lime juice, water, sugar, fish sauce, and red pepper flakes until sugar dissolves, then stir in sliced shallots | Cook rice noodles in boiling salted water until just tender, 4 to 5 minutes â€” drain, rinse under cold water, and drain well | Toss noodles with 1/2 cup of the dressing | Cut apple into thin matchsticks | Combine apples, Asian greens, and mint in a large bowl â€” add 1/2 cup dressing and toss well | Thinly slice steak across the grain | Arrange noodles on a large platter, mound the greens on top, and arrange steak slices on the greens | Sprinkle with chopped peanuts | Serve at room temperature with remaining dressing on the side

ingredients: 6 large eggs, 2 tbsp unsalted butter (melted), 4 plum tomatoes (diced), 1/2 medium onion (diced), 1 tbsp red wine vinegar, salt and black pepper to taste, fresh parsley for garnish
instructions: Hard-cook the eggs: place eggs in a saucepan and cover with cold water | Bring to a boil and cook for 10 minutes | Drain and rinse under cold water to make them easier to peel | Peel eggs and cut in half lengthwise | Remove yolks and place them in a small bowl | Combine yolks with melted butter and season with salt | Fill the egg white halves with the yolk mixture and place them in a baking dish | Place eggs in a 350Â°F (175Â°C) oven for 8 minutes until warmed through | Meanwhile, make the sauce: in a saucepan over medium heat, cook diced tomatoes and diced onion until the onion is tender and a rich tomato sauce forms, about 10-12 minutes | Season with salt, pepper, and a splash of red wine vinegar | Pour the tomato sauce over the warm eggs | Garnish with fresh parsley and serve immediately

ingredients: 1/4 cup water, 1/4 cup bourbon, 1/4 cup soy sauce, 2 tbsp honey, 1 tsp dry mustard, 1/2 tsp garlic powder, 4 sirloin steaks (about 200g each, 1-inch thick)
instructions: Prepare the marinade: pour water, bourbon, soy sauce, honey, dry mustard, and garlic powder into a large zip-top bag | Seal the bag and lay it flat on the counter | Massage the bag with your fingers to dissolve the mustard and garlic powder and mix all ingredients well | Add steaks to the bag and seal | Refrigerate overnight or for at least 6 hours, turning the bag occasionally | About an hour before grilling, remove the bag from the refrigerator and place it on the counter â€” turn after 30 minutes | Remove steaks from the bag and discard the marinade | Preheat grill to medium-high heat | For 1-inch steaks, grill about 10 minutes per side or until internal temperature reaches 140-145Â°F (60-63Â°C) for medium | Remove from grill and cover steaks loosely with foil for about 10 minutes before serving | Serve as whole steaks or slice thinly across the grain before serving

ingredients: 4 slices thick bread, 4 large eggs, 2 tbsp butter, 1/4 cup cheddar cheese (shredded, optional), salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Heat a large square skillet or griddle over medium heat | Using a cookie cutter or a small glass, cut out the center of each slice of bread â€” reserve the cutouts | Melt butter on the skillet and place the bread slices on the hot surface | Crack one egg directly into the cutout of each bread slice â€” the egg will cook and attach to the toast | Cook for 1-2 minutes until the bottom is golden and the egg is set on the bottom | Carefully flip with a spatula and cook the other side for 1-2 minutes more, depending on how you like your eggs | If desired, top with a little shredded cheese after flipping | Toast the reserved bread cutouts in the pan alongside the eggs | Season with salt and pepper and serve immediately

ingredients: 1 large butternut squash (halved, seeds removed), 3 tbsp butter, 1 medium onion (diced), 2 tbsp dried shallots, 3 cloves garlic (minced), 2 medium russet potatoes (peeled and diced), 4 cups low-sodium chicken broth, 1/4 tsp cayenne pepper, 1/4 tsp ground allspice, 1/4 tsp ground nutmeg, 1/2 tsp ground ginger, 1/4 tsp ground black pepper, 1 tbsp apple cider vinegar, 1/4 cup white wine, 1/2 cup water, salt to taste
instructions: Preheat oven to 375Â°F (190Â°C) | Pour a thin layer of water into the bottom of a cookie sheet with sides or jelly roll pan | Place the squash halves cut-side down on the pan | Bake for 40 minutes until the squash is tender | Remove from oven, let cool slightly, then scoop out the flesh and cut into large pieces â€” set aside | Melt butter in a large stock pot over medium heat | Add diced onion, dried shallots, and minced garlic â€” sautÃ© for 5 minutes until tender | Pour in chicken broth and add diced potatoes | Increase heat and bring to a boil, then reduce heat to medium-high and boil for 20 minutes until potatoes are tender | Add the cooked squash and stir until well mixed | Using a handheld immersion blender, purÃ©e the soup until completely smooth â€” or cool slightly and blend in batches in a food processor | Season the soup with cayenne pepper, allspice, nutmeg, ginger, and black pepper | Add apple cider vinegar, white wine, and water â€” stir well | Taste and adjust seasoning with salt as needed | Ladle into bowls and serve hot

ingredients: For dough: 2 cups whole milk, 1/2 cup vegetable oil, 1/2 cup granulated sugar, 2 1/4 tsp active dry yeast, 9 cups all-purpose flour (divided), 1 tsp baking powder, 1/2 tsp baking soda, 1 tsp salt. For filling: 1/2 cup unsalted butter (melted), 1 cup granulated sugar, 2 tbsp ground cinnamon. For glaze: 2 cups powdered sugar, 1 tsp maple extract, 1/2 cup whole milk, 1/4 cup unsalted butter (melted), 2 tbsp brewed coffee, pinch of salt
