instructions: In a large soup pot, mix milk, vegetable oil, and sugar | Scald the mixture by heating until just before the boiling point â€” turn off heat and let cool for 45 minutes to 1 hour | When the mixture is lukewarm to warm but NOT hot, sprinkle in the yeast | Let sit for a minute so the yeast gets warm and activated | Add 8 cups of all-purpose flour and stir together | Cover and let sit for at least an hour until the dough has risen | Add 1 more cup of flour, baking powder, baking soda, and salt â€” stir together | At this point the dough can be refrigerated overnight or used immediately | Sprinkle a work surface generously with flour | Take half the dough and form a rough rectangle, then roll thin while maintaining a rectangular shape | Drizzle melted butter generously over the dough | Sprinkle sugar over the butter, followed by a generous sprinkling of cinnamon | Starting at the opposite end, begin rolling the dough in a neat line toward you, keeping the roll relatively tight | Pinch the seam to seal | Spread 1 tablespoon melted butter in each of 7 round foil cake or pie pans | Cut rolls approximately 3/4 to 1 inch thick and place in the buttered pans | Repeat with remaining dough â€” recipe makes approximately 7 pans (about 56 rolls) | Let rolls sit for 20 to 30 minutes to rise | Preheat oven to 400Â°F (200Â°C) and bake for 15 to 18 minutes until light golden brown | Meanwhile, make the glaze: combine powdered sugar, maple extract, milk, melted butter, brewed coffee, and a pinch of salt â€” stir until thick but pourable | Generously drizzle the glaze over warm rolls as soon as they come out of the oven | Serve warm

ingredients: 1/2 cup unsalted butter (softened), 1 1/2 cups white sugar (divided), 1 cup all-purpose flour, 2 tsp baking powder, 1/4 tsp salt, 3/4 cup whole milk, 1 can (825g) sliced peaches in juice (juice reserved), 1/2 tsp ground cinnamon, 2 tbsp brown sugar
instructions: Preheat oven to 375Â°F (190Â°C) and butter an 8x8-inch baking dish | Cream softened butter with 1/2 cup of the white sugar until light and fluffy | In a separate bowl, combine flour, baking powder, and salt | Add the dry mixture to the creamed mixture alternately with the milk, mixing well until a smooth batter forms | Pour the batter into the prepared baking dish and spread evenly | Top with peach slices, arranging them evenly over the batter | Pour all of the reserved peach juice evenly over the peaches | Sprinkle the remaining 1 cup white sugar, brown sugar, and cinnamon over the top | Bake for 45 minutes until the top is golden brown and the cobbler is bubbly | Let cool for 10 minutes before serving | Serve warm with vanilla ice cream or whipped cream

ingredients: For cake: 3 ripe Bosc pears (peeled, halved, and cored), 3/4 cup unsalted butter (divided), 1/2 cup brown sugar, 3/4 cup granulated sugar, 1 large egg, 1 tsp vanilla extract, 1 1/2 tsp baking powder, 1/4 tsp salt, 1 1/2 cups all-purpose flour, 2/3 cup whole milk. For orange butter sauce: 1/2 cup orange juice, 1 tbsp cornstarch, 1/4 cup sugar, 2 tbsp unsalted butter, 1/4 tsp ground ginger
instructions: Preheat oven to 350Â°F (175Â°C) | Peel, halve, and core the pears â€” set aside | Place 1/4 cup of the butter into a 10 x 6-inch baking pan and put it in the oven as it preheats until the butter is melted | Remove from oven and sprinkle brown sugar evenly over the melted butter | Arrange the pear halves cut-side down in a single layer over the brown sugar | In a large bowl, cream the remaining 1/2 cup butter with the granulated sugar, egg, and vanilla until light and fluffy | Mix in the baking powder and salt | Add the flour alternately with the milk, mixing until the batter is smooth | Pour the batter evenly over the pears | Bake for 45 minutes or until a wooden skewer inserted into the center of the cake comes out clean | While the cake bakes, make the orange butter sauce: combine orange juice, cornstarch, sugar, butter, and ginger in a small saucepan | Heat to boiling over medium-high heat, stirring constantly | Cook, stirring, until thickened â€” remove from heat | When cake is done, invert while still warm onto a serving plate | Serve warm with the orange butter sauce drizzled over the top

ingredients: 30g dried mushrooms (porcini or mixed), 1 cup boiling water, 2 tbsp olive oil, 2 tbsp butter, 1 large onion (diced), 500g fresh mushrooms (sliced), 4 cups chicken or vegetable stock, 1 tbsp dried parsley, 1/2 tsp salt, 1/4 tsp black pepper, 1 tbsp balsamic vinegar (for drizzling)
instructions: In a medium bowl, cover the dried mushrooms with the boiling water and let soak for 30 minutes | In a large pot, heat olive oil over medium heat | SautÃ© diced onion for 5 minutes until softened but not browned | Add butter and fresh sliced mushrooms â€” sautÃ© for about 8 minutes until mushrooms release their liquid and begin to brown | Add the soaked dried mushrooms along with their soaking liquid (strain if sandy), chicken stock, and dried parsley | Bring the soup to a gentle simmer and cook uncovered for about 1 hour, allowing flavors to concentrate | Taste after 1 hour â€” if the soup needs more depth, cook a bit longer to reduce further | Season with salt and pepper to taste | PurÃ©e the soup using an immersion blender, or cool slightly and blend in batches in a food processor or regular blender until smooth | Return to the pot and reheat if necessary | Ladle into individual bowls and drizzle each serving with a small amount of balsamic vinegar | Serve hot

ingredients: For stuffing: 1 whole pheasant (cleaned), 1 medium onion (diced), 2 tbsp butter, 1 carrot (diced), 1 celery stalk (diced), 2 tbsp fresh parsley (chopped), salt and pepper. For dough: 2 cups all-purpose flour, 1/2 tsp salt, 2/3 cup shortening, 1/3 cup cold water. For serving: giblet gravy
instructions: Rinse the inside and outside of the pheasant several times with warm water and drain well | Salt the inside cavity | Cook giblets separately if desired for gravy | Make the stuffing: sautÃ© diced onion in heated butter until softened, about 4-5 minutes | Add diced carrot, celery, and parsley â€” toss to mix well | Fill the cavity of the pheasant with the stuffing and truss (tie legs together with kitchen twine) | Make the dough blanket: sift together flour and salt | Cut in shortening with a pastry blender or two knives until the mixture resembles rice grains | Add cold water gradually, stirring to make a dough soft enough to roll | Roll out on a lightly floured surface into a rectangle about 1/8 to 1/4 inch thick, about 15 by 10 inches in size | Wrap the dough around the stuffed pheasant, completely covering it | Moisten the edges of the dough with water and pinch together to seal | Place the dough-wrapped pheasant breast-side up on a trivet in a shallow roasting pan | Roast uncovered in a 350Â°F (175Â°C) oven for 1 1/2 to 2 1/2 hours until fully cooked | Remove from oven and let rest for 10 minutes | Break away the crusty golden brown dough blanket in pieces | Serve the pheasant with the stuffing, pieces of crust, and giblet gravy on the side

ingredients: 1 1/2 cups all-purpose flour, 1/2 cup whole wheat flour, 1 tsp baking soda, 1/2 tsp sea salt, 1/2 cup walnuts (chopped, divided), 1/2 cup unsalted butter (softened), 3/4 cup brown sugar, 2 large eggs, 1/2 cup sourdough starter discard, 1/4 cup honey, 3 ripe bananas (mashed), 2 tbsp extra virgin olive oil, 1 tsp vanilla extract, 1 tbsp lemon zest
instructions: Preheat oven to 350Â°F (176Â°C) and grease a 9 x 5-inch baking pan | In a large mixing bowl, combine all-purpose flour, whole wheat flour, baking soda, and salt | In a small bowl, mix a handful of chopped walnuts with a few pinches of sugar â€” set aside for topping | In another bowl or stand mixer, cream softened butter and brown sugar until fluffy | Add eggs one at a time, scraping down the sides of the bowl occasionally | Add sourdough starter discard, honey, mashed bananas, olive oil, and vanilla â€” mix well | Slowly add the flour mixture, pausing to scrape down the sides if necessary | By hand, fold in the remaining walnuts (except the topping) and lemon zest | Pour batter into the prepared pan and smooth the top with a spatula | Sprinkle the reserved sugared walnuts over the top | Bake for 55-65 minutes until the internal temperature in the center reaches 200-205Â°F (93-96Â°C) | Let cool in the pan for 10 minutes, then gently remove onto a wire rack to cool completely

ingredients: 1 1/2 cups whole wheat flour, 1/2 cup brown sugar, 1/2 cup unsweetened applesauce, 1/4 cup canola oil, 1 tsp baking soda, 1 tsp ground cinnamon, 1/2 cup raisins, 1 large egg, 1/4 cup milk
instructions: Preheat oven to 350Â°F (175Â°C) and grease a muffin tin | Mix all ingredients together in the order listed, stirring just until combined â€” do not overbeat | Spoon batter into the greased muffin tins, filling each cup about 2/3 full | Bake for 19 minutes until a toothpick inserted in the center comes out clean | Let cool in the pan for 5 minutes before transferring to a wire rack | Serve warm or at room temperature

ingredients: 750ml bottle rosÃ© wine, 1 cup fresh strawberries (hulled and sliced), 2 tbsp granulated sugar, 60ml lemon-flavored vodka, 1 tbsp grenadine, fresh strawberries and lemon slices for garnish
instructions: Pour the rosÃ© wine into ice cube trays and freeze until solid, at least 8 hours or overnight | Combine fresh strawberries and sugar in a blender â€” let sit at room temperature for about 10 minutes until the berries begin to release their juices | Add lemon vodka, grenadine, and the frozen rosÃ© cubes to the blender | Blend on high until completely smooth and slushy | Pour into glasses and garnish with fresh strawberry slices and lemon slices | Serve immediately

ingredients: 750ml bottle rosé wine, 1 cup fresh strawberries (hulled and sliced), 2 tbsp granulated sugar, 60ml lemon-flavored vodka, 1 tbsp grenadine, fresh strawberries and lemon slices for garnish
instructions: Pour the rosé wine into ice cube trays and freeze until solid, at least 8 hours or overnight | Combine fresh strawberries and sugar in a blender — let sit at room temperature for about 10 minutes until the berries begin to release their juices | Add lemon vodka, grenadine, and the frozen rosé cubes to the blender | Blend on high until completely smooth and slushy | Pour into glasses and garnish with fresh strawberry slices and lemon slices | Serve immediately

ingredients: For batter: 2 large eggs, 3/4 cup whole milk, 1 tbsp olive oil, 1 cup all-purpose flour, 1 tsp baking powder, 1/2 tsp salt. For filling: 2 chicken breasts (diced), 2 tbsp all-purpose flour, 1 medium onion (diced), 1 tbsp olive oil, 1 1/2 cups chicken stock
instructions: Blend the eggs, milk, and olive oil together, then add the flour, baking powder, and salt while continuing to blend â€” refrigerate the batter for at least 30 minutes | Preheat oven to 200Â°C (400Â°F) | Toss diced chicken with 2 tablespoons flour until lightly coated | Heat olive oil in a skillet and stir-fry the chicken and diced onion until cooked through and browned | Place the cooked chicken and onion in a casserole dish and add just enough chicken stock to almost cover | Pour the chilled batter evenly over the chicken mixture | Bake for 30-40 minutes until the top is puffed and golden brown | Serve hot

ingredients: 300g soft silken tofu, 3 tbsp honey, 2 tbsp confectioners sugar, 1 tsp vanilla extract
instructions: Combine softened tofu, honey, confectioners sugar, and vanilla extract in a blender | Blend on high until completely smooth and creamy | Transfer to a bowl, cover, and chill for several hours or overnight to allow flavors to blend | Serve as a dairy-free topping for fruit, desserts, or pancakes

ingredients: 1 can (400g) fire-roasted diced tomatoes, 1 can (400g) crushed tomatoes, 4 cloves garlic (minced), 2 tbsp chili powder, 1 tsp ground cumin, 1/2 tsp salt, 2 cans (400g each) black beans (drained and rinsed), 1 medium red onion (diced), 1 red bell pepper (diced), 2 cups butternut squash (peeled and cubed), fresh cilantro and sour cream for serving
instructions: Pour both types of tomatoes into a slow cooker | Add minced garlic, chili powder, cumin, and salt â€” mix well | Add drained black beans, diced red onion, diced bell pepper, and cubed butternut squash â€” gently stir to combine | Cover and cook on high for 3-4 hours or on low for 7-8 hours until the vegetables have softened | Serve hot topped with fresh cilantro or a dollop of light sour cream

recipe_name: Duck Magret with Blueberry Port Sauce
ingredients: For duck: 2 duck breasts (magret, skin scored), 2 cloves garlic (minced), 1 tsp fresh thyme leaves, 1 tsp orange zest. For blueberry sauce: 1 cup port wine, 200g fresh blueberries (divided), 2 tbsp red currant jelly, 1 tsp Dijon mustard, 1 tsp cornstarch mixed with 1 tbsp water. For spinach: 1 tbsp olive oil, 1/2 red onion (diced), 1 clove garlic (minced), 1 tbsp butter, 200g fresh spinach. For rosti: 1 tbsp butter, 1/2 onion (diced), 1 clove garlic (minced), 2 large potatoes (grated and squeezed dry)
instructions: Place duck breasts in a container with minced garlic, orange zest, and thyme leaves | Cover and refrigerate to infuse for a few hours | Cook duck breasts skin-side down in a cold pan over medium-high heat to render the fat and crisp the skin â€” this will take 8-10 minutes, draining fat periodically | Transfer duck to an ovenproof dish on a wire rack and cook in a 180Â°C (350Â°F) oven for 20-25 minutes for medium-rare | For extra crispy skin, switch to grill setting for the last few minutes | Make the sauce: heat port, half the blueberries, and red currant jelly in a pan over medium-high heat | Simmer for 8-10 minutes until reduced to a thin sauce consistency | Add cornstarch slurry to thicken slightly, then whisk in Dijon mustard | Remove from heat and stir in the remaining blueberries | For spinach: heat olive oil in a pan, add onion and garlic, cook until softened | Melt butter, add spinach, and cook until wilted | For rosti: heat butter, cook onion and garlic until soft | Squeeze excess liquid from grated potatoes, add to pan, and cook until sticky | Press into egg rings and cook until browned and crisp on both sides | To serve: spoon sauce on a plate, place sliced duck breast on top, with spinach and rosti on the side

ingredients: 1 cup granulated sugar, 1/2 cup shortening, 1/2 cup sour cream, 2 large eggs, 1/2 tsp baking soda, 1/2 tsp ground nutmeg, 1 tsp vanilla extract, 1/4 tsp salt, 1/2 tsp cream of tartar, 3 cups all-purpose flour (approximately)
instructions: Preheat oven to 350Â°F (175Â°C) | In a large mixing bowl, cream together sugar, shortening, sour cream, and eggs until smooth | Stir in baking soda, nutmeg, vanilla, salt, and cream of tartar â€” do not add the flour yet | Chill the mixture for 1 to 24 hours | Gradually add flour to the chilled mixture until the dough is stiff enough to roll for cut-out cookies | On a generously floured work surface, roll out the dough a little at a time with a floured rolling pin until about 1/2-inch thick | Use flour-dipped cookie cutters to cut into desired shapes | Place cut-outs onto a lightly greased cookie sheet, spacing cookies about 2 inches apart | Bake for 10-12 minutes or until the tops are no longer shiny and the bottoms are lightly browned | Cool on a wire rack | Decorate with icing of your choice and store in an airtight container

ingredients: 4 large bell peppers (tops cut off and seeded), 1 cup cooked rice, 500g lean ground beef, 1 can (400g) diced tomatoes, 1/2 cup water, 1 tsp dried basil, 1 tsp dried oregano, 1 tsp chili powder, 1 tsp paprika, 1/2 tsp black pepper, 3 cloves garlic (minced), 1/2 tsp garlic powder, 1 medium onion (diced), 1 cup shredded cheese, salt to taste
instructions: Preheat oven to 450Â°F (230Â°C) | In a saucepan, sautÃ© diced onion and rice for about 5 minutes until lightly browned | Add water, cover, and cook for about 10 minutes | In a large pan, fry ground beef with 1 tablespoon of the seasonings (garlic, chili powder, oregano, basil, paprika, pepper) until almost cooked through | Add diced tomatoes and the cooked rice mixture to the beef | Add the remaining seasonings (except garlic powder) and cook for 5 minutes | Gut the peppers and dust the insides lightly with garlic powder | Layer the rice and meat mixture with shredded cheese while stuffing each bell pepper | Place the tops back on the peppers and stand them upright on a baking sheet | Bake for 45 minutes or longer depending on how tender you want the peppers | Remove from oven and let cool for 5 minutes before serving

ingredients: 1 ripe avocado (mashed), 2 tbsp low-fat mayonnaise, 1 tbsp fresh lime juice, 1 chipotle chili in adobo sauce (minced, plus 1 tsp sauce), 1/4 tsp salt, 1/4 tsp ground cumin, 1/4 tsp dried oregano, 4 large flour tortillas, 200g sliced deli ham or cooked pork, 1 cup shredded iceberg lettuce, 1/4 cup salsa
instructions: Combine mashed avocado, mayonnaise, lime juice, minced chipotle chili with adobo sauce, salt, cumin, and oregano in a bowl â€” stir well | Warm tortillas according to package directions until pliable | Spread about 2 tablespoons of the avocado mixture over each tortilla, leaving a 1-inch border around the edges | Arrange sliced ham or pork down the center of each tortilla | Top each with 1/4 cup shredded lettuce and 1 tablespoon salsa | Fold in the sides and roll up tightly | Serve immediately or wrap in foil for a portable meal

ingredients: 3 large eggs, 2 tsp water, 1 tbsp butter, 2 tbsp fresh chives (chopped), 1 tbsp fresh dill (chopped), 1 tbsp fresh parsley (chopped), 1 small tomato (sliced), 60g Brie cheese (sliced), salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Beat eggs, 2 teaspoons water, salt, and pepper in a bowl until frothy and light | Heat butter in a non-stick skillet over medium heat until foaming | Pour beaten eggs into the pan and let cook undisturbed until the edges begin to set | Using a spatula, gently lift the edges and tilt the pan so uncooked egg flows underneath | When the surface is nearly set, lay out fresh herbs, tomato slices, and Brie cheese in that order over one half of the omelette | Fold the empty half over the filling | Add 1 teaspoon of water to the pan and cover â€” the steam will help melt the cheese | Cook covered for 1 more minute until the cheese is melted and the omelette is just done | Slide onto a plate and serve immediately

ingredients: For rub: 2 tbsp brown sugar, 1 tsp ground allspice, 1 tsp onion powder, 1 tsp dried thyme, 1 tsp salt, 1/2 tsp ground nutmeg. For pork: 2 kg pork shoulder roast, 1/4 cup dark rum, 2 tbsp canola oil. For mop: 1 cup water, 2 tbsp cider vinegar, 1 tbsp dark rum. For sauce: 1 ripe mango (diced), 1/2 onion (diced), 1/4 cup mango chutney, 1/2 cup chicken stock, 3 tbsp dark rum, 1/4 cup cream of coconut, 2 tbsp butter, salt to taste
instructions: The night before cooking, combine all rub ingredients in a small bowl | Massage the pork roast well with the dark rum, then coat generously with about half of the rub | Transfer pork to a plastic bag and refrigerate overnight | Prepare a smoker for barbecuing, bringing the temperature to 200-220Â°F (93-104Â°C) | Remove pork from refrigerator and pat down lightly with another coating of rub | Let the meat sit at room temperature for 30-40 minutes | If basting, stir any remaining rub with the mop ingredients in a saucepan and warm over low heat | Transfer pork to the smoker, fattier side up, and cook for 4-3/4 to 5 hours until internal temperature reaches 160Â°F (71Â°C) | Mop the meat every 40-45 minutes | While the roast cooks, make the sauce: purÃ©e mango, onion, and chutney in a food processor with a bit of stock if needed | Spoon into a heavy saucepan and add remaining stock, rum, cream of coconut, and any remaining dry rub | Warm over medium heat and simmer for about 20 minutes, then season with salt to balance | Add butter just before serving | Remove pork from smoker and let rest at room temperature for 10-15 minutes | Carve the roast and serve with the warm sauce

ingredients: 1 cup dark raisins, 1 cup golden raisins, 1/2 cup dried currants, 1/2 cup pitted dates (chopped), 1/4 cup dried peaches (chopped), 1/4 cup dried apricots (chopped), 1 tsp ground cinnamon, 1/2 tsp ground nutmeg, 1/2 tsp ground allspice, 1/4 tsp ground ginger, 1/2 cup dark corn syrup, 1/4 cup dark rum, 1/2 cup brown sugar, 1/4 cup apple cider syrup or apple juice concentrate, 1/4 cup apple juice, 3 tbsp unsalted butter
instructions: In a large mixing bowl, combine both raisins, currants, chopped dates, chopped peaches, and chopped apricots â€” set aside | In a large nonreactive saucepan, combine cinnamon, nutmeg, allspice, and ginger | Stir in dark corn syrup, dark rum, brown sugar, apple cider syrup, and apple juice | Add butter and bring to a boil over medium heat â€” boil for 3 minutes, stirring occasionally | Pour the hot liquid over the dried fruit mixture and stir well to combine | Cool to room temperature, stirring occasionally | When completely cooled, pour or spoon equal amounts into 3 clean quart glass jars | Seal tightly and refrigerate for up to 12 months | Use as a filling for mince pies, tarts, or as a festive topping

ingredients: 2 tbsp olive oil, 1 medium onion (diced), 2 carrots (diced), 3 cloves garlic (minced), 1 cup dried lentils (rinsed), 1 can (400g) tomato sauce, 1 tbsp dried parsley, 1 tsp dried thyme, salt and black pepper to taste, 4 large potatoes (peeled and cubed), 1/4 cup rice milk or plant-based milk, 2 tbsp vegan butter, 1/2 tsp garlic powder, 2 tbsp fresh chives (chopped), 1 prepared vegan pie crust
instructions: Preheat oven to 350Â°F (175Â°C) | Prepare a pie plate with the pie crust | Put cubed potatoes in a large pot and cover with water â€” bring to a boil and cook until tender | While potatoes are cooking, heat olive oil in a large pan over medium heat | Cook diced onion, carrots, and minced garlic together for 5-10 minutes until soft | Add rinsed lentils, tomato sauce, parsley, thyme, salt, and pepper â€” turn heat to low, cover, and let simmer for 10 minutes until lentils are tender | When potatoes are tender, drain and mash them, adding rice milk, vegan butter, garlic powder, chives, salt, and pepper until smooth and creamy | Fill the prepared pie crust with the lentil mixture and top evenly with the mashed potatoes | Bake for 30 minutes or until the pie crust is cooked and the top is lightly golden | Let cool for 5 minutes before serving

ingredients: 500g ground beef, 150g frozen chopped spinach (thawed and squeezed dry), 1/2 cup mozzarella cheese (shredded), 1/2 cup cheddar cheese (shredded), 1/2 tsp salt, 1/4 tsp black pepper, 1/2 tsp garlic powder, 4 hamburger buns, lettuce, tomato, and condiments for serving
instructions: In a large bowl, combine ground beef, well-drained spinach, mozzarella cheese, cheddar cheese, salt, pepper, and garlic powder â€” mix until evenly combined | Shape the mixture into 8 patties | Grill or broil the patties over medium-high heat for 4-5 minutes per side until cooked through and cheese is melted | Serve on toasted hamburger buns with your favorite toppings like lettuce, tomato, and condiments

ingredients: 2 1/4 tsp active dry yeast, 1 1/2 cups warm water (110Â°F / 43Â°C), 2 cups cake flour, 2 1/2 cups all-purpose flour (plus extra for dusting), 1 tsp salt, 2 tbsp olive oil (plus extra for bowl)
instructions: Sprinkle yeast over warm water in a bowl â€” let stand for 1 minute until the yeast is creamy, then stir until dissolved | In a large bowl, combine cake flour, 2 1/2 cups all-purpose flour, and salt | Add the yeast mixture to the flour and stir until a soft dough forms | Turn the dough out onto a lightly floured surface and knead, adding more flour if necessary, until smooth and elastic, about 10 minutes | Lightly coat a large bowl with olive oil â€” place the dough in the bowl, turning it to oil the top | Cover with plastic wrap and place in a warm, draft-free place to rise until doubled in size, about 1 1/2 hours | Flatten the dough with your fist | Cut the dough into 2 to 4 pieces and shape into balls â€” dust the tops with flour | Place balls on a floured surface and cover each with plastic wrap, allowing room for expansion â€” let rise for 60-90 minutes or until doubled | Shape and bake pizzas as directed at 475Â°F (245Â°C) for 10-12 minutes

ingredients: 500g boneless skinless chicken breasts (cut into 1-inch strips), 1 1/2 cups sweetened shredded coconut, 1/2 cup all-purpose flour, 1 tsp salt, 1/4 tsp black pepper, 2 large eggs (beaten), 2 tbsp unsalted butter (melted), apricot preserves for dipping
instructions: Preheat oven to 400Â°F (200Â°C) | Combine shredded coconut, flour, salt, and pepper in a heavy-duty resealable plastic bag â€” shake to mix | Cut chicken breasts into 1-inch wide strips | Dip each chicken strip into the beaten egg, letting excess drip off | Place egg-coated strips in the plastic bag with the coconut mixture and shake until the chicken is well coated | Place coated chicken strips in a shallow nonstick baking pan in a single layer | Drizzle melted butter evenly over the chicken | Bake for 25 minutes, turning once halfway through, until chicken is cooked through and golden brown | Serve immediately with apricot preserves as a dipping sauce

ingredients: 1 large egg, 1/4 cup milk, 1 tbsp Worcestershire sauce, 1/2 tsp onion powder, 1/4 tsp black pepper, 1/2 cup breadcrumbs, 500g ground beef or ground pork, For glaze: 1/4 cup brown sugar, 1/4 cup ketchup, 1 tbsp white vinegar, 1 tsp prepared mustard
instructions: Preheat oven to 325Â°F (160Â°C) | In a medium bowl, beat the egg, then add milk, Worcestershire sauce, onion powder, pepper, and breadcrumbs â€” mix well | Add ground beef or pork and mix thoroughly until well combined | Shape the mixture into two 5-inch x 2 1/2-inch individual loaves | Place loaves in a small baking pan | In a separate small bowl, combine brown sugar, ketchup, vinegar, and mustard to make the glaze | Pour the glaze evenly over the loaves | Bake uncovered at 325Â°F for 1 hour or until no longer pink in the center and internal temperature reaches 160Â°F (71Â°C) | Let rest for 5 minutes before serving

ingredients: 2 tbsp butter, 1 medium onion (sliced), 1 red bell pepper (sliced), 1 yellow bell pepper (sliced), 3 cloves garlic (minced), 3 boneless skinless chicken breasts (cut into strips), 1 tsp dried tarragon leaves, 1/2 tsp salt, 1/4 tsp fresh coarse ground black pepper, 1 cup mozzarella cheese (shredded), 1/4 cup Parmesan cheese (grated), 1/2 cup half-and-half cream, 300g vermicelli or angel hair pasta
instructions: Melt butter in a 12-inch skillet until sizzling | Stir in sliced onion, bell peppers, and minced garlic â€” cook over medium-high heat until peppers are crisply tender, about 2 to 3 minutes | Remove vegetables from skillet with a slotted spoon and set aside, reserving the juices in the pan | Add chicken strips, tarragon, salt, and pepper to the juices in the pan | Continue cooking, stirring occasionally, until chicken is lightly browned and no longer pink, about 7 to 9 minutes | Meanwhile, cook vermicelli according to package directions until al dente â€” drain | Return vegetables to the skillet with the chicken | Add mozzarella cheese, Parmesan cheese, and half-and-half | Reduce heat to medium and cook until cheese is melted, about 3 to 5 minutes | Add the hot cooked vermicelli and toss gently to coat everything evenly | Serve immediately

ingredients: 3 tbsp fish sauce, 2 tbsp fresh lime juice, 1 tbsp sugar, 3 cloves garlic, 3-5 seedless Thai bird's eye chilies (fresh or dried)
instructions: Chop the chilies and garlic, then pound them together in a mortar and pestle until a rough paste forms | Add fish sauce, lime juice, and sugar to the mortar | Pound gently just to mix all the ingredients together | Taste and adjust the balance of salty, sour, sweet, and spicy as desired | Serve as a dipping sauce for grilled meats, seafood, or rice dishes

ingredients: 2 tbsp olive oil, 500g kielbasa sausage (sliced into rounds), 1 medium onion (sliced), 1 green bell pepper (sliced), 1 red bell pepper (sliced), 2 cups prepared couscous or long grain wild rice, Parmesan cheese for serving (optional), ketchup for serving (optional)
instructions: Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat | Add sliced onions and bell peppers â€” stir-fry until tender, about 5-6 minutes | Add sliced kielbasa and continue to stir-fry until everything is golden and heated thoroughly, about 10-15 minutes | While kielbasa cooks, prepare couscous or long grain wild rice according to package directions | Serve the kielbasa and pepper mixture over the prepared couscous or rice | Garlic or Parmesan couscous varieties go especially well with this dish | Serve with ketchup on the side if desired

ingredients: For topping: 1/2 cup walnuts (chopped), 1 tsp ground cinnamon, 1/2 cup granulated sugar. For cake: 1/2 cup unsalted butter (softened), 1 cup granulated sugar, 2 large eggs, 1 tsp vanilla extract, 1 1/2 cups all-purpose flour, 1 tsp baking powder, 1/4 tsp salt, 1/2 tsp baking soda, 1 cup sour cream, 1 large apple (peeled, cored, and thinly sliced). For serving: whipped cream or sweetened sour cream
instructions: Preheat oven to 350Â°F (175Â°C) | Make the topping: combine chopped walnuts, cinnamon, and 1/2 cup sugar â€” set aside | Grease and flour a 9-inch angel food or tube pan â€” set aside | Beat softened butter until fluffy, then add remaining 1 cup sugar, beating well | Add eggs one at a time, beating after each addition | Add vanilla extract | Sift together flour, baking powder, salt, and baking soda â€” add to the batter alternately with the sour cream, mixing just until combined | Spread half the batter in the prepared pan | Place sliced apples evenly over the batter | Top with half of the walnut mixture | Pour the remaining batter over the walnuts and spread gently | Sprinkle the remaining cinnamon-walnut mixture evenly over the top | Bake for 40 minutes until a tester inserted comes out clean | Cool on a wire rack for 30 minutes | Loosen from the pan, then cool completely | Serve with whipped cream or sour cream sweetened with a touch of maple syrup

recipe_name: Asparagus and Brie Wrapped in Prosciutto
ingredients: 12 asparagus spears (woody ends trimmed), 6 slices prosciutto (halved lengthwise), 100g Brie cheese (cut into 12 thin slices), olive oil for drizzling, salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Preheat oven to 180Â°C (350Â°F) | Cut the woody ends off the asparagus spears | Lay prosciutto slices flat on a baking tray | Top each prosciutto slice with an asparagus spear and a slice of Brie cheese | Wrap the prosciutto around the asparagus and Brie, rolling it up snugly | Place the wrapped bundles seam-side down on the baking tray | Drizzle lightly with olive oil and season with a pinch of salt and pepper | Place in the oven until the cheese starts to melt and the prosciutto is crisp, about 8-10 minutes | Serve immediately as an appetizer or side dish

ingredients: 400g rotini pasta, 4 tbsp extra virgin olive oil (divided), 500g mussels (scrubbed and debearded), 3 cloves garlic (minced), 1 medium zucchini (diced), 1/4 tsp black pepper, 200g shrimp (peeled and deveined), 200g scallops, 1/2 tsp salt, 2 tbsp fresh lemon juice, 2 tbsp fresh parsley (chopped)
instructions: Bring a large pot of water to a boil, season generously with salt, and cook rotini 1 minute less than the required cooking time | Drain and toss with 1 tablespoon olive oil, then spread on a sheet tray to cool | In a small pot, steam the mussels until they open, about 5-6 minutes â€” discard any that do not open | Remove mussels from shells, discard shells, and set aside | Meanwhile, in a skillet, sautÃ© minced garlic in 1 tablespoon olive oil until lightly golden | Add diced zucchini and sautÃ© for 4 minutes, then season with salt and pepper to taste | In a separate skillet, sautÃ© shrimp and scallops in 1 tablespoon olive oil until lightly golden and cooked through, about 3-4 minutes â€” season and set aside to cool | Once everything has cooled, combine all the seafood with the pasta and zucchini in a large bowl | Toss to combine and add the remaining 1 tablespoon olive oil, fresh lemon juice, and chopped parsley | Serve at room temperature or chilled

ingredients: 2 medium potatoes (peeled and diced), 1 cup broccoli florets (chopped), 1/4 cup onion (diced), 1/4 cup water, 6 large eggs, 1/4 cup milk, 1/2 tsp salt, 1/4 tsp black pepper, 1/2 cup cheddar cheese (shredded), 1/2 tsp dried tarragon
instructions: In a 10-inch omelet pan or skillet, stir together diced potatoes, chopped broccoli, diced onion, and water | Cover and cook over medium heat until potatoes are tender, about 15 minutes | Uncover and, if necessary, continue cooking until any remaining water is evaporated | Reduce heat to low | In a medium bowl, beat together eggs, milk, salt, and pepper until well blended | Pour the egg mixture over the cooked vegetables | Cover and cook until eggs are almost set, about 15 minutes | Remove from heat | Sprinkle shredded cheese and dried tarragon over the top | Cover and let stand until eggs are completely set and cheese is melted, about 3 to 5 minutes | Cut into wedges and serve directly from the pan

ingredients: 2 cans (400g each) black beans (drained and rinsed), 1 can (200g) diced green chilies, 1/2 tsp ground cumin, 1/2 tsp garlic powder, 1/4 tsp salt, 1/4 cup water
instructions: Place all ingredients in a crock pot â€” drained black beans, diced green chilies, cumin, garlic powder, salt, and water | Stir to combine | Cover and cook on low for 2 hours until heated through and flavors have melded | Serve as a side dish or on top of Cafe Rio-style pork

ingredients: 1 can (400g) sweetened condensed milk, 1 1/4 cups cold water, 2 packages instant vanilla pudding mix, 2 cups whipped topping (thawed, plus extra for garnish), 1 prepared pound cake or sponge cake (cut into 1-inch cubes), 2 tbsp orange juice, 1 cup fresh strawberries (sliced), 1/2 cup fresh raspberries, 1/3 cup kiwi (sliced), chocolate curls or cocoa powder for garnish
instructions: Bake one cake according to package directions in two 9-inch round cake pans â€” cool and cut one cake into 1-inch cubes (freeze the other cake for future use) | In a medium bowl, combine sweetened condensed milk and cold water â€” stir well | Add both packages of instant vanilla pudding mix and beat until blended â€” chill for 5 minutes | Fold the 2 cups of whipped topping into the pudding mixture until smooth | In a trifle bowl, layer the ingredients as follows: spread 2 cups of pudding mixture covering the bottom of the bowl, layer cake cubes covering the pudding, sprinkle with orange juice, top with sliced strawberries, raspberries, and sliced kiwi | Repeat the layers once more and finish with a final layer of pudding on top | Garnish with extra fruit, chocolate curls, or a dusting of cocoa powder | Refrigerate for at least 2 hours before serving

ingredients: 500g lean ground beef, 1 medium onion (diced), 2 tbsp taco seasoning, 1 can (400g) pinto beans (undrained), 1 can (400g) kidney beans (undrained), 1 can (400g) yellow hominy (undrained), 1 can (400g) stewed tomatoes, 1 can (400g) diced tomatoes with green chilies, 1 packet dry ranch dressing mix, tortilla chips for serving, 1 cup cheddar cheese (shredded)
instructions: Brown ground beef and diced onion in a large pot over medium-high heat â€” drain excess fat | Add taco seasoning and mix thoroughly | Add all canned ingredients without draining: pinto beans, kidney beans, hominy, stewed tomatoes, and diced tomatoes with green chilies | Stir in the dry ranch dressing mix | Simmer over low heat until bubbly and heated through, about 15-20 minutes | To serve, place a handful of tortilla chips in each bowl, ladle the soup over the top, and sprinkle with shredded cheddar cheese

recipe_name: Swiss Chard with Tomato and Bacon
ingredients: 1 large bunch Swiss chard (washed and roughly chopped into 2-3 inch pieces), 3 slices bacon (chopped), 1/2 medium onion (diced), 3 cloves garlic (minced), 1 tbsp olive oil, 1/4 tsp red pepper flakes, 1/4 tsp salt, 1/2 cup chicken stock, 2 medium tomatoes (sliced), 1 tbsp balsamic vinegar
instructions: Wash and rinse Swiss chard thoroughly | Roughly chop the chard into 2-3 inch pieces, keeping the stalks and leaves separate | In a large skillet, add olive oil and chopped bacon â€” cook until the fat has rendered and the bacon is crisp | Add the chard stalks, diced onion, and minced garlic â€” cover and cook until wilted, about 4-5 minutes | Add salt and red pepper flakes | Uncover and as the water steams off, add chicken stock, adding more as needed so the pan does not burn | Lower heat to medium-low and continue to simmer until chard stalks and onion are tender, about 5 minutes | Add chard leaves and sliced tomatoes â€” cook for another 3-5 minutes until leaves are wilted | Dress with balsamic vinegar to taste and serve immediately

ingredients: 1 kg pumpkin (peeled, seeded, and cut into wedges), 3 tbsp olive oil, 1 tsp ground cinnamon, 1/2 tsp sea salt, 1/4 tsp black pepper, 1/2 cup plain yogurt, 1 tbsp fresh lemon juice, 1/4 cup pine nuts (toasted), 1 red chili (sliced, optional), fresh coriander leaves for garnish
instructions: Preheat oven to 200Â°C (400Â°F) | Place pumpkin wedges in a large bowl with olive oil and cinnamon â€” season with salt and pepper and toss to combine | Transfer the pumpkin mixture to a baking tray in a single layer | Bake for approximately 30 to 40 minutes until golden and cooked through | Arrange the roasted pumpkin on a serving platter | Drizzle with yogurt and fresh lemon juice | Scatter toasted pine nuts, sliced chili, and fresh coriander leaves over the top | Best served at room temperature when all the flavors have melded together

ingredients: 4 large eggs, 1/2 tsp salt, 2 tbsp butter, 1 small onion (diced), 1 green pepper (diced), 1 medium tomato (diced), 2 tbsp fresh parsley (chopped, plus extra for garnish)
instructions: In a medium bowl, whisk eggs well until frothy | Add salt and whisk again | In a frying pan, heat butter over medium heat and sautÃ© the diced onion, green pepper, and tomato until almost done, about 5-6 minutes | Pour the beaten eggs over the sautÃ©ed vegetables | Add more salt if required | Cook without stirring until the eggs are set on the bottom, then gently lift the edges to allow uncooked egg to flow underneath | When nearly set, garnish with additional fresh parsley | Serve hot directly from the pan

ingredients: 1/3 cup canola oil, 3/4 cup dark brown sugar, 1/2 cup pumpkin purÃ©e, 1 tsp ground cinnamon, 1/2 tsp ground ginger, 1/4 tsp ground nutmeg, 1 tsp vanilla extract, 1 1/2 cups all-purpose flour, 1 tsp baking powder, 1/4 tsp salt, 1/2 cup rolled oats. For ganache: 1/2 cup dark chocolate chips, 2 tbsp soy creamer or heavy cream
instructions: Begin heating your waffle iron according to the manufacturer's instructions | In a large bowl, whisk together canola oil, brown sugar, pumpkin purÃ©e, cinnamon, ginger, nutmeg, and vanilla until smooth | Sift together flour, baking powder, and salt â€” stir into the wet ingredients, but be careful not to overbeat the batter â€” a few lumps are fine | Fold in rolled oats just enough to distribute them evenly | Lightly grease the waffle iron before cooking each batch | Portion out batter into each waffle indent as you would for standard waffles and spread it lightly to fill evenly | Close the iron and cook for 2 to 5 minutes, depending on your waffle iron, until golden brown all over | Transfer hot waffle cookies to a wire rack to cool â€” repeat with remaining batter | Once completely cool, prepare the ganache: microwave chocolate chips and soy creamer in a microwave-safe bowl in 30-second bursts, stirring thoroughly until smooth | Use a spoon or piping bag to drizzle ganache over the cooled waffle cookies | Let the ganache set before serving

ingredients: 2 cups granulated sugar, 3 large eggs, 1 can (425g) pumpkin purÃ©e, 3 cups all-purpose flour, 1 tsp salt, 2 tsp ground cinnamon, 1 tsp baking powder, 1 tsp baking soda, 1/2 tsp ground nutmeg, 1 cup vegetable oil, 1/2 cup water, 1 tsp vanilla extract, 1 cup pecans (chopped). For glaze: 1/2 cup granulated sugar, 1/4 cup water, 1/2 tsp vanilla extract
instructions: Preheat oven to 350Â°F (175Â°C) and grease three loaf pans | Beat sugar and eggs together until fluffy â€” add pumpkin purÃ©e and mix well | In another bowl, combine flour, salt, cinnamon, baking powder, baking soda, and nutmeg | Stir dry ingredients into the pumpkin mixture alternately with vegetable oil and water â€” add vanilla and mix well | Beat for 3 minutes until smooth â€” fold in chopped pecans | Divide the batter evenly among the 3 greased loaf pans | Bake for 1 hour until a toothpick inserted in the center comes out clean | While loaves bake, make the glaze: combine sugar, water, and vanilla in a small saucepan â€” bring to a boil and boil for 3 minutes | Brush the hot glaze over the tops of the warm loaves as soon as they come out of the oven | Let cool in the pans for 10 minutes, then transfer to a wire rack to cool completely

ingredients: 1 whole fryer chicken (cut into pieces), 2 medium onions (diced), 1 green bell pepper (diced), 2 medium tomatoes (diced), 4 cloves garlic (minced), 3 tbsp olive oil, 1 bay leaf, 2 cups chicken broth, 1 cup long grain white rice, 1/2 tsp saffron threads, 1 tsp salt, 1/2 cup baby green peas, 1/4 cup white wine (plus extra for finishing), roasted red peppers and asparagus tips for garnish
instructions: In a large skillet, sautÃ© chicken pieces in heated olive oil until the skin is golden on all sides â€” remove chicken and place in a casserole dish | In the same oil in the skillet, sautÃ© diced onion, green pepper, tomatoes, and garlic for 5 minutes â€” pour over the chicken in the casserole dish | In the same skillet, add chicken broth, white wine, saffron, salt, bay leaf, and rice | When the mixture begins to boil, pour it over the casserole | Cover and bake in oven at 350Â°F (175Â°C) for 20 minutes or until the chicken is cooked through | Sprinkle with a splash of white wine and garnish with peas, roasted red peppers, and asparagus tips | Serve hot directly from the casserole

ingredients: 1 tsp ground cumin, 1 tsp ground coriander, 1 tsp sweet paprika, 1/2 tsp fresh ground black pepper, 1/4 tsp cayenne pepper, 8 lamb loin chops, 1 tsp salt, 1/4 cup olive oil (plus extra for drizzling), 2 tbsp unsalted butter, 3 shallots (thinly sliced), 400g fresh spinach leaves
instructions: In a small bowl, mix together cumin, coriander, paprika, black pepper, and cayenne | Season the lamb chops with salt and drizzle with olive oil | Coat both sides of the chops generously with the spice mixture | In a very large skillet, heat the 1/4 cup olive oil until shimmering | Add the chops and cook over moderate heat until browned and medium-rare, about 7 minutes per side â€” remove and let rest | Meanwhile, in a large deep skillet, melt the butter | Add sliced shallots and cook over moderate heat until softened and golden, about 5 minutes | Add handfuls of spinach to the skillet and cook over moderate heat, stirring and adding more spinach after each batch wilts | Season spinach with salt | Mound the spinach on plates and serve with the lamb chops on top

ingredients: For chicken: 4 boneless skinless chicken breasts, 1/4 cup fresh cilantro, 2 tbsp fish sauce, 1 tbsp soy sauce, 2 stalks lemongrass (white part only, chopped), 4 cloves garlic, 1 tbsp lime zest, 2 tbsp fresh lime juice, 1/2 tsp fresh ground white pepper. For slaw: 3 scallions (sliced), 1 red bell pepper (julienned), 1 cup jicama (julienned), 1 cup snow peas (julienned), 1 tbsp sugar, 1 tbsp fish sauce, 1 tsp chili sauce, 1 tsp sesame oil, 1 tbsp toasted sesame seeds. For serving: 200g rice noodles, 1 tbsp extra virgin olive oil, fresh cilantro
instructions: Make the chicken marinade: purÃ©e cilantro, fish sauce, soy sauce, lemongrass, garlic, lime zest, lime juice, and white pepper in a blender to a coarse paste | Coat chicken breasts with the mixture and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes, turning and recoating after 15 minutes | Make the slaw: place sliced scallions, julienned bell pepper, jicama, and snow peas in a large mixing bowl | In a small bowl, whisk together sugar, fish sauce, chili sauce, sesame oil, and toasted sesame seeds | Pour the sauce over the vegetables and mix thoroughly â€” cover and refrigerate until ready to serve | Prepare a grill to medium-high heat | Boil water for rice noodles | Grill chicken (with the marinade paste still on) until cooked through â€” remove from heat, cover, and let rest | Add rice noodles to the boiling water and turn off the heat â€” let soak until tender, then drain and toss with a dash of olive oil to prevent sticking | To serve, plate the noodles and top with the slaw | Slice the chicken and place on top â€” garnish with fresh cilantro

ingredients: 4 chicken thighs (bone-in, skin-on), 1/2 tsp salt, 2 tbsp curry powder, 2 tbsp olive oil (divided), 1 red bell pepper (sliced), 1 cup fresh pineapple (diced), 1 serrano pepper (minced), 1 cup unsweetened coconut milk, 1 tbsp brown sugar, steamed rice for serving
instructions: Sprinkle chicken thighs with salt and curry powder, coating evenly | In a 12-inch skillet, quickly brown chicken on both sides in 1 tablespoon hot olive oil over high heat | Reduce heat to medium-high and cook for 12 minutes until tender and no longer pink â€” remove and keep warm | For the sauce: in a second skillet, cook sliced bell pepper in 1 tablespoon hot olive oil over medium-high heat for 3 minutes â€” set aside | Add diced pineapple to the same skillet and cook for 5 minutes until lightly browned | Add minced serrano pepper and cook for 1 minute | Stir in coconut milk and brown sugar â€” heat through until the sauce is warm and slightly thickened | Serve the sauce with peppers and pineapple over the chicken with steamed rice on the side

ingredients: 1 medium onion (diced), 3 cloves garlic (minced), 2 tbsp olive oil, 6 cups water, 1 cup basmati rice, 1/4 cup fresh basil (chopped), 1 medium zucchini (diced), 200g fresh mushrooms (sliced), 2 cups cooked chicken (shredded), 1 tsp salt, 1/2 tsp black pepper
instructions: In a large pot, sautÃ© diced onion and minced garlic in olive oil until tender, about 5 minutes | Add water, basmati rice, chopped basil, diced zucchini, sliced mushrooms, and shredded chicken | Season with salt and pepper | Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer for 40 minutes or until the rice is fully cooked and the vegetables are tender | Taste and adjust seasoning | Serve hot in bowls

ingredients: 1 whole kutum fish or trout (cleaned and scaled, about 1 kg), 1/2 cup walnuts (chopped), 1 medium onion (diced), 2 tbsp butter, 1/4 cup sour cherries (dried, plumped in water), 1/4 cup sultana raisins (plumped in water), 1/2 tsp salt, aluminum foil for wrapping
instructions: Plump the raisins and dried cherries in warm water for 15 minutes, then drain | Clean and wash the fish thoroughly inside and out â€” if kutum is not available, substitute trout or another freshwater white fish | Preheat oven to 400Â°F (200Â°C) | Make the stuffing: in a bowl, combine diced onion, chopped walnuts, butter, drained cherries, and drained raisins â€” mix well and add salt if needed | Stuff the fish cavity with the mixture, packing it evenly | Wrap the stuffed fish tightly in aluminum foil | Place on a baking sheet and bake for 20 minutes until the fish is cooked through and flakes easily | Remove from foil and slice crosswise to serve

ingredients: 250g Philadelphia cream cheese (softened), 1 can (400g) sweetened condensed milk, 1 tsp lemon zest, 2 cups fresh strawberries (hulled and blended until smooth), 1/2 cup graham cracker crumbs
instructions: Mix cream cheese, sweetened condensed milk, and lemon zest with an electric mixer until well blended and smooth | Pour into a freezer-safe container and freeze for 4 hours or until almost solid | Remove from freezer and beat the cream cheese mixture with a mixer until creamy | Blend fresh strawberries in a blender until smooth | Add the strawberry purÃ©e and graham cracker crumbs to the cream cheese mixture â€” mix well | Return to the freezer and freeze for 8 hours or until firm | Remove from freezer 15 minutes before serving â€” let stand at room temperature to soften slightly before scooping

ingredients: 2 salmon fillets (about 150g each), 2 tbsp fresh lemon juice, 1 tsp dried dill, 1 tbsp olive oil, salt and black pepper to taste, fresh spinach or stir-fried vegetables for serving
instructions: Preheat oven to 180Â°C (350Â°F) | Rub 2 sheets of aluminum foil with olive oil (about 1/2 tablespoon per sheet) | Slice each salmon fillet in half and place one piece on each sheet of foil | In a small bowl, mix lemon juice and dried dill together | Drizzle the lemon-dill mixture over the fillets | Season with salt and pepper | Wrap up the foil parcels tightly | Place on a baking sheet and bake for 20-25 minutes until the salmon flakes easily with a fork | Serve over fresh spinach leaves or with your favorite stir-fried vegetables

ingredients: 1 prepared sponge or pound cake (split into 2 layers), 1 package lemon pie filling, 2 cups heavy whipping cream, 2 tbsp powdered sugar, 1 tsp vanilla extract, lemon zest for garnish
instructions: Prepare the lemon pie filling according to package directions | Cover the surface directly with waxed paper to prevent a skin from forming and refrigerate until completely chilled | Spread half of the chilled lemon filling between the layers of the cake | Whip the heavy cream with powdered sugar and vanilla until stiff peaks form | Fold the remaining half of the lemon filling into the whipped cream until smooth | Spread the lemon cream mixture over the top and sides of the cake | Chill for at least 4 hours before serving | Garnish with lemon zest before slicing

ingredients: 2 cups cooked ham (diced), 6 cups water, 450g dried navy beans (rinsed), 3 celery stalks (diced), 1 medium onion (diced), 2 carrots (diced), 1 tsp dried thyme, 1 tbsp liquid smoke, 1/4 cup fresh parsley (chopped), salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Combine all ingredients except the parsley in a crock pot â€” diced ham, water, navy beans, celery, onion, carrots, dried thyme, and liquid smoke | Mix well, cover, and cook on low for 10 to 12 hours until the beans are tender and the stew is thick | Just before serving, stir in the chopped fresh parsley | Season with salt and black pepper to taste | Serve hot in bowls with crusty bread on the side

ingredients: 2 roasted garlic cloves (minced), 2 portabella mushrooms, 1 medium onion (sliced), 1 medium zucchini (sliced), 1 red bell pepper, 3 tbsp olive oil (for marinade), 2 tbsp balsamic vinegar, 1 tsp fresh rosemary (chopped), 500g fresh tortellini (cooked and cooled), 1 cup provolone cheese (cubed), 1/4 cup black olives (sliced). For dressing: 1 clove garlic, 3 tbsp olive oil, 2 tbsp balsamic vinegar, 1 tsp fresh rosemary
instructions: Place mushrooms, sliced onion, sliced zucchini, and bell pepper in a zip-lock bag with 3 tablespoons olive oil, balsamic vinegar, minced roasted garlic, and rosemary â€” marinate for 1 hour | Grill the vegetables over medium-high heat until browned, about 2-3 minutes per side | Dice the grilled onions, peppers (charred skin removed), zucchini, and mushrooms | Make the dressing: in a blender, blend garlic, olive oil, balsamic vinegar, and rosemary until smooth | In a large bowl, combine cooked tortellini, grilled vegetables, provolone cheese, and black olives | Toss with the dressing, adding more oil and vinegar if necessary | Serve at room temperature or chill and serve cold

ingredients: 1/2 cup creamy peanut butter, 2 tbsp unsalted butter (softened), 1/2 tsp salt, 2 cups powdered sugar, 1 tsp vanilla extract, 2 cups semi-sweet chocolate chips, 1 tbsp paraffin wax or coconut oil (for melting)
instructions: Mix peanut butter, softened butter, salt, powdered sugar, and vanilla in a bowl in the order listed until a smooth dough forms | Form the mixture into egg shapes and place on a parchment-lined baking sheet | Melt chocolate chips and paraffin wax (or coconut oil) in a double boiler over gentle heat, stirring until smooth | Dip each peanut butter egg into the melted chocolate, coating completely | Place on waxed paper until set | Decorate with decorator icing if desired | Store in the refrigerator

ingredients: 6 medium beets (trimmed, leaving root end intact), 3 green onions (thinly sliced, white and green parts separated), 2 tbsp extra virgin olive oil, 2 cloves garlic (minced), 1/2 tsp ground coriander, 1/2 tsp salt, 1/4 tsp black pepper, 1 tbsp orange zest, 1/4 cup fresh orange juice
instructions: Leaving the root end intact, trim the tops from the beets leaving about 1-inch of stem | In a saucepan of boiling salted water, cover and cook beets for 25 minutes or until fork-tender | Drain and let cool enough to handle | Slip off the skins and quarter the beets | Meanwhile, thinly slice green onions and set aside the light and dark green parts separately | In a shallow Dutch oven or saucepan, heat olive oil over medium heat | Cook the light green parts of the onions, minced garlic, coriander, salt, and pepper for about 2 minutes until softened | Stir in orange zest and orange juice â€” boil for 30 seconds or until reduced by half | Stir in the quartered beets | Cover and cook, stirring once, for about 4 minutes until beets are heated through | Sprinkle with the dark green parts of the green onions and serve

ingredients: 1 jar maraschino cherries (drained, juice reserved, halved), 1/2 cup unsalted butter (softened), 1 cup granulated sugar, 1 large egg, 1 tsp vanilla extract, 2 tsp cherry juice (from jar), 1 1/2 cups all-purpose flour, 1/3 cup unsweetened cocoa powder, 1/2 tsp baking powder, 1/4 tsp baking soda, 1/4 tsp salt, 1 cup semi-sweet chocolate chips, 1/2 cup sweetened condensed milk
instructions: Drain cherries, reserving 3 teaspoons of the juice â€” cut cherries in half | Beat butter and sugar at medium speed until creamy | Add egg, vanilla, and 2 teaspoons of the reserved cherry juice â€” beat until blended | In a separate bowl, combine flour, cocoa powder, baking powder, baking soda, and salt | Gradually add the flour mixture to the butter mixture, beating until a dough forms | Shape dough into 1-inch balls and place on an ungreased cookie sheet | Make a thumb imprint in the center of each cookie | Place a cherry half in each indent | In a saucepan over low heat, melt chocolate chips and condensed milk together | Add the remaining 1 teaspoon cherry juice to the melted chocolate â€” cool slightly | Spoon 1 teaspoon of the melted chocolate mixture over each cherry half | Bake at 350Â°F (175Â°C) for 10 minutes | Let cool on the baking sheet for 5 minutes before transferring to a wire rack

ingredients: 2 stalks lemongrass (finely minced), 3 tbsp soy sauce, 2 fresh chili peppers (minced), 1/2 tsp red pepper flakes, 1/2 tsp ground turmeric, 1 tsp sugar, 1/2 tsp salt, 400g firm tofu (pressed and cubed), 3 tbsp vegetable oil (divided), 1 yellow onion (sliced), 2 shallots (sliced), 3 cloves garlic (minced), 1/4 cup roasted peanuts (chopped, divided), 1/4 cup Thai basil leaves, steamed rice for serving
instructions: Combine minced lemongrass, soy sauce, fresh chilies, red pepper flakes, turmeric, sugar, and salt in a bowl | Add the cubed tofu and turn gently to coat evenly â€” marinate for 30 minutes | Heat half the oil in a 12-inch nonstick skillet over moderately high heat | Add sliced onion, shallots, and garlic and stir until fragrant, about 1 minute | Reduce heat to low and cook until the onions are soft, about 3 minutes â€” transfer to a plate and keep warm | Wipe the pan clean and heat the remaining oil over moderate heat | Add the marinated tofu mixture and, using chopsticks or wooden spoons, turn so it cooks evenly, about 4 to 5 minutes | Add the onion mixture back to the pan and cook uncovered for another 2 to 3 minutes | Add half the chopped peanuts and all the basil leaves | Remove from heat and transfer to a serving plate | Garnish with the remaining peanuts and serve immediately with steamed rice

ingredients: 4 medium potatoes (peeled and cubed), 3 carrots (sliced), 3 celery ribs (sliced), 1 medium onion (diced), 1 green bell pepper (diced), 500g bratwurst sausages (sliced), 2 cups chicken broth, 1 tsp salt, 1/2 tsp dried basil, 1/4 tsp black pepper, 1/2 cup half-and-half cream, 2 tbsp cornstarch mixed with 2 tbsp cold water
instructions: In a 5-quart slow cooker, combine cubed potatoes, sliced carrots, celery, diced onion, and diced green pepper | Top with sliced bratwurst | In a bowl, combine chicken broth, salt, basil, and pepper â€” pour over the top | Cover and cook on low for 7 hours until vegetables are tender and sausage is no longer pink | Stir in the half-and-half cream | Combine cornstarch and cold water until smooth â€” stir into the stew | Cover and cook on high for 30 minutes until the gravy is thickened | Serve hot in bowls

ingredients: 400g dried pasta (penne or fusilli), 3 tbsp olive oil (divided), 1 medium onion (diced), 3 cloves garlic (minced), 2 cups frozen broccoli florets, 2 cans (200g each) tuna in olive oil (drained and flaked), 4 slices bacon (cooked and crumbled), 1 tsp Italian seasoning, 1/2 tsp fresh ground black pepper, 1/4 cup dry white wine, 1/4 cup Parmesan cheese (grated)
instructions: Cook pasta in salted boiling water until al dente â€” drain and set aside | Meanwhile, heat 2 tablespoons olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat | SautÃ© diced onion and minced garlic until soft, about 4-5 minutes | Add frozen broccoli and flaked tuna â€” cook until broccoli is tender, about 5-6 minutes | Add crumbled bacon, Italian seasoning, black pepper, and white wine â€” heat through | Add the cooked pasta to the skillet and toss everything together | Drizzle with the remaining 1 tablespoon olive oil and sprinkle with Parmesan cheese | Toss gently and serve immediately

ingredients: 1/2 cup caster sugar (superfine sugar), 1 cup unsalted butter (softened), 2 cups all-purpose flour, 1/4 tsp salt, 1 tsp vanilla extract
instructions: Preheat oven to 300Â°F (150Â°C) and butter an 8-inch round pan | Cream softened butter and caster sugar together until no lumps remain | Add vanilla extract and salt â€” blend until smooth | Add flour in increments, blending until a smooth dough forms | Pat the dough down evenly in the buttered 8-inch round pan | Chill in the refrigerator for 45 minutes | Bake on the lower rack of the oven for 45 minutes until light golden brown on top | Cut into 8 wedges while still hot using a sharp knife | Cool completely before serving â€” it will fall apart if handled while hot | Store in an airtight container

ingredients: 1 can (400g) crushed pineapple with juice, 1 ripe banana, 1/2 cup plain yogurt, 1/4 cup pineapple juice, 1 cup fresh or frozen fruit (strawberries, mango, or berries), 1/2 cup ice cubes
instructions: Combine crushed pineapple with juice, banana, yogurt, pineapple juice, fresh or frozen fruit of your choice, and ice cubes in a blender or food processor | Cover and blend on high until completely smooth | Taste and add a little honey if additional sweetness is desired | Pour into glasses and serve immediately

ingredients: 1 sheet puff pastry (thawed at room temperature for 30 minutes), 2 large eggs (divided), 1 tbsp water, 500g bulk pork sausage, 2 cups herb stuffing mix, 1/2 medium onion (diced), 100g mushrooms (diced)
instructions: Preheat oven to 375Â°F (190Â°C) | Mix one egg with 1 tablespoon water â€” set aside as egg wash | In a large bowl, mix together sausage, herb stuffing mix, the remaining egg, diced onion, and diced mushrooms until well combined | Unfold puff pastry onto a lightly floured baking sheet, creating 3 sections lengthwise â€” do not separate the sections | Cut 9 strips in each of the two outer sections, about 1 inch apart, cutting just to the fold line in the pastry â€” these strips will be criss-crossed over the stuffing | Spoon the sausage mixture down the center of the pastry | Starting at one end, fold the pastry strips over the sausage mixture, alternating sides to create a braided effect | Brush the top with the reserved egg wash | Bake for 35 minutes until golden brown | Slice and serve warm

ingredients: For topping: 1/4 cup brown sugar, 1/4 cup heavy whipping cream. For dough: 1 1/2 cups all-purpose flour (plus 1 1/2-2 cups for kneading), 3 tbsp granulated sugar, 2 1/4 tsp active dry yeast, 1/2 tsp salt, 1/2 cup warm water, 1 large egg, 3 tbsp unsalted butter (melted). For filling: 2 tbsp unsalted butter (softened), 1/3 cup brown sugar, 1 tbsp ground cinnamon
instructions: Sprinkle brown sugar in the bottom of a greased 9x13-inch pan â€” pour heavy cream over the top and set aside | In a large bowl, combine 1 1/2 cups flour, granulated sugar, yeast, and salt | Add warm water, egg, and melted butter â€” beat at low speed until moistened | By hand, stir in an additional 1 1/2 to 2 cups flour to form a soft dough | Knead for 3 minutes, then let rest for 10 minutes | Roll the dough into a 7x15-inch rectangle | Spread with softened butter and sprinkle with brown sugar and cinnamon | Roll up tightly from the long side and seal the edges | Cut into 1-inch rolls and place in the prepared pan | Cover and let rise until doubled, about 45 minutes | Bake at 350Â°F (175Â°C) for 20-25 minutes until golden | Invert onto a serving plate so the caramel topping drips down over the rolls | Serve warm

ingredients: 2 shots espresso coffee (cooled), 2 cups vanilla ice cream, 1/4 cup milk, 2 tbsp mascarpone cheese, 1 tbsp cocoa powder (plus extra for dusting), 1 tbsp sugar (optional), whipped cream for topping
instructions: Brew 2 shots of espresso and let cool completely | In a blender, combine cooled espresso, vanilla ice cream, milk, mascarpone cheese, cocoa powder, and sugar if using | Blend on high until smooth and creamy | Pour into a tall glass | Top with a generous swirl of whipped cream | Dust with cocoa powder and serve immediately

ingredients: 500g carrots (peeled and sliced into rounds), 2 tbsp honey, 1 tbsp unsalted butter, 1/4 tsp salt, 1/4 tsp ground cinnamon, 1 tbsp fresh parsley (chopped)
instructions: Bring a pot of salted water to a boil â€” add sliced carrots and cook until tender, about 8-10 minutes | Drain carrots and return to the pot | Add honey, butter, salt, and cinnamon â€” stir gently over low heat until the butter melts and the carrots are evenly glazed | Transfer to a serving dish and garnish with fresh chopped parsley | Serve hot as a side dish

ingredients: 1/4 cup plus 2 tbsp extra virgin olive oil (divided), 4 medium red bliss potatoes (peeled and thinly sliced), 1 medium onion (thinly sliced), 6 large eggs, salt and black pepper to taste
instructions: Heat 1/4 cup of olive oil in a large cast-iron skillet over medium heat | Add the sliced potatoes and onion â€” season with salt and pepper | Cook over moderate heat, stirring frequently, until the potatoes and onion are tender but not browned, about 15 minutes | In a large bowl, lightly beat the eggs and season with salt and pepper | Gently scrape the potato mixture into the bowl with the eggs, making sure not to leave any in the skillet | Return the empty skillet to the heat and add the remaining 2 tablespoons olive oil | Add the egg and potato mixture, spreading it out in an even layer | Cover and cook over low heat until the tortilla is set on the bottom and edges, about 10 minutes | Set a large plate over the skillet and carefully invert the tortilla onto the plate, then slide it back into the skillet to cook the other side for a few minutes until fully set | Slide onto a serving plate and let stand for 5 minutes | Cut into wedges and serve warm or at room temperature

ingredients: For cocktail sauce: 1/2 cup tomato sauce or ketchup, 2 tbsp prepared horseradish, 1 tbsp red wine or burgundy wine, 1 tbsp fresh lemon juice, 1/4 tsp black pepper, 1/4 tsp salt. For serving: 2 whole fresh Dungeness crabs (cleaned and cracked), shredded iceberg lettuce, 2 fresh lemons (quartered)
instructions: Make the cocktail sauce: combine tomato sauce, horseradish, red wine, lemon juice, pepper, and salt in a bowl â€” stir by hand until well mixed | Cover and chill thoroughly | Line a serving bowl with shredded iceberg lettuce | Arrange the cracked crab attractively on top of the lettuce | Garnish with lemon quarters | Serve the cocktail sauce in a separate bowl on the side | Serves 4

ingredients: 1/2 cup fontina cheese (shredded), 1/2 cup GruyÃ¨re cheese (shredded), 1/2 cup mozzarella cheese (shredded), 2 tbsp cherry brandy, 2 tbsp dry white wine, 8 slices crusty bread, 2 tbsp olive oil (for brushing), 1 clove garlic (halved)
instructions: Combine the three shredded cheeses with cherry brandy and white wine in a large bowl â€” mix well | Brush olive oil on one side of each bread slice and turn over | Spoon the cheese mixture evenly onto 4 of the 8 bread slices (on the un-oiled side) | Top with the remaining 4 bread slices, oiled side up | Heat a large non-stick skillet over medium-high heat for 2 minutes | Place the sandwiches in the skillet (in batches if necessary) | Cover and cook for 2 to 3 minutes until the undersides are golden brown and the cheese has begun to melt | Uncover, flip the sandwiches with a spatula, and cook for 2 to 3 minutes until the other side is golden and the cheese has fully melted | Turn once more and cook for 30 seconds | Remove from pan and let cool for 3 to 5 minutes | Cut sandwiches in half | Rub the cut side of the garlic clove over the top of each sandwich and serve immediately

ingredients: 2 cups cooked long-grain rice, 3 tbsp olive oil, 200g pork (cubed), 200g chicken (cubed), 100g breakfast sausage (sliced), 200g shrimp (peeled and deveined), 12 clams (scrubbed), 2 medium tomatoes (diced), 4 cloves garlic (minced), 2 medium onions (diced), 1/2 cup green beans (trimmed), 1/2 cup peas, 1 tsp saffron threads, 1 tbsp smoked paprika, 1 red bell pepper (sliced), 1 green bell pepper (sliced), 100g chorizo (sliced), salt to taste
instructions: Separately, boil shrimp and clams in plenty of water until shrimp are pink and clams have opened â€” discard any clams that do not open | Reserve the seafood water for cooking the rice | Heat olive oil in a paella pan over medium-high heat | Fry cubed pork and chicken until browned â€” remove from pan | In the same pan, fry diced onions until softened, then add minced garlic and cook briefly | Fry diced tomatoes, then add green beans, peas, and bell peppers â€” cook for 5 minutes | Return the pork and chicken to the pan | Add the cooked rice and reserved seafood water | Stir in saffron and paprika | Test for salt and adjust | Cover with a clean cloth and cook until the rice is done and has absorbed the liquid, about 20 minutes | Just before finishing, decorate the top with sliced chorizo and red bell pepper strips | Serve hot with Spanish red wine and crusty bread

ingredients: 3 cups all-purpose flour, 1 tsp baking soda, 1 tsp ground cinnamon, 1/2 tsp salt, 3/4 cup unsalted butter (softened), 1 tsp vanilla extract, 2 cups granulated sugar, 3 large eggs, 2 cups mashed ripe bananas (about 4 bananas), 1 can (400g) crushed pineapple (undrained), 1 cup chopped pecans or walnuts, 1 cup sweetened shredded coconut. For frosting: cream cheese frosting
instructions: Preheat oven to 350Â°F (175Â°C) | Butter two 9-inch round cake pans and line the bottoms with parchment paper â€” butter the paper and dust with flour | In a bowl, whisk together flour, baking soda, cinnamon, and salt â€” set aside | In another bowl, stir together mashed bananas, crushed pineapple with juice, chopped nuts, and coconut | In a large bowl, cream butter, sugar, and vanilla until light and fluffy | Add eggs one at a time, beating well after each addition | Add the flour mixture to the butter mixture alternately with the banana-pineapple mixture, blending until just combined | Divide batter evenly between the prepared pans | Bake until golden brown, 30-40 minutes, rotating pans halfway through | Transfer pans to a wire rack to cool for 15 minutes before unmolding | Loosen sides with a knife and invert onto greased wire racks â€” to prevent layers from splitting, invert again so the tops are up | Cool completely before frosting with cream cheese frosting | Decorate with dried pineapple flowers if desired: thinly slice a fresh peeled pineapple and dry in the oven at 225Â°F (110Â°C) for 30 minutes or until dry, then arrange on the frosted cake

ingredients: For salad: 4 ripe pears (peeled and cut into wedges), 4 cups romaine lettuce (chopped), 2 cups iceberg lettuce (chopped), 1/4 cup pecans (chopped). For cream cheese layer: 8 oz cream cheese (softened), 2 tbsp mayonnaise, 1 cup gingersnap cookies (crushed, divided). For dressing: 2 tbsp honey, 2 tbsp orange juice, 1 small shallot (minced)
instructions: Crush gingersnap cookies: add all cookies to a plastic bag and crush with a rolling pin or meat mallet â€” set aside (about 2/3 for the cream cheese and 1/3 for garnish) | Make the cream cheese mixture: in a small bowl, mix softened cream cheese and mayonnaise until smooth | Add 2/3 of the crushed gingersnaps and mix well â€” set aside at room temperature | Make the dressing: whisk together honey, orange juice, and minced shallot â€” set aside | Peel pears and cut into wedges | In a medium bowl, toss chopped iceberg and romaine lettuces with a couple tablespoons of the dressing | To plate: for each serving, add a portion of dressed lettuce, then top with one pear (about 8 slices) arranged in a spiral around the center of the plate | Place a spoonful of the cream cheese mixture in the center | Drizzle a little more dressing over the pears | Top with chopped pecans and the reserved crushed gingersnaps | Serve immediately

ingredients: 1 ripe banana, 1 cup fresh pineapple chunks, 1 tbsp sugar (or honey), 1/2 cup coconut milk, 1/2 cup ice cubes, pineapple wedge for garnish
instructions: Place banana, pineapple chunks, sugar, coconut milk, and ice cubes in a blender or food processor | Process on high until blended thoroughly and smooth | Taste and add more sugar if desired | Pour into a tall glass and garnish with a pineapple wedge | Serve immediately

ingredients: 400g penne pasta, 4 Italian sausages (about 300g), 4 cloves garlic (minced), 1/4 cup dry white wine, 3 tbsp extra virgin olive oil, 1 cup tomato sauce, 1/4 cup fresh basil (torn), 1/2 cup Parmesan cheese (grated), salt to taste
instructions: In a large skillet over medium-high heat, cook the sausages until browned on all sides, about 5 minutes | Slice sausages into 1/4-inch thick rounds | Return sliced sausage to the skillet and cook for about 7 minutes until no longer pink inside | Stir in minced garlic â€” cook for 1 minute until golden | Add white wine, stirring to scrape up any brown bits from the skillet | Cook for 5 minutes until the liquid is almost absorbed | Add olive oil and tomato sauce | Bring to a boil, reduce heat, and simmer for about 5 minutes | Stir in torn basil | Meanwhile, cook penne in a large pot of salted boiling water until tender but firm (al dente) â€” drain | In a large bowl, toss the pasta with the sausage sauce | Top generously with grated Parmesan cheese and serve immediately

ingredients: For apple layer: 2 medium apples (peeled and diced), 1/4 cup raisins, 1/4 cup light brown sugar, 1 tsp ground cinnamon, 1 tbsp unsalted butter. For batter: 1 1/2 cups all-purpose flour, 1 tsp baking powder, 1/2 tsp baking soda, 1/4 tsp salt, 1/2 cup light brown sugar, 3/4 cup buttermilk, 1/4 cup unsalted butter (melted), 1 large egg, 1 tsp vanilla extract
instructions: Preheat oven to 400Â°F (200Â°C) | Butter or spray 12 muffin cups with nonstick spray or line with paper liners â€” set aside | Make the apple layer: combine diced apples, raisins, brown sugar, and cinnamon in a small bowl â€” stir until well blended | Melt butter in a skillet over medium heat and add the apple mixture | Cook, stirring over low heat, until the apples are tender, about 5 minutes â€” let cool | Spoon a layer of the apple mixture into the bottom of each muffin cup, dividing evenly | Make the batter: combine flour, baking powder, baking soda, and salt in a large bowl â€” stir until well blended | Stir in the brown sugar until combined | In a separate bowl, whisk together buttermilk, melted butter, egg, and vanilla until smooth | Add the wet ingredients to the dry ingredients all at once â€” fold just until evenly moistened (do not overmix) | Divide the batter evenly among the muffin cups over the apple layer | Bake until the tops are golden and a toothpick inserted in the centers comes out clean, about 20-22 minutes | Cool on a wire rack before removing from the pan

ingredients: 1.5 kg sirloin tip roast, salt and black pepper, 2 tbsp vegetable oil, 2 medium onions (diced), 4 cloves garlic (minced), 2 carrots (diced), 3 whole cloves, 1 tbsp orange zest, 1/4 cup brandy, 2 cups dark beer, 1 tsp whole peppercorns, 2 bay leaves, 2 sprigs fresh thyme, 15g dried porcini mushrooms, For sauce: 2 tbsp red wine vinegar, 1 tbsp cornstarch, 1 tbsp brown sugar, braised fennel and boiled new potatoes for serving
instructions: Preheat oven to 325Â°F (160Â°C) | Season the beef generously with salt and pepper | Heat oil in a large skillet and brown the roast on all sides, approximately 5 minutes per side, until well browned | Transfer the roast to a roasting pan with a lid, just large enough to hold the beef and vegetables | Return the skillet to the heat and cook the diced onions, garlic, carrots, cloves, and orange zest for about 5 minutes | Use a slotted spoon to transfer the cooked vegetables to the roaster, surrounding the meat | Place the roaster over medium heat on the stovetop | Pour in the brandy | Using a long match or lighter, carefully set the brandy alight and allow the flames to die down | Add the dark beer, peppercorns, bay leaves, thyme, and dried porcini mushrooms â€” bring to a boil | Cover the roaster with foil, then add the lid | Transfer to the oven and cook for 2 1/2 to 3 hours until the roast is tender | Transfer the beef and vegetables to a platter and keep warm â€” reserve the juices in the roaster | For the sauce: mix red wine vinegar, cornstarch, and brown sugar in a small bowl until smooth | Add 2 tablespoons of the meat juices and mix well | Pour this mixture into the roaster with the remaining juices and cook over low heat for 10 minutes, stirring constantly | Carve the roast and serve with the sauce, braised fennel, and boiled new potatoes

ingredients: 1.5 kg boneless beef rump roast or tip roast, 3 cloves garlic (slivered), 3 tbsp prepared horseradish (divided), 1 packet brown gravy mix (divided), 4 carrots (cut into chunks), 4 potatoes (quartered), 2 celery ribs (cut into chunks), 1/2 cup water, 1/2 tsp salt, 1/4 tsp fresh coarse ground black pepper, 2 tbsp cornstarch, 3 tbsp water
instructions: With the tip of a knife, make small cuts in the top of the beef roast and insert garlic slivers | Spread beef with 1 tablespoon of the horseradish | Sprinkle with 1/2 teaspoon of the gravy mix | Place beef in a 3 1/2 to 4-quart slow cooker | Arrange carrots, potatoes, and celery around the beef | In a small bowl, combine 1/2 cup water, the remaining gravy mix, salt, and pepper â€” mix until well blended | Pour over the vegetables | Cover and cook on low for 8 to 9 hours until the beef is tender | Just before serving, remove the beef and vegetables from the slow cooker â€” place on a serving platter and cover to keep warm | In a medium saucepan, combine cornstarch, 3 tablespoons water, and the remaining 2 tablespoons horseradish â€” blend well | Pour the juices from the slow cooker into the cornstarch mixture and mix well | Bring to a boil over medium-high heat, stirring constantly, until the gravy thickens | Slice the beef and serve with the vegetables and horseradish gravy

ingredients: 1 package (85g) lemon gelatin, 1 cup boiling water, 1/2 cup raisins, 1/2 cup sultanas, 1/2 cup pitted prunes (cooked until soft, drained, and chopped), 1/2 tsp ground cinnamon, 1/4 tsp ground cloves, pinch of salt, whipped cream, custard, or ice cream for serving
instructions: Dissolve lemon gelatin completely in boiling water, stirring well | Cook the prunes in a little water until softened, then drain and chop finely | Add the chopped prunes, raisins, sultanas, cinnamon, cloves, and salt to the gelatin mixture | Mix well until all ingredients are evenly distributed | Pour into a mold or serving dish | Refrigerate until fully set, at least 4 hours | Serve icy cold with whipped cream, custard, or ice cream

ingredients: 2 cups whole milk, 2 tbsp potato starch or cornstarch, 1 tbsp unsalted butter, 1 tsp seasoning salt, 1 tsp chicken bouillon powder, 1/4 tsp fresh ground black pepper
instructions: Add all ingredients â€” milk, potato starch, butter, seasoning salt, chicken bouillon, and black pepper â€” to a blender | Blend on high until smooth and well combined | Transfer mixture to a saucepan and heat over medium heat, stirring constantly, until it thickens to a creamy soup consistency | Use immediately as a base for casseroles or creamy dishes, or serve as a simple soup | The mixture will thicken further with additional heating

ingredients: 2 cups plain yogurt, 1 cup fresh spinach (finely chopped or purÃ©ed), 1/2 tsp salt, 1/2 tsp garlic paste, 1/2 tsp ginger paste, 1/4 tsp black pepper, 1/4 tsp mustard seeds, 1/4 tsp red chili powder, 1 tbsp fresh green coriander (chopped)
instructions: Whisk yogurt in a bowl until it reaches a smooth and creamy consistency | Add the chopped spinach, salt, garlic paste, ginger paste, black pepper, and mustard seeds â€” mix well until evenly combined | Transfer to a serving bowl | Garnish with a sprinkle of red chili powder and fresh chopped green coriander | Serve chilled as a cooling side dish

ingredients: 1 package (85g) unflavored gelatin, 1/4 cup cold water, 1 cup boiling water, 2 tbsp granulated sugar, 1/2 tsp salt, 1/4 cup cider vinegar, 2 tbsp fresh lemon juice, 1/2 cup celery (diced), 1/2 cup green bell pepper (diced), 1 cup green cabbage (shredded), 1/2 cup cooked peas, 2 tbsp onion (finely diced), 1/4 cup maraschino cherries (halved)
instructions: Soak the gelatin in the cold water for 5 minutes to bloom | Dissolve the bloomed gelatin completely in the boiling water, stirring well | Add sugar, salt, cider vinegar, and lemon juice â€” stir until dissolved | Let the mixture cool to room temperature | When the mixture begins to set and has a syrupy consistency, fold in the diced celery, bell pepper, shredded cabbage, peas, onion, and maraschino cherries | Pour into an oiled mold or serving dish | Refrigerate until fully set, at least 4 hours or overnight | To serve, unmold onto a serving plate or serve directly from the dish

ingredients: 2 sheets puff pastry (thawed), 6 slices bacon (diced), 100g mushrooms (sliced), 2 medium tomatoes (sliced), 1/2 medium onion (diced), 1/4 tsp ground black pepper, 4 large eggs, 2 tbsp milk (for glazing)
